Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury says Anthony Joshua fight is set to be CALLED OFF because 'money-thirsty piece of s***' Eddie Hearn wants more cash - as he calls out 'drug-dealing idiot' AJ in explosive rant
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says Anthony Joshua fight is set to be CALLED OFF because 'money-thirsty piece of s***' Eddie Hearn wants more cash - as he calls out 'drug-dealing idiot' AJ in explosive rant

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tyson Fury says his long-awaited heavyweight fight with Anthony Joshua now 'doesn't look like it's going to happen' - in a long, explosive rant at his rival and 'money-thirsty' right-hand-man promoter Eddie Hearn.

Joshua and Fury are understood to have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York City but Hearn has insisted there is still work to be done on the deal - and the situation has now blown up over the terms.

Fury accused Hearn of 'wanting more money' from Saudi boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh and funding his Saudi-linked snooker, boxing and darts ventures off the back of the prospective Fury-Joshua fight.

In a post on Instagram today, Fury, 38, said: 'Quick update: Doesn't look like they're going to sign the fight, doesn't look like it's going to happen. All because Eddie Hearn and that want more money.

'They've already had that much money off of Turki in the last few years, Eddie and AJ. They've had boxing deals, darts deals, snooker deals, they've had everything. And yet they've had the audacity and cheek of flea-bitten rats to ask for more money from Turki, who's given you everything combined in the last couple of years.

'You're disgusting, money-thirsty pieces of shit. It is what it is, same old cliche a decade later, keep running you little cowards.'

Tyson Fury has suggested his fight against Anthony Joshua is now unlikely to happen

Fury's rant included barbs at promoter Eddie Hearn and 'coward' Joshua

Hearn revealed it was written into 36-year-old Joshua's contract that the fight had to be staged in Britain - only for reports of an agreement to fight at New York's Madison Square Garden to emerge this week.

'All this talk of, "We want the fight in England, we want this, we want that'. It's only to get more money to go to America," Fury added.

'Look at the money he's had off Turki, and yet he still has to do darts deals and snooker deals off the back of my fight. That's got fuck all to do with you, Eddie. You're paid a percentage of Joshua's wages. You're not the promoter, you're not f*** all. You're just a bag carrier like you've always been. End of.'

And he turned more ire on Joshua, who this week was called 'dangerous, reckless and stupid' by boxing legend Johnny Nelson for sharing golf buggy stunts online eight months after surviving a car crash that killed two of his closest friends.

'Tell you what it is, I've never seen such cowardly-a** men in my life,' said Fury. 'You got one sausage up and down on holiday trying to jump off golf buggies. Has he not learned his lesson? He could break his arm, break his leg. Fight's off. Don't even give a f*** about the fight. You pieces of s***. Cowards.'

In a later video, an increasingly exasperated Fury added: 'You 50 pence drug-dealing f***ing idiot. A few muscles don't scare me. Lifting a few weights and doing a couple of CrossFit sessions don't bother me.'

Fury said Joshua had 'not learned his lesson' after a golf buggy video emerged this week

In 2011 Joshua avoided a jail term for possession of cannabis after being found not guilty of attempt to supply.

'I'd drink 20 pints and still beat the f*** out of you,' Fury continued. 'I won't be bothered for you or 50 men like you, that's a f***ing fact. Cause I'm the f***ing Gypsy King, and I'll tear you to pieces, you piece of s***. You and your f***ing full team. Eddie Hearn's a w****r, they're all f***ing scumbags. All scumbags!'

Fury is threatening to fight a different opponent in November if an agreement with Joshua is not reached.

According to IFLTV, Hearn has confirmed that Joshua and his team had requested an increased fight purse to cover the tax costs of the bout taking place in New York.

The promoter is not believed to have received a response to his request for the past three days.

Fury previously announced on Tuesday that the fight was on the verge of being publicised, with the Gypsy King taking to Instagram to share that 'a big fight is on the horizon'.

Fury publicly called out Joshua to make their fight after his win against Arslanbek Makhmudov

But Hearn stressed that there were still elements of the deal to be agreed due to the changed location of the fight, with Wembley preferred by Joshua's camp for the all-British affair.

Speaking in an interview released after Daily Mail Sport's story broke, Hearn added: 'It seems like everyone is adamant the fight takes place in New York. There isn't really any consideration or willingness to speak to the government. Sadiq Khan, Transport for London. It's just like "we want to do this fight in America".

'Tyson Fury has agreed to do it in America and we haven't at the moment. We are talking through a roadmap of what that might look like to change the deal and if they do all the things we've discussed and agreed in principle, then I think there is a very good chance the fight will happen in America.'

Madison Square Garden was the site of one of Joshua's greatest defeats - his shock loss to Andy Ruiz Jr in June 2019.

Talks between Fury and Joshua over their long-awaited showdown have been part of boxing's conversation since 2017, with the biggest opportunity coming in 2021 when the two men appeared to be moving towards a two-fight agreement.

A deal was publicly discussed, but the proposed fight ultimately collapsed after Fury became obligated to face Deontay Wilder following an arbitration ruling.

Fury subsequently fought Wilder for a third time, while Joshua suffered back-to-back defeats against Oleksandr Usyk, losing his WBA, IBF and WBO titles in 2021 before being beaten again in their 2022 rematch.

Sports.title: Two-time world champion boxer, 38, shot dead in deadly ambush outside his home with killers still at large
Sports.content:
Two-time world champion boxer, 38, shot dead in deadly ambush outside his home with killers still at large

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Zolani Tete, a two-time world champion boxer, has been shot dead outside his home in South Africa.

The 38-year-old was killed in an apparent ambush in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape, at around 6:30pm on Friday night, officials confirmed.

Police said he had been arriving at his residence when he was approached by two unknown armed suspects wearing balaclavas while he was waiting for the gate to open.

The suspects, who are still at large, emerged from a vehicle and opened fire on Tete and a 27-year-old female passenger, who remains in hospital.

'He unfortunately succumbed to his injuries and was declared deceased on the scene,' police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana said.

'The female passenger sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was immediately rushed to a nearby hospital for medical treatment. She remains hospitalized.'

Boxer Zolani Tete was shot dead outside his home in Eastern Cape, South Africa

Tete was a two-time world champion, most notably holding the WBO bantamweight belt

Gantana revealed: 'In an attempt to escape the hail of bullets, the deceased drove his vehicle into the yard.

Tete most notably held the WBO bantamweight title from 2017 to 2019. He also holds a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a title fight after he knocked out Siboniso Gonya inside just 11 seconds in 2017.

Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture Gayton McKenzie said: 'South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced. Zolani "Last Born" Tete was shot and killed this evening in Mdantsane, at his own home, at the age of 38. A 27-year-old woman who was in the car with him was shot multiple times and is in hospital tonight. I wish her a full recovery, and I ask that her privacy and the family's be respected.

'I want to speak first to his family and to the people of Mdantsane. There are no words I can offer tonight that will be equal to what you have lost. Your son's name will not be treated lightly by this country, and my Department and I are at your disposal in the days ahead, in whatever way is useful to you.

'He was sitting at his own gate, waiting for it to open, and that is where they came for him. I will not speculate about who did this or why. That investigation belongs to the South African Police Service, and the detectives working it tonight need support.

'Two armed men in balaclavas got out of a car in Mdantsane and killed one of our greatest world champion at his own front gate, and they are still out there tonight. I appeal to anyone who saw anything, who knows anything, who heard anything, to come forward. Somebody in that community knows who did this.'

Tete last fought in London in July 2022, beating Jason Cunningham by knockout for his 30th professional win in 35 fights. But it was later ruled a no-contest after he failed a drugs test.

A year later, he was issued a four-year ban by the UK Anti-Doping Agency after testing positive for stanozolol. His ban ended on July 29 this year and after his death, manager Mla Tengimfene, confirmed he was training for a comeback fight on November 29.

Tete had not fought since 2022 but was training for a comeback after a drugs ban

Boxing South Africa said Tete 'inspired a generation of fighters' with his career

'It's been a tough and long journey and I am happy it's finally coming to an end,' Tete told The Ring earlier this year, still protesting his innocence over the adverse drug test finding, insisting: 'I don't accept the ban because I'm a clean and fair athlete.'

When asked if he was going to return to boxing, he said: 'Oh yes definitely, my plan is still unfinished,' he said. 'It's been a while since I stepped inside the ring, I am looking forward to my comeback fight and getting back to winning ways.'

News of his passing was met with an outpouring of tributes from across the boxing world, including a statement from the sport's governing body in South Africa.

It read: 'Boxing South Africa (BSA) has learnt with profound shock and sadness of the untimely passing of former IBF Junior Bantamweight and WBO Bantamweight World Champion, Zolani 'Last Born' Tete.

'The tragic incident reportedly occurred on the evening of Friday, 21 August 2026, in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape. Our thoughts and prayers are with the Tete family, his manager Mlandeli Tengimfene, the All-Winners Boxing Club, and Last-Born Boxing Promotions during this incredibly difficult time.

'Zolani Tete was more than a champion. He was an icon of South African boxing. A product of the famed All Winners Mdantsane boxing stable.

'He etched his name in history as one of the country's few two-weight world champions. His achievements in the ring from winning the IBF junior-bantamweight title in Japan in 2014 to claiming the WBO bantamweight crown, inspired a generation of fighters.

'His legacy includes holding the record for the fastest world title defence in boxing history, needing just 11 seconds to stop Siboniso Gonya in 2017 .

'We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, and the entire boxing fraternity. The sport has lost a true warrior and ambassador.

'Further details regarding official tributes and memorial arrangements will be shared upon engagement with the Tete family. We kindly request that the family's privacy be respected during this period of mourning.'

Sports.title: Ex-British boxing champion Darren Barker shares heartfelt Ricky Hatton message as he sets off on epic 1,800-mile fundraising challenge
Sports.content:
Ex-British boxing champion Darren Barker shares heartfelt Ricky Hatton message as he sets off on epic 1,800-mile fundraising challenge

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Darren Barker has issued an emotional message about Ricky Hatton as he continues his inspiring 'The Longest Round' fundraising challenge, in memory of the boxing great.

Barker, former IBF world middleweight champion, set off from Edinburgh on Wednesday morning on a mega 1,800-mile endurance challenge to Morocco across land and sea.

The challenge sees him cycle from Edinburgh to Dover, swim the English channel (21 miles), cycle from Calais to Gibraltar before he ends off the adventure with an open-water swim across the Strait of Gibraltar into Morocco (nine miles).

The challenge will push Barker to the absolute limits, testing him both physically and mentally but he's determined to complete it for Ricky and 'for all the people out there suffering'.

Barker is raising funds for suicide prevention charity Campaign Against Living Miserably (CALM), in which Hatton had been an ambassador of.

Darren Barker is currently on a 1,800-mile endurance challenge in honour of Ricky Hatton

And speaking ahead of the challenge, the 44-year-old said: 'Last September, I had the honour and the privilege to speak to Ricky Hatton on a podcast. And days later he wasn't with us, so it really struck home and hit hard. And made me really understand what a terrible illness mental health is. I want to do something for Ricky, I want to do something to spread awareness.

'I feel like I owe this to Ricky. He gave up his time to speak to me, so this is something I need to do for him, and I want to do - and I need to do for the bigger picture. I need to do this for all the people out there suffering, to know that it's OK to not be OK. I want to encourage these people to have these uncomfortable conversations, and hopefully save lives in the future.'

He added: 'He will always be a hero of mine. He was the man that brought the big nights to British boxing. The man that brought the big crowds.

'But away from boxing, he was so likeable - he was the man next door - everyone could relate to Ricky. So funny, charming, just a real good guy with a big heart and someone that people could look up to. He is massively missed.'

Barker spoke from the heart as he explained what 'The Longest Round' and CALM mean to him.

Barker spoke to Hatton on a podcast a few days before his friend was found dead at his home

He continued: 'It means an awful lot. It means that I, along with the team, and everybody else following this - that we have an opportunity to make a real difference here. This is about changing lives, helping people. This is bigger than swimming and cycling, this is a huge opportunity to try and make a difference, and that's what I want to do.

'You, I guess, go through your early stages of life, being selfish, and you're on your own journey, trying to fulfil dreams and aspirations to do this and that, and then you kind of - in my situation anyway - achieve that - and it's about what next. And for me, it feels right to help and just try and raise money and awareness for something now that has really resonated with me.

'Even myself as a retired fighter, grieving the loss of boxing, grieving the loss of my brother, my grandad - understanding that grief is a part of mental health. So along with everyone else, this isn't just me - I may be getting on the bike and in the sea - but this is all of us pulling together and being there for one another. Let's be nice to one another, let's be there, let's support. So much hardship in the world as it is, so if we all pull together - we're halfway there you know.'

Any donations can be made to: https://www.justgiving.com/page/thelongestround

Sports.title: 'Dangerous, reckless and stupid' Anthony Joshua is called out over golf buggy stunts by boxing icon Johnny Nelson, eight months after surviving Nigeria car crash that killed his friends
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has been called 'dangerous, reckless and stupid' by boxing legend Johnny Nelson for sharing golf buggy stunts online eight months after surviving a car crash that killed two of his closest friends.

The former world heavyweight champion has been on holiday in the Dominican Republic before he begins preparations for his long-awaited blockbuster showdown against his compatriot Tyson Fury.

But the Briton caught heat for sharing a video of himself racing golf buggies with friends, and at one point, appearing to attempt to climb between the two moving vehicles.

'Loser do 100 press-ups,' Joshua captioned the video.

Joshua was devastated by the loss of his best friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele last December, after the trio were involved in a car crash near Lagos.

After watching the social media video however, Nelson told Boxing King Media that it 'begs belief' that Joshua believed he should post the clip online for his followers.

🗣️JOHNNY NELSON NOT IMPRESSED WITH AJ POST…



In our latest episode of the uncomfortable truth, @SkyJohnnyNelson steps in to give his opinion on a video Anthony Joshua posted last night.



Watch full episode here ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/M5RinyUTUG — Boxing King Media (@boxingkingmedia) August 19, 2026

Anthony Joshua has been criticised by boxing legend Johnny Nelson after sharing a video of himself 'recklessly' driving golf buggies

The boxing star was involved in a fatal car accident in Nigeria last December which took the life of two of his closest friends

'I saw it, and I put my head in my hands,' the former world champion said. 'I thought, 'what are you thinking? What are you doing, man?'

'I know you're young, I know you want to live life, but to understand what's just happened to you... As a parent, I'd think - you know, I cussed out my daughter, she was in Bali, on the back of a motorbike without permission. I cussed out my daughter. And it reminded me of what happened with AJ over the Christmas period.

'And then I see AJ doing this. I'm like, 'you're not thinking. What is wrong with you?' And regardless of how much you try and play it off - thinking, 's***, I probably shouldn't have posted that' - you shouldn't have been doing that thing.

'It looked dangerous, it looked reckless. And people have looked and thought: 'You know what, this guy must have been through it.' Now people are thinking, 'you're an idiot'. And he's got to think, 'maybe I've got to fall on my sword here. It's a stupid thing I did.

'Post it or not, it was just a stupid thing to do. It had danger written all over it, you can see the worst-case scenario. When I saw it, I thought like a parent; I thought: "I hope your old man has a word with you, I hope your mum cusses you out. I just hope they have a strong word with you, because that was reckless, irresponsible and dangerous."

'After everything that's happened, to do something like that, it begs belief.'

Nelson added that he believed that Joshua would be unable to be 'p***ed off' with people who criticised the post.

'You've got people's pity, you've got people's understanding,' Nelson stressed. 'And then you do something like that.'

Joshua has been deeply affected by the death of his friends and surviving the fatal crash himself, with the accident coming just ten days after he took down YouTuber-turned-boxing star Jake Paul.

Upon his return to the ring in late July with his fight against Kristian Prenga, Joshua broke down during his post-fight interview as he credited Ayodele and Ghami for getting him through a tough first round.

'I don't want to talk about it anymore,' Joshua had said quietly as he let out his emotions.

Earlier in the evening he had stepped into the ring wearing his friends' names on pennants pinned to his chest and had admitted before the fight that he had spent months suppressing the pain of their loss.

Joshua has spoken out about the grief he has experienced after the deaths of Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele

Joshua was being driven along one of Nigeria's deadliest roads in December when his SUV crashed into a stationary truck on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

The 36-year-old is thought to have narrowly escaped major injury or worse after having switched to sit behind the driver in the back seat on the left-hand side of the car.

Joshua was admitted to hospital with 'minor injuries' after being pulled from the wreckage of the crash.

In February, Joshua added the names of 'LATZ' and 'SINA' to the tattoo outline of Africa he sports on his bicep.

A month earlier, he had stressed his commitment to the families of his friends in a touching Instagram video which also took in his bond with both men.

'My goal is to help their families and to help them achieve their goals, even though they may not be here in the physical,' Joshua told his fans. 'I will be saying my prayers, and I'm going to help them fulfill their dreams for their families. It's not only me though helping. There's a whole team working on that stuff.

'There is a whole system that will be helping fulfill their legacy, fulfill their dreams. But I know in my corner of the world, I know what I'm doing, and I know what we're gonna do to continue there.

'I'm gonna do what's right by their family. It's about what's important to me, and they're very important players, very important team, with very important friends and two of my brothers.

'So yeah, I don't think I've mentioned the love and appreciation. It's all acknowledged by me, by them, by their families. 100 per cent we acknowledge the 1000s, maybe going into millions around the world that show so much love to them both. I still can't get my head around it.

'We heard you all, we saw the messages, the tweets, the social media, the YouTubes, the prayers, it's all been acknowledged. So yeah, we know what we're going to do. Mumma Latz, Mumma Sina, Pappa Latz, Pappa Sina, one love.'

Joshua's video clip of his golf buggy exploits comes hours after it was announced that Joshua and Fury were understood to have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York.

He paid tribute to his friends before his fight against Kristian Prenga by wearing their names on a bar on his chest

The 36-year-old also added their names to his tattoo of the African continent on his bicep

Fury took to social media on Tuesday morning to tease the announcement, telling his followers that the fight was on the verge of being publicised.

He said: 'Big news being dropped very, very soon. A big fight on the horizon. It's the one you've all been waiting for. It's about to be announced imminently so stay tuned!'

While those close to the negotiations have told Daily Mail Sport that the blockbuster bout is done, with New York’s Madison Square Garden understood to have been agreed as the venue, Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn has insisted there is still work to be done on the deal.

Those familiar with the discussions say Joshua and his promoter Hearn continued to push for the fight to take place in the UK, with Fury also keen on a homecoming bout, but they were ultimately unable to secure their preferred location.

However, Hearn – who recently revealed it was written into Joshua's contract that the fight has to be staged in Britain – has told Daily Mail Sport that no agreement has yet been reached to change those terms.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua to SNUB Wembley and take place on a FRIDAY in New York to avoid clash with NFL: Date set with contracts signed as Britain's biggest fight goes abroad... and fans back home could face a VERY late night
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are understood to have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York City, raising concerns that the mega-fight will take place in the middle of the night for British fans.

Fury took to social media on Tuesday morning to tease the announcement, telling his followers that the fight was on the verge of being publicised. He said: 'Big news being dropped very, very soon. A big fight on the horizon. It's the one you've all been waiting for. It's about to be announced imminently so stay tuned!'

While those close to the negotiations have told Daily Mail Sport that the blockbuster bout is done, with New York’s Madison Square Garden understood to have been agreed as the venue, Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn has insisted there is still work to be done on the deal.

Those familiar with the discussions say Joshua and his promoter Hearn continued to push for the fight to take place in the UK, with Fury also keen on a homecoming bout, but they were ultimately unable to secure their preferred location.

However, Hearn - who recently revealed it was written into Joshua's contract that the fight has to be staged in Britain - has told Daily Mail Sport that no agreement has yet been reached to change those terms.

'We are in constant communication with Turki (Alalshikh, Saudi boxing supremo) and (Saudi Arabian sports company) SELA but as of yet there is no agreement to any variation within the contract,' he said.

It is understood that Anthony Joshua (left) and Tyson Fury (right) have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York City

The fight is said to be taking in New York and the iconic Madison Square Garden - where Joshua previously suffered his shock defeat by Andy Ruiz Jr in June 2019

Turki Alalshikh (above), who is helping bankroll the fight, had left the door open to staging the event in Britain, but made it clear that the numbers had to work

Speaking in an interview released after Daily Mail Sport's story broke, Hearn added: "It seems like everyone is adamant the fight takes place in New York. There isn't really any consideration or willingness to speak to the government. Sadiq Khan, Transport for London. It's just like 'we want to do this fight in America'.

'Tyson Fury has agreed to do it in America and we haven't at the moment. We are talking through a roadmap of what that might look like to change the deal and if they do all the things we've discussed and agreed in principle, then I think there is a very good chance the fight will happen in America."

Others close to the discussions say Alalshikh's position was that the fight could be staged in the UK if the financial case stacked up and the figures could be demonstrated.

But with that case ultimately unable to be made, the decision has been taken to move the blockbuster to New York and the iconic Madison Square Garden - the scene of Joshua's shock defeat by Andy Ruiz Jr in June 2019.

The fight is expected to take place on a Friday night in an attempt to avoid clashes with major American sporting events and maximise its exposure in the US.

It remains unclear, however, whether the main event will take place at a time convenient for British boxing fans.

And while Hearn's comments indicate that the contractual position has yet to be formally altered, Daily Mail Sport understands the final pieces are now being put in place for the official announcement, with the relevant parties due to meet in the coming days to organise the launch press conference.

That is expected to take place before the end of August.

Anthony Joshua has his hand raised following victory over Kristian Prenga on July 25

However, result didn't come without drama as he was knocked down in the first 20 seconds

Spencer Brown, Fury's manager, said several weeks ago that the announcement would be made at an iconic British landmark, adding that it would be 'like no announcement' fans have ever seen before and claiming they 'don't want to miss it'.

Hearn has also previously told Daily Mail Sport that the announcement press conference would take place before the end of the month and would be timed around Joshua's return from holiday.

The roots of Joshua-Fury go back to the beginning of the 2010s, when both men were establishing themselves as Britain's leading heavyweight prospects.

Joshua won Olympic gold at London 2012 before turning professional, while Fury had already made his professional debut in 2008 and was building an unbeaten record of his own.

For years, the prospect of the two eventually meeting was one of British boxing's biggest talking points.

Fury's victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 transformed him into a world heavyweight champion, while Joshua was rapidly moving towards the same position.

Joshua won the IBF heavyweight title by beating Charles Martin in 2016 and subsequently added the WBA and IBO belts.

By 2017, the possibility of an undisputed Joshua-Fury fight had become a genuine objective rather than simply a dream matchup.

Fury took on Mariusz Wach at the Max Muay Thai Stadium, Pattaya, Thailand on July 24

But the negotiations repeatedly failed.

The biggest opportunity came in 2021, when Joshua and Fury appeared to be moving towards a two-fight agreement. A deal was publicly discussed, but the proposed fight ultimately collapsed after Fury became obligated to face Deontay Wilder following an arbitration ruling.

Fury subsequently fought Wilder for a third time, while Joshua moved towards his own defining bouts.

Joshua then suffered back-to-back defeats against Oleksandr Usyk, losing his WBA, IBF and WBO titles in 2021 before being beaten again in their 2022 rematch.

The sport then appeared to get another opportunity to make Joshua-Fury. In late 2022, negotiations accelerated dramatically, with both camps discussing a proposed fight in December.

A deal again failed to materialise.

Fury instead moved on to other opponents, while Joshua continued his rebuilding process following the Usyk defeats.

The arrival of Alalshikh and the expansion of major boxing events in Saudi Arabia created a new route to making the fight.

Fury emerged victorious and had been expected ringside for AJ's fight with Prenga

Now, after years of failed negotiations and multiple points at which the fight appeared close before falling apart, the contracts have finally been signed.

Joshua-Fury is no longer a fight being negotiated.

It is happening.

November 20. Madison Square Garden. Or, so they say...

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua should not be fighting in New York - their fans have been forgotten and will now have to shell out their last pennies to see their heroes: JEFF POWELL
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua should not be fighting in New York - their fans have been forgotten and will now have to shell out their last pennies to see their heroes: JEFF POWELL

For our next trick, how about the FA Cup final at Giants Stadium? Soulless. Never mind.

Then the Wimbledon finals on the good old hard courts of Flushing Meadows?

The Open? What holes in golf could be more challenging than the First to Eighteenth Streets in Manhattan? No soft landings there.

What about The Ashes? Where better for the Poms and the Okkers to dispute the Ashes than Yankee Stadium?

I could go on.

The selection of New York's Madison Square Garden for the longest awaited boxing match in UK ring history was not exactly a surprise. Wembley Stadium had given up on the Gypsy King v AJ weeks ago.

Where better for the last hurrah for two grand old British warhorses than Madison Square Garden? Even if that nostalgic mausoleum is not exactly the most sentimental last resting place for two lions of our own.

We sell our history at our peril.

But for Nett-Profit-Flix? And to the oil-mongers?

I am all for the men in gloves who put their lives on the line between the ropes making the most money they can for themselves and the generational future of their families.

But neither Tyson Fury nor Anthony Joshua are short of a few bucks and the fans who made them are forgotten in this sell-out. Even if they manage to prop open their eyelids with matchsticks into the early hours of a dank winter morning.

Many of the faithful will do so. Especially those who have been imploring Joshua and Fury to get it on for a couple of decades.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua look set to finally battle it out on November 20

Madison Square Garden in New York City is expected to host the heavyweight bout

The sad part, even though we will all be drawn to it like curious cats, is that they have missed their moment in time

No world title on the line. Historically beyond its time.

Delayed by all those involved in case one heavyweight or the other got knocked off his perch of public admiration and corporate income before they fought each other.

That obsession was exposed as nonsense by Oleksandr Usyk and Daniel Dubois.

So overpowering is the scent of nostalgia in this most compelling of sports that we still want to see what happens when two of our national heroes collide.

Hundreds if not thousands of Brits will spend their last pennies on going to New York to bear witness to this last rite for two of their heroes.

They are worth more, much more than Big Daddy Netflix and Uncle Saudi.

Meanwhile, the British Croquet Association beware.

Sports.title: Boxing champion Prichard Colon dies aged 33, 11 years after taking 'illegal' punches in fight which left him in a 221-day coma and a vegetative state
Sports.content:
Boxing champion Prichard Colon dies aged 33, 11 years after taking 'illegal' punches in fight which left him in a 221-day coma and a vegetative state

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33 more than a decade after suffering catastrophic brain injuries.

Back in October 2015 Colon, competing as a super-middleweight at the time, suffered a bleed on the brain after taking repeated blows to the back of the head during a contest with America's Terrel Williams in Virginia.

After vomiting and collapsing in the dressing room after his defeat, the Puerto Rican was rushed to hospital before spending 221 days in a coma. The fight with Williams had seen part of his skull collapse as a result of the repeated rabbit punches, which are deemed illegal in the sport.

After emerging from the coma, Colon, once a promising rising star in the ring, was left in a vegetative state with life-altering injuries. He was under the near-constant care of his family.

Colon conquered multiple national amateur championships and won a Youth Pan American gold medal before turning professional.

Colon's dad and former trainer, Richard, announced the heartbreaking news on social media, writing: 'Good morning, everyone. I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world. He is now in a better place.'

He added: 'Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers.'

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, his family have announced

The Puerto Rican suffered catastrophic brain injuries during a 2015 fight (pictured)

Until that fateful fight almost 11 years ago, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects.

He had established an unblemished 16-0 record with 13 knockouts with many in boxing viewing him as a future star.

Following the bout against Williams, Colon was rushed to the hospital where doctors discovered a subdural hematoma.

He underwent emergency surgery as medics desperately attempted to relieve the swelling in his brain. After spending 221 days in a coma, Colon awoke unable to walk or talk.

Despite the traumatic injuries, just three years ago, Colon had vowed not to throw in the towel.

In an update on his Facebook profile at the time, Colon attempted to speak with his mother and even raised a smile in a moving video.

The post was captioned: 'I will not give up'.

In other clips, the ex-fighter could be seen attending a truck rally with his family, while also appearing to take a positive step in being able to brush his own teeth.

He was left in a vegetative state and was under the near-constant care of his family

Until that fateful fight, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects

His mother also shared a video of her son on his 31st birthday where she gave him a cupcake with a candle on it.

Colon's story is one of the most tragic in boxing history, with former heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder breaking down in tears while discussing it last year.

'We’ve seen what happens, look at Colon. How he got hit, Prichard Colon, correct,' Wilder said.

'This man didn’t have no kids… they don’t understand. Y’all don’t f****** understand what we go through, man.

'And I don’t even know him like that, but I will always be an advocate for us. Because this man will never know what it’s like to be somebody’s father. And that’s one of the most precious things in the world, to be somebody’s father. But he will never be nobody’s father, man.

'Because he got in the ring to support his family but now, his family got to take care of him for the rest of his life.'

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL: Frank Warren talks up new golden age of British heavyweight boxing as prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for Filip Hrgovic showdown
Sports.content:
JEFF POWELL: Frank Warren talks up new golden age of British heavyweight boxing as prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for Filip Hrgovic showdown

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Frank Warren has signalled a new ‘golden age' for British heavyweight boxing as his prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for his unexpected world title fight with Filip Hrgovic at London’s O2 on August 29.

The 21-year-old Itauma was already set to face the 31-year-old Croatian in a championship eliminator when the fight was promoted into a battle for the IBF title after undisputed heavyweight king Oleksandr Usyk vacated all four alpha-belts.

Hrgovic’s only defeat in 21 fights came when he was knocked out in the eighth round two years ago by Daniel Dubois, who went on to become the WBO champion by stopping Fabio Wardley in a bloodied slugfest this May. Those two Englishmen will meet again in a rematch in October.

Hall of Fame Promoter Warren also has in his stable Tyson Fury who is heading for his long, long awaited Battle of Britain with Anthony Joshua in November at either Wembley Stadium or New York’s fabled Madison Square Garden.

‘These are amazingly exciting times for heavyweight boxing in this country,’ says Warren. ‘We have a whole programme of mouth-watering fights pencilled in our calendar at Queensberry.

'Although Moses is in his toughest fight yet I expect him to become the second youngest ever world heavyweight champion behind Mike Tyson.

Moses Itauma is preparing for his unexpected world title fight with Filip Hrgovic

‘He would then have to deal with a mandatory defence against (American) Frank Mitchell, who I don’t think is as talented as Hrgovic.

'Win that and we should be looking at an IBF - WBO title unification fight between him and the winner of Dubois v Wardley. All of those are huge punchers and that fight would sell-out Wembley in a heart-beat.’

All the above are on Queensberry's books except Mitchell and Joshua and Warren says: ‘I expect Tyson to beat AJ on seniors night and quite possibly carry on to fight whichever of the young bloods comes out on top as the new undisputed heavyweight champion.

‘Imagine Itauma the hottest most talked about heavy on the planet against Fury the box office Gypsy King.

'Is there a stadium big enough for that.By the last Saturday night this month the UK will know for sure what Itauma is all about. And as it happens even at his age he has the maturity and the level head to carry it all off. Even though every fight in his sights now will be as dangerous as they come.

‘Buckle up.'

Sports.title: Why F1 fans need fewer sprints, not more
Sports.content:
A plague of technical problems beset the train network out of Amsterdam on the Saturday morning of the Dutch Grand Prix weekend, raising the possibility that thousands of fans might miss the sprint race.

Lucky them.

Sitting, or indeed standing, on a crowded vessel of public transport reading one of those wretched pieces of AI-generated slash-fiction slop which bedevil the Kindle Unlimited service would probably have been preferable to occupying a hard plastic bench in the bleachers as the 24 processional laps unfolded. It was an object lesson in the folly of holding these sprint events at venues where overtaking is unlikely, save for the invisible machinations of tyre performance. Hold my Hertog Jan! Norris's rear tyres are degrading! – said no one, ever.

Social media, a toxic waste of time these past couple of years, assumed some semblance of its former sporadically amusing self as users posted wit such as "This race could have been an e-mail…"Certainly one felt that anyone with a burning desire to see the drivers parading around in a line could do so on Sunday lunchtime when they wave at the crowd from the back of a flatbed truck. Failing that, they could put them in Lego cars again.

The long-standing argument in favour of sprint weekends is that having less practice time tends to lead to less predictable outcomes, since the teams have less time to finesse their set-ups. This, more or less, is true. Another point in favour is that practice sessions such as usually populate a weekend are inherently tedious for the audience, since there is no real narrative – just cars circulating a track to an unseen plan. Also difficult to dispute – but is there really such a difference between that and a high-speed procession masquerading as a motor race?

Also inarguable is the commercial reality that race promoters love sprint weekends because they sell more tickets - which is why F1 plans to double the number to 12 next season. Again, fine – but the racing needs to be better, or the sprint weekends should be distributed around those circuits where overtaking is possible, rather than operating via some abstruse grace and favour system where promoters get a sprint as an incentive or a pat on the head.

Leclerc achieved a rarity in the Zandvoort sprint - overtaking another car Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

One can understand Zandvoort being handed a little something to maximise weekend ticket sales for its final event, given the energy Jan Lammers and his team have invested in bringing the Dutch GP back to life as a private enterprise without state backing. But Singapore, of all places, will host the next sprint race, for reasons known only to the commercial rights holder.

It's time to accept that the sprint format isn't suitable for all venues. Granted, Zandvoort is now heading into the vault of history, but there are plenty of other tracks still on the calendar with only one practicable overtaking zone requiring the chasing car to be half a second quicker than the chased. Combine that with most of the field running the same tyre and a procession is inevitable.

Sadly, F1 itself seems to take the contrasting view – that the sprint format is the finished product with no further need for iterative development. When first evaluated, over three events in 2021, the format was a qualifying session on Friday which set the grid for Saturday's sprint race, the results of which in term determined the grid for the grand prix.

F1 was smart enough to iterate away from the initial flaws, would it not also be wise to continue that process and interrogate the format further

What quickly became obvious was that all this did was reset the grid in pace order, hence the evolution into the present format with separate qualifying sessions and parc ferme periods so the sprint in effect lives separately from the grand prix. At least it no longer functions as a spoiler for the main event.

Given that F1 was smart enough to iterate away from the initial flaws, would it not also be wise to continue that process and interrogate the format further, given the obvious shortcomings outlined above? The sprint races remain widely derided by drivers and fans, given their fundamentally uneventful nature.

Obviously the word "fans" does a lot of heavy lifting these days, since the size of F1's fanbase means it incorporates a broad demographic spectrum. This enables F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali to wave his hands and say airily, with no meaningful data to back up his contention, that most fans don't care about such things. Only last weekend, for instance, Domenicali once again sailed into Accidental Partridge territory in an interview with De Telegraaf where he opined, apropos the 2026 tech regulations, "There are die-hard fans who talk about clipping during a Formula 1 weekend, but there will also be many who think a clip is something you put in your hair."

No further comment, your honour…

To sprint or not to sprint, that is the question Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Sports.title: Antonelli set for Italian GP grid penalty
Sports.content:
Mercedes has officially decided its Formula 1 world championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start from the back of the grid at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix after it decided to give him a new power unit, exceeding his allowance for the year.

Drivers are allowed to use up to four power units for the season, but Mercedes' reliability woes over the first half of the campaign meant it has always been a question of when, not if, its drivers were going to exceed that allowance and take a grid penalty.

Antonelli is currently already at the limit with his V6 and exhaust system, while Russell has no more room for either a combustion engine or turbocharger.

Antonelli had been in line for a grid drop at his home race in Monza in two weeks' time, and Mercedes has now officially confirmed it will change the title favourite's engine. The 19-year-old is set for a full power unit switch, which sets him up for a back-of-the-grid start.

"With Kimi we are taking the full thing," Wolff confirmed, dismissing the notion that Mercedes could have been tempted to take into account Monza being Antonelli's home race.

Photo by: Pauline Ballet - Formula 1

"In theory, our calculations say that that's the best track to take it. Obviously, our algorithms don't take nationality into consideration. But we are here to fight for a championship and not get the most PR. So, that's what we are going to do."

Russell is also set for grid drop down the line, though the Brackley team hasn't decided yet where the Briton will swap power units yet.

Russell only took his fourth power unit at the recent Hungarian Grand Prix, the final race before the summer break. That gives him more flexibility on mileage, though the team could still opt to add a fifth power unit to his pool of components at any time.

"With George, the discussions are ongoing about where to take it," Wolff said.

The next suitable opportunity after Monza could be Baku's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which emphasises power unit performance and top speed while providing some overtaking opportunities to offset a grid drop.

Sports.title: What makes Norris say “I don't have a car to fight for the championship”?
Sports.content:
The 2026 Formula 1 championship finds itself at a curious intersection where nobody is willing to entertain the idea that they have the best car.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after finishing second to Lando Norris in the Dutch Grand Prix that Mercedes no longer has the best car – indeed, that it may only be the third best.

But Norris, now fourth in the standings with 159 points to Antonelli’s 242, was determined to play down talk of him staging a comeback in the final half of the season, despite winning two consecutive grands prix. "I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship," he said after his Dutch GP victory.

Many readers would be tempted to cite the so-called Mandy Rice-Davies principle – "Well they would say that, wouldn’t they?"

What’s clear, though, is that under the latest technical regulations there is still a difference in relative strengths between cars which complicates the competitive picture. In broad-brush terms the McLaren MCL40 thrives in fast corners, Ferrari’s SF-26 is strong in terms of carrying good speed into slow corners, while the Mercedes W17 is somewhere between the two. That makes the competitive balance heavily dependent on circuit layout.

Norris’s contention is that his car is insufficiently rounded to be dominant across the remaining rounds in the way last year’s McLaren was the car to beat at most tracks.

Norris played down the significance of his Dutch GP victory Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We have a strong car in certain areas," he said. "It's not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere. We're very, very strong in high speed. The place we've improved the car the most is high-speed performance.

"No one matches us in high speed. And that's a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in Turn 7, Turn 8 was crazy.

"But their advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore I don't have the confidence to say, yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. I know I've just won two races in a row and two poles in a row, but at the minute I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship.

"And I know that's quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed from me. And I know the level that I am now and what I can perform at. And I know just what I need from the car – and what tracks we have coming up where we're going to certainly struggle more."

The issue is more complex than simply saying a particular car is fast around a certain type of corner. This year’s cars are shorter, narrower and slightly lighter – and the chassis characteristics are more interconnected with power unit performance than ever before, given the influence of corner-entry speeds on energy harvesting.

McLaren's decision to run a short wheelbase, helping it save weight at the start of the season, has baked in certain shortcomings in terms of how much aerodynamic load the team can squeeze from the floor.

Performance is often hugely variable between tyre compounds. In Saturday’s sprint race, running mediums, Norris struggled with rear degradation and was overtaken by Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in the closing stages. In the grand prix he took the restart on used softs, was passed by Antonelli at the start, and didn’t really get into the race until the hard-compound tyres went on.

Norris was able to pressure championship leader Antonelli later in the Zandvoort race Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

"We put on the hard tyres," he said. "We were a bit more aggressive with how we wanted to approach the stint. And we turned things around. I had that feeling in the car that I wanted. I went from just not feeling like I was going to win a race to at least we can force him [Antonelli] to make mistakes.

"When I get what I need from a car, when I have the front I want, when I get the confidence with the rear on entries – just when I get what I need to be able to know and predict every single corner, I'm going to win a race."

Norris has a driving style slightly more aligned to Max Verstappen than the likes of George Russell or even his own team-mate, Oscar Piastri. Rather than separating the throttle off/brake on and turning phases, he likes to blend the throttle and brakes and take a shallower approach angle. Essentially he is feeling for the point in the overlap where the front tyres begin to exert more lateral grip, which helps rotate the car and carry more speed into the corner, towards the apex.

This requires the car not only to have a 'strong' front end, but also to communicate what the front tyres are doing, which represents a tough engineering challenge. Modern F1 cars require a consistent ride height for the aerodynamics to function optimally, so the suspension geometry is designed to minimise dive and squat. A side of this is that it saps driver 'feel'.

Some can live with that, some can’t, which is why McLaren designed an alternate front suspension geometry with a revised kingpin angle for Norris when he was floundering at the beginning of last season. Once he has that feel he can be very adaptable in terms of his lines and the degree of overlap between throttle and brake, which is why he thrives in low-grip conditions.

But although he has a huge amount of adaptability within this range, he still needs that strong front end, good transmission of feel, and confidence that the rear axle will rotate predictably on cue.

"It's clear where our weaknesses are," Norris concluded. "Therefore we need to attack those things. And until we do that, it's still going to be a very tough end of the season."

Sports.title: FIA explains safety car formation lap after F1 driver criticism at Dutch GP
Sports.content:
The opening stages of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort descended into chaos after rain had started to fall during the grid procedure.

Max Verstappen crashed heavily on the exit of the final corner on the opening lap of the race. The Red Bull driver admitted that it was entirely his own mistake. The Dutchman thought he could get back on the throttle, but that part of the track was clearly still too wet.

Behind Verstappen, Gabriel Bortoleto also came close to crashing, although he miraculously managed to keep his Audi out of the wall, while it was even more remarkable that team-mate Nico Hulkenberg managed to avoid him.

The German immediately said over the radio that he feared he was going to T-bone Bortoleto.

"It was just that corner, if I'm very honest with you. It was full wets, that place. I think that's why Max lost it and it was the same for me," Bortoleto said in the media pen post-race.

"I was on the downside of the banking. I did a little reaction move to the left, I think, when I saw big smoke coming up ahead. And when I did that, I just went as well."

According to Gasly, F1 drivers would have been able to get their tyres up to temperature more effectively if the formation lap had been completed without the safety car Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

Would a normal formation lap have been better?

According to the drivers, the rest of the track had already dried by that point, meaning it was simply a matter of surviving the final two corners. Starting on slicks therefore made sense, as did the FIA’s decision to opt for a standing start.

That said, several drivers were critical of how the start procedure was carried out at Zandvoort.

"If we would go the way we did with one lap behind the safety car and a standing start, then I would have preferred to just do a normal out-lap, so we would have pushed a bit faster,” Pierre Gasly said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I thought the point was to go at least once through the last corner and the banking with the safety car before doing the normal race start. And yeah, it was damp."

According to the Alpine driver, the FIA would have been better off choosing between two conventional options: a rolling start behind the safety car or a standing start with a normal formation lap.

"I'm sure we'll review at the next race what the drivers' feedback was," Gasly continued. "But I think it was either no safety car and only one formation lap or with the safety car at least giving us one extra lap."

Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson shared that view and added that he already knew before the start that the procedure would lead to chaos.

Lawson emphasises that he deliberately left more margin than his team-mate Verstappen in the final corner Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

"I don't know why we had the safety car. To do a standing start and also do a lap behind the safety car makes no sense," Lawson said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I'm not sure what the reasoning of that was, but I feel like we could all see that coming. We were all probably saying the same thing before when we got the news, but we didn't have control over that."

FIA explains reasoning behind safety car formation lap

When asked by Motorsport.com, the FIA clarified that it acted on the information available at the time.

The race director first sent the medical car out for a reconnaissance lap, something an FIA spokesperson said does not normally happen.

The feedback from the medical car was that there was still standing water at Turns 2 and 3, with Turn 3 – the Hugenholtz corner – also being the first banked corner on the circuit. Based on that information, the FIA considered it safer to complete the formation lap behind the safety car.

The intention at that point was to have a standing start, but by completing the formation lap behind the safety car, race control kept both options open. If the standing water had been deemed too dangerous, it could still have opted for a rolling start.

Williams driver Carlos Sainz, however, felt the latter would not have been a solution and would not have prevented the chaos in the final corner.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I think, given it was towards the end of the lap, a non-standing start, a rolling start, would have ended up in the same result, because by that time we were all one by one," Sainz said. "So I don't think it would have changed much. It's an unfortunate situation with a lot of water in only one corner."

It therefore came down to the drivers’ own judgement, with Lawson stressing that he deliberately left more margin – considerably more than Verstappen, who was running ahead of him.

"It was just impossible. The whole first half of the lap was dry and then the last few corners were completely soaked. So, it was really easy to do that [what Max has done] when you have this much power on a slick tyre," he said.

"I really lifted out of it because honestly I had no confidence in how much grip we were going to have there and I think Max was probably trying to get closer and make an overtake, and just lost it."

Verstappen himself, however, did not want to blame any external factors and stressed that he had simply made a mistake.

Sports.title: Hamilton explains Dutch GP radio outburst over Ferrari team orders
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has urged Ferrari to be more like Mercedes with its efficiency after growing frustrated by a lack of team orders during the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix.

The Ferrari driver finished fourth in an action-packed contest at Zandvoort on Sunday, with his mid-race battle with stablemate Charles Leclerc arguably being Hamilton’s defining period.

Hamilton had just overtaken McLaren’s Oscar Piastri for fifth on lap 35 and was right behind a much slower Leclerc, so was therefore angling for team orders but they did not arrive.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job,” complained a sarcastic Hamilton, who eventually took fourth when Leclerc pitted on lap 43 to end a very drawn-out process.

That is compared to Mercedes which swapped its cars with seven laps remaining, as George Russell gave second to Kimi Antonelli, who had fresher tyres so could attack Lando Norris.

Although the McLaren driver still took victory, it was a decision both Antonelli and Russell agreed with as they completed the podium ahead of Hamilton and fifth-placed Leclerc.

“I want to win,” Hamilton told F1 TV. “I want to win. I'm here to win and it is difficult when you're looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it's done - they execute straight away.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy. It's not the same here and that's a little bit difficult, but we just have to take it.

“We'll take it offline, and when I go back now, I'll speak to them about it.”

Russell did well to take third though, as he feared that Mercedes had “lost a double podium”, because by letting Antonelli by, it put him under instant pressure from Hamilton.

The Mercedes driver held firm though, helped by the lap 70 virtual safety car for debris at Turn 5, and Hamilton reckons the earlier fiasco harmed his chances of overtaking his former team-mate.

When asked by Motorsport.com if the VSC stopped him from getting a podium, the seven-time world champion replied: “It felt like it was the closest opportunity I had.

“I think I'd come out of [Turn] 14 pretty close to him and I was just opening SM [Straight Line Mode] and just getting on the boost.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT Images via Getty Images

“I don't know whether or not we would have got by because the Mercedes is just so quick. You saw the McLaren fly past just on power. We're losing like four tenths of a lap here just on straight lines.

“So that was a challenge, but I do think the time was lost when I was behind Charles, which ultimately meant I had a bigger distance to cover to try and catch up with George at the end.”

The result leaves Hamilton tied with Russell in second and 59 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining, a run where the Ferrari driver is hoping to add to his Barcelona victory.

But to do so Hamilton thinks the Italian marque must reduce its engine power deficit to Mercedes, despite various chassis upgrades it brought to the Netherlands.

“The one thing I'm definitely really proud of the team, they brought an upgrade here this weekend,” the 41-year-old added.

“We are getting closer to them but half the season we've been down in power. We really need to pick up the power if we're going to be anywhere near trying to fight for them and closing the gap to them.”

Sports.title: What caused Verstappen’s F1 Dutch GP crash
Sports.content:
Making mistakes may be uncharacteristic of Max Verstappen, but that’s exactly what the four-time world champion did on the first lap of his home Formula 1 race.

Starting the Dutch Grand Prix from seventh on the grid after feeling unwell all weekend, Verstappen took a decent getaway but found himself squeezed on the grass in a four-wide moment on the run to Turn 1. He was consequently challenged by Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson in the following corners – which he didn’t mind: “We are allowed to race, so I think that's normal.”

Verstappen eventually held on to that seventh position, but a rain shower which occurred some 50 minutes before the start had dampened the track, and two drivers lost control in the banked final corner on lap one.

While Gabriel Bortoleto escaped from a 360-degree pirouette unscathed, Red Bull’s superstar couldn’t catch the RB22 and suffered a substantial crash, which caused a red flag.

“I think the start is just a consequence of what is happening on the right. It's OK, it can happen,” Verstappen commented regarding about the incident at lights out.

“Then, yeah, I got caught out. It was still quite wet in that corner, and as soon as I saw the dry patch coming, I was like, ‘Now you can accelerate’, but clearly that didn't work. So probably it was still a bit too early.”

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

Verstappen described the impact as “a decent hit” but clarified he’d “had worse”.

Red Bull eventually endured its worst grand prix since the April break results-wise, with Lawson its top car in seventh.

Verstappen did admit to “a disappointing weekend” in terms of pace as McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes were out of reach, but this situation was no surprise to him.

“I wish for more, but you need to be realistic this season,” the Red Bull racer insisted. “We are the fourth-fastest team, so it's not like walking up to Zandvoort and suddenly we can do some magic things.

“It's just how it is, other teams have brought upgrades, we haven't. When you're already on the back foot, it puts you even more on the back foot. So, there's nothing surprising, it's just the reality that we live in.”

So Verstappen will now focus on resting ahead of the Italian Grand Prix, two weeks from now: “I've just not been feeling well. I'm just looking forward to a break where I can just recover also, because I really didn't feel good.”

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Norris overhauls Antonelli for victory, Verstappen suffers heavy crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris produced a mega drive to win the Dutch Grand Prix from pole while home hero Max Verstappen caused a red flag by crashing out.

The McLaren driver crossed the line 11.5s ahead of runner-up Kimi Antonelli, with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell completing the podium at Zandvoort.

It came after Norris pipped sprint winner Russell for pole ahead of third-placed Antonelli and they all, like the rest of the grid, started on slicks despite rain an hour before lights out.

But the rain was on and off causing a wet-dry surface, the dangers of which emerged at the end of the opening lap once Norris had a perfect getaway while Antonelli overtook Russell at Turn 1.

That’s because Verstappen dipped a tyre onto the white line on the inside of the final corner, causing the Red Bull driver to spin into the barrier which spread debris on the circuit.

“Yeah that’s it - sorry!,” said the Dutchman via team radio, having brought out the red flag just as Gabriel Bortoleto also had a 360-degree spin at the banking but somehow avoided damage.

So another standing start followed - after Oliver Bearman suffered an engine failure on the formation tour - and much to Norris’ dismay this time, as Antonelli squeezed by at Turn 1 for the lead.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

That was despite softs on the McLaren compared to mediums for Antonelli, who essentially had a double delight as title rival Russell lost third to hard runner Oscar Piastri at Turn 7.

Russell just didn’t have the pace, soon being pressurised by Charles Leclerc as he reported balance problems, but the tight track allowed him to hold firm before swapping mediums for hards on lap 18.

McLaren responded the previous lap with Piastri, but this backfired as a slow 5.4s stop put him behind Russell just as Antonelli had streaked 2.2s clear of Norris out front.

That gap closed to a second once the pit window - where all the frontrunners chose hard tyres bar Leclerc on mediums - had passed, yet the reigning champion struggled to make inroads.

The wheel-to-wheel battles were more prevalent lower down: Yuki Tsunoda came out on top in a mega multi-car fight for the top 10, while Leclerc was constantly on Piastri’s tail.

That little battle finally ended on lap 34 when the Ferrari and McLaren went through the opening corners wheel-to-wheel, only for Leclerc to edge by for fourth around the outside of Turn 3.

There was yet more misery for Piastri as he was overtaken for fifth at Turn 1 on the following tour by Lewis Hamilton, who quickly closed in on team-mate Leclerc.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

The seven-time world champion was angling for team orders but they did not arrive and Hamilton sarcastically told his Ferrari squad: “Great way of wasting time guys, good job!”

Hamilton eventually moved by though once Leclerc made his second pitstop on lap 43, two tours after the Mercedes duo, and five before Norris came in for another set of hard tyres.

But Ferrari kept Hamilton out which left him with first on track, yet the battle for the net lead emerged behind as Norris rapidly closed on Antonelli, who complained about his rear Pirellis.

So come lap 54 Hamilton, Antonelli and Norris were all within a second and the reigning world champion made a sweeping move on Antonelli around the outside of Turn 1.

It was that same lap that Norris subsequently took the actual lead at Turn 11 from Hamilton, who dropped behind Antonelli at Turn 1 the following lap - just as Esteban Ocon caused a virtual safety car by stopping at Turn 4.

“Are you using me as a guinea pig,” complained Hamilton, wanting to pit, and that he finally did under the VSC by taking softs - likewise for Antonelli, while Norris and now second-placed Russell stayed out on hard rubber.

Norris admitted he was “worried” by that decision and had reasons to be so, as the advantage of the fresher tyre became evident with Antonelli quickly reducing his gap to Russell.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Mercedes eventually told the Briton to let his team-mate by with the swap occurring at Turn 1 on lap 65, but this left Russell vulnerable against Hamilton, claiming “we’ve lost a double podium”.

But Russell held firm, helped by a brief VSC on lap 70 for debris at Turn 5, to take the final podium spot, 4.3s behind Antonelli and 15.8s off Norris who took his second win of 2026.

Hamilton finished fourth, Leclerc took fifth and Piastri was sixth, while Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson, Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg, Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly respectively completed the top 10.

The result has extended Antonelli’s championship advantage, as the 19-year-old leaves the Netherlands with a 59-point lead over both Russell and Hamilton in second.

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP red-flagged after Verstappen crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1's Dutch Grand Prix has been red-flagged after one lap following an enormous accident for home hero Max Verstappen.

At the end of lap 1 on a damp circuit, Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull as he tagged the white line on the inside of Zandvoort's final turn - the banked, flat out Luyendyk corner leading onto the main straight.

Verstappen veered head on into the outside wall, before his car crossed the track and came to a standstill on the inside.

The Dutchman soon reported he was OK and apologised to his team for ending his race early.

Verstappen was fortunate not to be collected by any other cars, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly taking avoiding action, while in the background Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also narrowly avoided a huge accident as his team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto spun in front of him.

Under the red flag all drivers gathered in the pitlane awaiting the restart. They were having to navigate a field of debris before pit entry, but teams are allowed to change tyres under a red flag ahead of the restart. That restart is expected at 15:33 local time.

Max Verstappen Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

At the time Verstappen was running seventh after a disappointing qualifying session. Polesitter Lando Norris retained his lead during a chaotic start sequence, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli passing George Russell for second.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc gaining two positions to hold down fourth ahead of the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri and team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

For Verstappen, the accident marks an unfortunate end to a six-year spell racing on home soil, winning the first three editions of the Dutch Grand prix revival in 2021, 2022 and 2023. The race will disappear from the calendar after organisers decided not to pursue a contract renewal with F1 management.

Earlier in the week, the four-time world champion announced he had extended his Red Bull contract until the end of the 2030 season.

Sports.title: Stroll demanded penalties after Bearman and Bortoleto passed red pit exit light | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lance Stroll urged race control to penalise two of his rivals for leaving the pit lane while a red light was shown during the Dutch Grand Prix.

The incident occured as the field left the pits when the race resumed following the stoppage caused by Max Verstappen’s crash.

The pit lane exit lights were green as the field began to leave the pits. However after Fernando Alonso passed by the signal changed to a flashing red light.

Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto both drove past the flashing red light. Neither acknowledged the pit lane exit had been closed and continued to the grid, though Bearman suffered a power unit failure before he got there.

Stroll, who was following the pair, noticed the light had changed and alerted his race engineer Gary Gannon:

Stroll The lights red, huh? Light’s red. Gannon Checking, I’m checking. Stroll I’m not going unless it’s green. Gannon Yeah, understood Lance. Stroll 10 seconds later

Tell me if I can go or not. Gannon Waiting to hear back from the FIA.

The signal changes to green and Stroll leaves the pit exit

He repeatedly called for the drivers who had passed the red signal to be penalised. Stroll correctly noted that Formula 1’s penalty guidelines state drivers who pass a red light at the pit lane exit during a race should receive 10-second stop-and-go penalties:

Stroll So everybody that went under a red should get a penalty. Gannon Yep, yep. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Understood, we’ll report it. So the back of the pack… Stroll It’s the rules. Gannon …the back of the pack is in nine, so you can build temp. Good pushing to build temp

Stroll appeared to be under the impression that many more drivers than just the two immediately in front of him had driven past the red signal:

Stroll It’s clear that everyone went under red, then they all should get a penalty. Gannon We’re checking it now. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Yeah, we’re checking now. Stroll Everybody. Gannon It started out green and then it went red and we’re checking who went through red and reporting it ASAP. Absolutely Lance.
