The Aston Martin driver continued to press his case on the formation lap, even when his race engineer was trying to warn him about Bearman’s stoppage ahead:

Gannon ‘Bearman is slow between 10-11. Yellow ahead for Bearman stopped. Bearman stopped between 10-11. Watch for Bearman… Stroll Those are the rules. Gannon …there, watch for Bearmen. Stroll The rules are: it’s red… Gannon Lance, we’ve reported it, we reported it. Now let’s get focused getting around to the grid, okay? We’ve reported and they will action it.

However the stewards chose instead to only reprimand the pair, pointing out that the incident occured before the race resumption and neither had gained an advantage.

“The pit exit light turned red when the driver was approaching the pit exit to join the track for the re-start of the race after a suspension,” they noted. “Such an infringement happening during the race normally requires a very significant penalty as the drivers are obliged to obey light signals at all times. However, in this case the infringement did not happen during a live race, but rather on the build-up before the re-start, although the race had technically already resumed in accordance with Article B5.15.2g.

“In addition to that, the stewards acknowledge that neither any advantage was gained nor any potentially dangerous or unsafe situation was created. Therefore a reprimand to the driver is deemed appropriate given the mitigating circumstances and the unique scenario.”

Sports.title: Mercedes is “clearly not the fastest car on the grid any more” claims Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes are no longer the team to beat in Formula 1 claimed Andrea Kimi Antonelli after McLaren’s second consecutive victory in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Lando Norris passed Antonelli on his way to victory in yesterday’s race at Zandvoort, as he did in the previous round in Hungary.

“For sure, we’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid,” said Antonelli, who holds a 59-point lead in the drivers’ championship. “We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.”

However Antonelli has high hopes for Mercedes’ forthcoming upgrade for its W17. “The team has been working super-hard on this next package that is coming up and they just want to make sure that it’s going to work out well once we put it on,” he said.

“So for sure, in this race, it’s going to be more difficult, it’s going to be challenging, but we’re ready to do our best and to maximise every opportunity. And then hopefully it’s going to be our turn to bring the package that’s going to give us a little bit of the upper hand again.”

Antonelli’s team mate George Russell believes McLaren’s strength in the last two races has been partly due to the similarities in the track layouts.

“I don’t think it’s a major surprise for us, seeing how competitive Lando was this weekend, considering he won in Budapest,” he said. “It’s a very similar circuit with the long corners, high tyre degradation, with the two-stop strategy, so there’s a lot of similarities between the two circuits.

“I think this may continue for the coming two or three races until we start to bring more to the car, and fingers crossed our competitors don’t.”

He expects Mercedes will be “slightly more competitive” in the next race at Monza, the fastest circuit on the calendar. “However, I believe Ferrari have an engine upgrade incoming, and the truth is we just don’t know.

“But I do believe that these high-degradation circuits really suit McLaren very well, and especially Lando. He’s always been a bit of a specialist in those conditions. We also saw it last year. Monza may be slightly different, but I think they are the team to beat right now.”

Sports.title: Russell defends “fair” decision to let Antonelli into second place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.

Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.

However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.

“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.

“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”

Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.

“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.

“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says extra pit stop “put George at risk” too | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell

Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.

Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.

“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.

“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”

Sports.title: “We weren’t unlucky”: Hamilton tells Ferrari their tactics cost him third place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton told Ferrari they cost him a chance to finish third by failing to use team orders during the Dutch Grand Prix.

He finished fourth behind George Russell after losing time earlier in the race when he caught team mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton repeatedly urged Ferrari to tell Leclerc to let him through, but the team instead to chose wait a lap and then bring the leading Ferrari into the pits.

“Let’s not hold ourselves up from an potentially better result,” Hamilton told the team when he caught Leclerc.

After spending a lap behind Leclerc, Hamilton warned Ferrari “we’re just losing time.” Once Leclerc came in, Hamilton sarcastically remarked: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

Hamilton’s attempt to pass Russell at the end of the race was thwarted when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed. After he finished fourth race engineer Carlos Santi told Hamilton: “Thank you Lewis, was a bit unlucky with Russell.”

“We weren’t unlucky,” Hamilton replied, “we lost time earlier on and that cost us P3.”

“We can discuss it offline,” he added.

Hamilton explained his frustration after the race, pointing out Mercedes did not hesitate to swap the order of their two drivers when it benefitted them overall.

“I want to win,” said Hamilton. “I’m here to win and it is difficult when you’re looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it’s done and they execute straight away.

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it was not the same here.

“That’s a little bit difficult but we just have to take it, we’ll take it off line. When I go back now, I’ll speak to them about it.”

Sports.title: Moses Itauma’s Record Chase Cannot Sell Hrgovic PPV
Sports.content:
Mentioning Tyson invites attention that does Itauma no favors. Tyson was already must-see television before defeating Berbick in 1986 because of the way he destroyed opponents. He pressed forward, stayed in the pocket, threw combinations, and kept attacking until the fight was over. Itauma is not that type of heavyweight. He fights on the outside, waiting to launch one shot rather than remaining close and overwhelming opponents with power shots. When opponents pressure him, he tends to retreat to escape. It’s a style that looks like a bigger version of Shakur Stevenson.

That approach may be effective, but it is not guaranteed to turn him into a pay-per-view attraction. Fans watching Tyson knew they would see aggression and violence.

His personality doesn’t make up for what he lacks in the excitement department. Itauma looks half-asleep during interviews and brings low energy to the promotion. He comes across as dull rather than as a young heavyweight eager to take over the division.

Patterson also won a vacant heavyweight championship, defeating Archie Moore after Rocky Marciano retired. Itauma would not be breaking new ground by taking an available title. He would simply be doing it two months younger than Patterson.

The more revealing contrast remains Tyson. Berbick held the WBC belt when Tyson destroyed him in the ring. Itauma received his opportunity after Oleksandr Usyk relinquished the IBF title and Frank Sanchez agreed to step aside.

Winning would make Itauma an IBF champion, but the promotional campaign is using their ages to connect two fighters whose appeal and championship victories bear little resemblance.

Queensberry also waited too long to present Hrgovic as dangerous. A few interviews during fight week cannot transform him into a marquee name. Daniel Dubois would have brought greater attention from fans, punching power, and a real British rivalry.

The age statistic is being asked to create interest that the matchup, undercard, and promotion have failed to produce. Casual fans do not purchase pay-per-views to watch someone move ahead of Patterson on a list. Their money goes toward fighters and rivalries they already care about.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Takes Credit For Zepeda, Teofimo Title Wins
Sports.content:
His loss was not as one-sided as the official scores of 118-110, 118-110, and 119-109 suggested. Stevenson landed 295 of 565 punches, compared with Zepeda’s 272 of 979. Shakur was far more accurate, connecting at approximately 52% against Zepeda’s 28%, but only 23 landed punches separated them across 12 rounds.

A later victory over Lamont Roach Jr. gave Zepeda the WBC lightweight title that Stevenson previously held. It was his first full world championship, but he had already reached interim title status before meeting Shakur.

What was interesting is how Shakur handled it publicly. Before Zepeda fought Lamont Roach Jr, Shakur openly predicted Roach would dish out a beating. Once Zepeda walked away with the full WBC lightweight title, Shakur immediately flipped his tune to build up his own credentials.

By comparison, Lopez had a much stronger championship history. He defeated Vasiliy Lomachenko at lightweight and Josh Taylor at light welterweight before surrendering his WBO 140-pound belt to Stevenson in January. Saturday’s majority-decision victory over Rolando Romero made Teofimo a three-division champion.

Those latest wins add value to Shakur’s record because they confirm that Zepeda and Lopez continued operating at the championship level. Stevenson deserves credit for beating them, especially his dominant performance against Teofimo at Madison Square Garden.

However, the WBC title came to Zepeda through his victory over Roach, while Lopez moved to welterweight and took Romero’s WBA belt.

At most, Shakur can use those wins as proof that he defeated quality opposition. He cannot take partial ownership of championships that Zepeda and Teofimo won through their own performances.

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Says Teofimo Lopez May Delay Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
Allowing Teofimo to take that fight first would only weaken Catterall’s position. Lopez could earn the enormous payday, lose the title in the process, or move toward another opponent, leaving Catterall waiting without any guarantee that his opportunity would retain the same value. His better business decision is to demand the Lopez fight next and pursue the Garcia–Benn winner afterward.

Jack Catterall Blocks Teofimo Lopez’s Three-Unification Plan

Jack Catterall says Teofimo Lopez does not have the freedom to select another opponent after capturing the WBA “Super” welterweight title from Rolando Romero on Saturday night.

When Ring Magazine asked who Teofimo should fight next following his majority-decision win, Catterall responded that the WBA had already provided the answer through its 180-day directive.

“180 days @WBABoxing which means November ✅ I understand the politics of boxing better than most. Rolly had a voluntary; now it’s time for my shot! No ducks, no more swerving. Me v Teo next,” said Catterall on X.

His message also answered Teofimo’s intention to pursue three consecutive unification matches without making a mandatory defense. Such a schedule would leave no room for Catterall and require the WBA to ignore or alter its previous ruling.

Romero was elevated to Super champion before Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s secondary welterweight title on May 23. The WBA ordered the Super champion to face the winner within a maximum of 180 days, placing the deadline in November.

One voluntary defense has already been granted. Romero used it against Teofimo rather than facing Catterall, and the British southpaw does not believe the new champion should receive another exception.

A fight with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn is Teofimo’s preferred next step, and he has discussed collecting the remaining welterweight belts. Those matches involve more money than a Catterall defense, which explains his preference. Still, taking Romero’s belt also meant inheriting the obligation attached to it.

This is not merely a request for consideration. Catterall holds the secondary belt and has a WBA directive supporting his demand. If the organization enforces its own ruling, three straight unification fights will have to wait.

Teofimo Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory

Teofimo Lopez believes his DAZN contract will take him directly from one welterweight unification to another without stopping for a mandatory defense of his WBA title.

The newly crowned champion is targeting Liam Paro, the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn, and eventually Devin Haney. If Lopez gets his way, every appearance during the rest of his deal will involve another champion.

During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Mannix: Jaron Ennis vs. Josh Kelly Talks Are Advanced
Sports.content:
“Boots is chomping at the bit to get back in the ring, and I’m told there are advanced negotiations for Jaron Ennis to face Josh Kelly in a unification fight sometime in November or December,” Mannix said during DAZN’s Sources Say. “Josh Kelly, coming off a win this past month, had some injury issues after that fight. He had a nose injury, but Matchroom, Boots’ team, believes that injury will be healed. I’m told they are targeting that fight on the East Coast before the end of this year.”

If Kelly were a stronger champion, he might be able to make several defenses and earn money from the IBF title before pursuing a unification. His July 25 showing against Caoimhin Agyarko demonstrated why waiting would carry considerable risk.

Heavy punishment left Kelly with a badly damaged nose as he squeezed out a narrow 12-round unanimous decision in Jeddah. Agyarko is ranked No. 15 by the IBF, yet Kelly struggled to keep him under control.

Higher in the IBF rankings are Brandon Adams, former champion Bakhram Murtazaliev, Nikita Tszyu, Israil Madrimov, Ben Mahoney, Xander Zayas, Milan Prat, Giovani Santillan, Yan Marcos, Pavel Sosulin, Ibrahima Diallo, and Bilal Fawaz. Kelly would have a difficult time holding the belt for long against that group.

His title-winning victory over Murtazaliev in Newcastle was also viewed by many as a hometown gift. Kelly stayed mobile rather than engage for long. Near the end of rounds, he used quick shoeshine combinations to impress the judges. Murtazaliev landed the heavier punches and dropped Kelly in the ninth, yet lost on two cards.

Ennis presents a far more severe test. The WBA and WBO champion has more speed, power, combination punching, and offensive variety. The difference is wide enough that placing the fight in Newcastle probably would not change the outcome.

That nose injury may be the greatest immediate concern. If it breaks down during sparring, the unification may have to be postponed. Assuming Kelly gets through camp, taking the Ennis fight now makes more financial sense than continuing with lower-paying title defenses.

Sports.title: Regis Prograis Calls Rocky Marciano Overrated
Sports.content:
“For me, I think Rocky Marciano was overrated,” Prograis said on social media. “He retired undefeated, right? But in this book, I bought this book about Sonny Liston. It said right here about Rocky Marciano that ‘his good fortune was to rise to prominence at a time when his major competitors were either old, like 37-year-old Joe Louis.’ He was 37 when he fought him. Joe Walcott was 37 years old. A natural light heavyweight like Ezzard Charles was 34 years old, and then Archie Moore was 41 at the time.”

The overall point has some merit, but several ages quoted by Prograis are inaccurate. Louis was 37, but Walcott was 38 when Marciano took his heavyweight title in September 1952. Charles was 32 in their first fight and turned 33 before the rematch, not 34. Moore’s birth year remains disputed, leaving him either 38 or 41 when he challenged Marciano in 1955.

Prograis also accused Marciano of avoiding 6-foot-3 Cuban contender Nino Valdes because of his size.

“They had a Cuban fighter called Nino Valdes, and he didn’t want to fight him,” Prograis said. “He said he was too big. So I know a lot of older guys say that Rocky Marciano was this and undefeated this. But I feel Rocky Marciano was overrated at the time.”

Valdes had a legitimate case after rising to the top of the heavyweight rankings, but saying Marciano simply refused to face him leaves out part of the story.

The Cuban lost a 15-round title eliminator to Moore in May 1955. Marciano then met Moore four months later and stopped him in the ninth round. Valdes also suffered numerous defeats during Marciano’s championship reign, making the claim that he was deliberately avoided difficult to prove.

Marciano’s leading opponents were older, and his era lacked the talent found in later generations. Still, Walcott, Charles, and Moore remained dangerous elite fighters. Those victories do not settle every historical argument, but dismissing his entire career as fortunate goes too far.

Sports.title: Rick Glaser Tattles on Eddie Hearn to Turki
Sports.content:
“Turki Alalshikh, you have a great event in the deep planning stage for November 20 on Netflix at the Mecca of Boxing Madison Square Garden in New York And as you know, Eddie Hearn is attempting to undermine your great event,” said Glaser on X. “Whatever Hearn’s reasons may be, personal gain, or other motives, it’s causing havoc in Boxing circles, & the sporting public, especially with Hearn saying on video’s “I don’t care who this upsets” as he mouths off. “Turki Alalshikh, you deserve much better than you are receiving from Hearn in his lack of respect. Best regards from Sonya & I.”

The sign-off completes the effect. Having reported Hearn’s alleged misconduct and lavished Turki with praise, Glaser closes the message as though he were sending a polite letter to a school principal.

Nothing in the post proves that Hearn is trying to damage the event for “personal gain” or any other hidden motive. He represents Anthony Joshua, who signed for the fight to take place at a UK stadium. Joshua prefers Wembley, while Turki and Tyson Fury favor New York.

As Joshua’s promoter, Hearn is supposed to argue his position, even when it clashes with Turki’s plans. That does not automatically make him disloyal or disrespectful.

The message presents the dispute as something more serious. In Glaser’s version, Hearn is creating chaos, sabotaging Turki’s work, and failing to show proper gratitude toward the man financing the event. It is an extraordinary display of public loyalty. Glaser did everything except ask Turki to send Hearn to the headmaster’s office.

Sports.title: Julio Cesar Chavez Broke Edwin Rosario Piece By Piece
Sports.content:
Rosario presented the kind of danger Chavez had not encountered. The WBA champion had knocked out Livingstone Bramble in two rounds the previous year and possessed genuine power in both hands. He also attacked Chavez’s opposition before the bout, dismissing many of his previous opponents as “guys right out of the bar.”

Rosario Could Not Keep Chavez Away

Any doubts about Chavez at lightweight disappeared quickly. Rather than feeling his way into the contest, the 25-year-old Mexican closed the distance and began digging hooks into Rosario’s body.

Rosario had success during the third and fourth rounds. He landed several hard punches and briefly forced Chavez onto the ropes, but nothing discouraged the advancing challenger. Chavez absorbed Rosario’s best shots, turned him, and reclaimed control with short combinations. Once the bout moved into close range, the difference became brutal. Chavez did not simply walk forward and throw punches. He slipped Rosario’s right hand, blocked shots with his elbows and gloves, then answered before the Puerto Rican champion could reset.

The body attack gradually robbed Rosario of his movement and power. Chavez mixed hooks downstairs with uppercuts and straight rights to the head, rarely wasting a punch. HBO’s PunchStat count credited him with landing 450 of 743 punches, an extraordinary 61 percent. Rosario connected with 263 of 731.

A Beating That Lasted Too Long

By the later rounds, Rosario’s left eye was swollen shut, his face was cut, and blood covered his nose and mouth. Still, he refused to go down. His courage allowed the punishment to continue far longer than it should have.

Chavez looked almost untouched as he drove Rosario into a corner during the 11th. With the champion taking another sustained attack, his corner threw in the towel. Referee Richard Steele stopped it at 2:38. All three judges had Chavez far in front: 98-92, 99-91, and 100-92.

The performance made Chavez a two-division champion and erased every question surrounding his move to lightweight. He had taken one of boxing’s most feared punchers, neutralized his power, and broken him down without ever needing a knockdown. Rosario brought danger into the ring that night, but Chavez made it disappear.

Sports.title: Teofimo Defeats Rolly, Now He Has His Eyes Set On Undisputed
Sports.content:
During the first three rounds of the world title bout, Lopez was in control as he used his jab and touched the body of Romero. Late in the fourth round, Romero landed a check left hook that knocked Lopez off balance.

In the fifth round, Rolly got more aggressive, and as a result, he landed a big left hook that produced a cut over Teofimo’s right eye.

Seconds later, Romero connected with a vicious overhand right that buckled Lopez’s knees.

Romero followed the big right hand with a flurry of shots, but Lopez was able to survive the round. Lopez bounced back in the sixth as he returned to his game plan of working off the jab and attacking the body.

Lopez continued to apply intelligent pressure in the seventh as he landed a solid right hand. As round seven was coming to a close, Romero caught Lopez with a powerful check left hook.

For the remainder of the WBA welterweight title bout, Teofimo Lopez fought a smart and very disciplined fight. Despite the low punch output, Rolly had the more eye-catching shots, but Teofimo outworked him and won by majority decision.

With the victory, Teofimo “The Takeover” Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) became a three-division world champion. As soon as Lopez was announced as the winner, the boxing community was seeking the answer to the proverbial question: What’s next?

During the post-fight press conference, Teofimo Lopez spoke about his future and the path he plans to travel in his boxing journey.

“I think I’m here, this is the road to undisputed, you know what I’m saying? I’m here to reclaim and collect all of the next world titles, and whoever the next champion is, that’s what it’s all about.”

Teofimo Lopez went on to say, “Honestly, I got four fights with, well now three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title.”

Currently, the world champions in the welterweight division are Teofimo Lopez (WBA), Devin Haney (WBO), Ryan Garcia (WBC), and Liam Paro (IBF). In his quest to become undisputed, the first step for Lopez is to become a unified world champion.

If Lopez wants what looks like the softer touch, a unification bout with IBF champion Liam Paro may be next. If Lopez wants a fight that is going to be a big event, then he may want to pursue a bout with the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner.

Ghana News.title: Adenta Circuit Court 1 judge cautions lawyers against attacking judges
Ghana News.content:
The Presiding Judge of the Adenta Circuit Court 1, Her Honour Angela Attachie, has cautioned lawyers to use the law and established ethical procedures to address grievances arising from court decisions rather than attacking judges.

She urged lawyers to desist from attempting to dictate how judges should act, stressing that there are legitimate legal avenues for challenging court decisions.

According to her, anyone dissatisfied with a ruling has the right to appeal to a higher court rather than resorting to public attacks, insults or threats against judges.

Her Honour Angela Attachie, who said she had personally come under attack over some of her rulings, stressed that the law provides mechanisms for addressing grievances against judicial decisions.

She noted that if the Ghana Bar Association paid closer attention to such conduct, some lawyers could face disciplinary action.

The judge also expressed concern about the conduct of some politicians who are lawyers, saying some resort to the media to “play to the gallery” instead of using the appropriate legal channels to challenge court decisions.

She said she had personally experienced attacks over some of her decisions at the Adenta Circuit Court 1.

She cited the case involving Abronye, saying she received threats from individuals over the matter, even though, according to her, he had never appeared before her court.

She revealed that the threats had compelled her to move with a bodyguard, although, under the applicable arrangements, a Circuit Court judge is not ordinarily entitled to one.

Her Honour Angela Attachie therefore appealed to the public to desist from threatening or attacking judges, stressing that judges consider the facts and evidence before them rather than the personalities involved in cases.

She emphasised that judges also have families and should not be subjected to threats and insults simply because someone disagrees with a court ruling.

The Presiding Judge made the remarks in an interview with the media during the inauguration of the KAAF University Faculty of Law Advisory Board, where she represented the Chief Justice, Justice Baffoe Bonnie.

She explained that the Advisory Board had been established to guide, mentor and advise the Faculty of Law to attain higher standards, with several Court of Appeal judges serving on the board.

Meanwhile, a Justice of the Court of Appeal and member of the Advisory Board, Justice Nana Yaw Barima Koddie Oppong, who spoke on behalf of the Board Chairperson, Professor Lydia A. Nkansah, said members of the board would work professionally with the management of KAAF University to achieve the objectives of the Faculty of Law.

For his part, the Council Chair of KAAF University, Professor K. B. Omane-Antwi, said the university was focused on producing ethical lawyers who could become authentic leaders in society.

According to him, the country needs lawyers who command public confidence, particularly at a time when public trust in the legal profession appears to be declining.

He said KAAF University had therefore placed strong emphasis on ethics in its law programme to ensure that its graduates stand out as responsible and principled professionals.

Ghana News.title: GH¢22billion DGPP loss is a deliberate profiteering scheme – Gideon Boako
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako

Tano North MP and Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako, has alleged that the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP) was structured as a “profiteering scheme”, resulting in a reported GH¢22 billion loss to the state.

The reported loss, equivalent to about US$1.7 billion, has triggered intense debate over the management of Ghana’s domestic gold purchasing operations and the respective roles of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), the Bank of Ghana (BoG) and the Ministry of Finance.

Speaking on Adom TV on Monday, August 24, Dr Boako alleged that the structure of the programme created opportunities for financial gain at the expense of the public purse.

He said the scale of the reported loss warranted a thorough examination of how the programme was designed and implemented, as well as who ultimately benefited from the transactions.

“The whole thing was a profiteering scheme. It was designed to create the create, and share the same. I call it ‘create the bag, share the bag’,” he said.

Dr Boako’s comments come amid an escalating dispute between the parliamentary Minority and GoldBod over the reported losses associated with the DGPP.

The disagreement has also drawn in GoldBod Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, and Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, with both sides challenging each other’s interpretation of the programme’s financial performance, losses and accountability.

The Minority has been demanding greater parliamentary scrutiny of the reported loss, while GoldBod has disputed interpretations that seek to attribute the loss directly to the Board.

Dr Boako’s allegation adds to growing calls for greater clarity on the transactions underpinning the DGPP and the financial implications for the state.

Ghana News.title: Boako questions GoldBod’s GH¢907m profit claim over alleged GH¢1bn BoG overdraft
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee and Member of Parliament for Tano North, Dr Gideon Boako

Tano North MP and Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Gideon Boako, has questioned claims by the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) that it recorded a profit of about GH¢907 million, arguing that the figure does not adequately account for an alleged GH¢1 billion overdraft owed to the Bank of Ghana (BoG).

Dr Boako claims GoldBod obtained about GH¢1 billion in overdraft from the central bank and argues that the liability should be reflected in the institution’s financial accounts when assessing its overall financial position.

Speaking on Adom TV on Monday, August 24, he questioned how GoldBod could describe itself as profitable if the reported overdraft remained outstanding.

“I’ve heard people say that GoldBod says they made a profit of GH¢907m, but that cannot be true because GoldBod took GH¢1bn overdraft from Bank of Ghana and if that is reflected in their books, they’ll actually be in a loss,” he said.

His comments come amid an ongoing political and economic dispute over the financial performance of GoldBod and the accounting treatment of transactions under the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP).

GoldBod has reported a profit of about GH¢907 million, while the Minority in Parliament has been demanding greater clarity over a reported GH¢22 billion loss associated with the DGPP.

The Minority has argued that the reported loss requires parliamentary scrutiny, while GoldBod has maintained that its own financial performance should be distinguished from losses recorded on the Bank of Ghana’s balance sheet.

Dr Boako’s latest claim adds to the debate over how the financial obligations and transactions involving GoldBod and the central bank should be accounted for and assessed.

Ghana News.title: Any growth model built on environmental destruction will fail – Prof. Bokpin on galamsey
Ghana News.content:
Professor of Finance and economist at the University of Ghana Business School (UGBS), Godfred Bokpin, has warned that Ghana cannot achieve sustainable economic development through a growth model that relies heavily on illegal mining, environmental destruction and primary commodities.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, August 24, Prof Bokpin criticised illegal mining, commonly known as galamsey, for its impact on Ghana’s forests, water bodies and wider ecosystems.

He said the government had placed too much emphasis on the foreign exchange earnings and macroeconomic gains associated with gold purchases and exports through the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), while paying insufficient attention to the environmental costs of gold production.

“Any growth model that is heavily reliant on environmental destruction and primary commodities is never sustainable. It is weak,” he said.

Prof Bokpin called for a comprehensive value-chain assessment of the gold sector that takes into account both the financial contribution of GoldBod and the environmental damage associated with illegal mining.

He argued that Ghana could only determine whether it had truly benefited from the current gold boom after comparing the financial gains with the full cost of the destruction of forests, water bodies and ecological systems.

Prof Bokpin also criticised what he described as the government’s approach to illegal mining, saying the celebration of gains from gold trading should not overshadow the long-term environmental consequences of the activity.

He described as selfish any attempt to celebrate macroeconomic stability while overlooking the damage being inflicted on the environment and the implications for future generations.

“We are sacrificing long-term survivability for short-term praise. This is not leadership,” he said.

Prof Bokpin further warned that Ghana’s recent economic gains remained vulnerable to global commodity price shocks.

He said a sharp decline in gold prices could reverse the gains within six to eight months, further highlighting the risks of relying heavily on gold and other primary commodities to drive economic growth.

Ghana News.title: Macroeconomic stability cannot justify environmental destruction – Prof Bokpin
Ghana News.content:
Professor of Finance and economist at the University of Ghana Business School (UGBS), Godfred Bokpin, has criticised attempts to justify the destruction of Ghana’s environment with the macroeconomic gains associated with gold trading.

Prof Bokpin argued that Ghana could not claim to be better off while forests, water bodies and ecosystems were being destroyed through irresponsible mining, commonly known as galamsey.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, August 24, while discussing the reported losses under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP), he said the environmental costs of gold production must be properly accounted for when assessing the sector’s contribution to the economy.

“It is a selfish position to think that you can cause such harm to the environment and water bodies in the name of macroeconomic stability and say you have gained,” he said.

Prof Bokpin maintained that the assessment of Ghana’s gold sector should go beyond foreign exchange earnings, reserve accumulation and improvements in key economic indicators.

He called for a comprehensive value-chain analysis that takes into account the cost of environmental degradation and the loss of ecological integrity before determining whether the country had truly benefited from the gold boom.

According to him, Ghana risks sacrificing its long-term sustainability for short-term economic gains if environmental destruction continues to be treated as an acceptable cost of economic growth.

He said responsible leadership required policymakers to pursue economic policies that protect the country’s natural resources while creating sustainable prosperity.

“Any growth model that is heavily reliant on environmental destruction and primary commodities is never sustainable,” he warned.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s gold-driven economic gains could vanish within months – Prof Bokpin
Ghana News.content:
Professor of Finance and economist at the University of Ghana Business School (UGBS), Godfred Bokpin, has warned that Ghana’s recent gold-driven economic gains could be wiped out within months if global gold prices experience a sharp decline.

Prof Bokpin said the country’s improved macroeconomic indicators remained highly exposed to fluctuations in international gold prices and therefore could not be considered durable.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, August 24, while discussing the reported losses under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP), he warned that a significant fall in gold prices could quickly reverse the gains being celebrated.

“If the gold price should dip by more than 40 per cent, this macroeconomic stability we talk about will only exist in the textbook,” he said.

According to Prof Bokpin, a price shock of that magnitude could wipe out the reported gains within six to eight months, leaving the economy significantly exposed.

He noted that commodity prices have historically undergone sharp corrections after periods of strong growth, cautioning policymakers against treating the current gold boom as evidence of lasting economic stability.

Prof Bokpin called for rigorous stress testing and sensitivity analysis to determine how Ghana’s economy, particularly its foreign exchange position and reserves, would withstand a significant decline in global gold prices.

Listen to him.

He also urged the government to adopt a broader value-chain approach to assessing the gold sector, taking into account not only foreign exchange earnings and reserve accumulation but also the environmental costs of gold production.

These costs, he said, include the destruction of forests, water bodies and wider ecological systems through irresponsible mining.

Prof Bokpin maintained that Ghana’s long-term development strategy must move beyond dependence on primary commodities and avoid economic growth that comes at the expense of environmental sustainability.

He warned that a growth model heavily reliant on primary commodities and environmental destruction would ultimately prove weak and unsustainable.

Ghana News.title: Egyptian Ambassador commends Ghana Armwrestling, calls for collaborative development
Ghana News.content:
The Ambassador of Egypt to Ghana, Wael Fathy Ahmed, has commended the leadership of Ghana Armwrestling Federation for the development of armwrestling in Ghana and called for stronger collaboration between Ghana and Egypt to advance armwrestling, the sports business, sports tourism and broader sports development across Africa.

Ambassador Fathy made the call when the leadership of the Ghana Armwrestling Federation engaged him at the embassy in discussions on strengthening Ghana-Egypt sports cooperation, with particular emphasis on Armwrestling development, its inclusion in the 2027 African Games, athlete and technical exchanges, sports business and tourism.

The meeting was attended by board members Dr. Kofi Addo-Agyekum, Edwin Amankwah, Joseph Cudjoe, Kenneth Odeng Adade, Husseni Akueteh Addy, Robert Appiah Ameyaw, and Benjamin Ohene Danso.

Ambassador Fathy commended Ghana's achievements in Armwrestling and described sport as an important platform for strengthening relations between Ghana and Egypt, particularly through youth development and people-to-people engagement.

“Ghana and Egypt have a long and historic relationship, and we should continue to look for new areas where our two countries can work together. Sport provides an excellent platform for bringing our people, especially our young people, closer together,” Ambassador Fathy said.

He called for cooperation that goes beyond competition, encouraging both countries to explore the commercial and tourism opportunities that can emerge from sporting activities. “We should look beyond the competition itself and see the wider opportunities that sport can create. There is potential for cooperation in investment, business, tourism, training and youth development, and these are areas where Ghana and Egypt can work together,” he added.

A key issue discussed was the inclusion of Armwrestling in the 2027 African Games in Egypt as a sports code. The Ghanaian delegation highlighted the sport's ability to contribute significantly to a host nation's medal campaign, pointing to its strong showing at the previous African Games hosted by Ghana and the potential for its inclusion to further strengthen Egypt's prospects on home soil.

President of the Ghana Armwrestling Federation and Africa Armwrestling Federation, Charles Osei Asibey Br, said the engagement provided an opportunity to build a strategic partnership between the two countries around Armwrestling and wider sports development.

“We see Egypt not only as a sporting powerhouse but also as a strategic partner for the development of Africa Armwrestling. Our objective is to build a partnership that goes beyond the table to technical development, athlete exchanges, business, tourism and sports diplomacy. We believe Ghana and Egypt can pull Africa together to create a stronger future for Armwrestling and African sport,” president Osei Asibey said.

He said the proposed collaboration could include technical and athlete exchanges, coaching programmes, training camps and competitions, allowing both countries to share expertise and strengthen the capacity of athletes, coaches, referees and administrators.

“When Armwrestling succeeds, it creates opportunities for athletes, coaches, businesses, tourism operators and young people. We want Ghana and Egypt to work together to make Cairo 2027 a success and to ensure that Armwrestling becomes a permanent and valuable part of the African Games movement,” Osei Asibey added.

The meeting further explored opportunities to connect the Ghanaian and Egyptian business communities through sports, including sponsorship, sports marketing, event management and investment, while using major Armwrestling competitions and training camps to promote sports tourism, hospitality and cultural exchange.

The Ghana Armwrestling Federation believes the engagement could provide a foundation for sustained Ghana-Egypt cooperation in Armwrestling, sports development, business and tourism, while strengthening sports diplomacy and contributing to the growth of the sport across Africa.

Ghana News.title: Ghana risks repeating post-HIPC debt mistakes – Prof Bokpin
Ghana News.content:
Economist and Professor of Finance at the University of Ghana, Godfred Bokpin

Economist Professor Godfred Bokpin has warned that Ghana risks repeating the mistakes that followed the country’s debt relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) programme if the government fails to properly manage the fiscal space created by recent debt restructuring and expenditure controls.

He said Ghana was now almost at the same stage it reached in 2006, when the country had completed the HIPC programme and benefited from significant debt relief.

Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Monday, August 24, Professor Bokpin said the current improvement in Ghana’s debt position should be treated as an opportunity to build a stronger and more sustainable economy, rather than as a justification for increased spending and borrowing.

“This is not the first time. Ghana is almost at the same stage where we were in 2006 when we had finished HIPC,” he said.

Professor Bokpin explained that Ghana completed the HIPC programme in 2004 and the Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative in 2006, after which the country’s debt-to-GDP ratio fell to below 30 per cent.

“When we're done, Ghana's debt-to-GDP ratio came down to less than 30 per cent,” he said.

The debt relief also significantly reduced debt-servicing pressures, giving the government greater fiscal space to finance economic activities.

According to Professor Bokpin, the improved fiscal position was one of the reasons Ghana sought to move away from its dependence on the International Monetary Fund (IMF) under former President John Agyekum Kufuor.

“In fact, it was a reason why Ghana filed for divorce from the IMF under President Kufuor in 2006. That we could be on our own,” he said.

He said the country believed it had sufficient fiscal room to finance growth and access international capital markets.

“We have fiscal space. We could inject growth to external debt financing by going to the international capital market. So we filed for that divorce,” he said.

The IMF subsequently approved the arrangement, paving the way for Ghana to return to the international capital market and issue its first Eurobond in 2007.

“It wasn't so difficult. The IMF granted the divorce, which also allowed us to do our first Eurobond in 2007. So we did all of that,” he said.

‘Within three years, the fiscal space was dissipated’

Professor Bokpin said the fiscal space created by the HIPC-related debt relief was not sustained, warning that Ghana could repeat the same pattern if the current gains are not managed prudently.

“But remember what happens. Within three years, the fiscal space we are celebrating today, we celebrated that also in 2006. Within three years, the fiscal space has been dissipated,” he said.

Ghana eventually returned to the IMF in 2009 after its fiscal position deteriorated.

“Ghana made a U-turn in 2009, asked for the hand of the IMF in another marriage. Within three years, we made a quick U-turn,” Professor Bokpin said.

He urged the government to use the current fiscal improvement to strengthen economic management systems and prevent another cycle of excessive borrowing and debt accumulation.

“So it's good news we are celebrating this fiscal space. Let's put in place the right structures, spend efficiently, borrow prudently, invest in enhancing the cash flow generating capacity of the economy,” he said.

Professor Bokpin stressed that the lessons from the post-HIPC period should guide current economic policy.

“Otherwise, we have been there before.”

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: US military says strike on alleged drug-smuggling boat kills two
World.content:
US Southern Command says that Sunday’s strike targeted a vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific.

The United States military said it struck a suspected drug-trafficking boat in the Pacific Ocean, killing two people.

In a Monday post on X, US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said Sunday’s strike targeted a vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific.

“Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking,” SOUTHCOM added.

“This operation is a clear and decisive reminder that SOUTHCOM is taking the fight directly to the cartels.”

Grainy, black-and-white video accompanying the post appeared to show a boat moving through the water immediately before a large explosion.

The post stated that under the direction of SOUTHCOM Commander General Francis L. Donovan, the Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal kinetic strike on the low-profile vessel.

“We are committed to imposing total systemic friction on narco-terrorists — disrupting their operations, dismantling their leadership and eliminating cartel terror across the region,” Donovan was quoted as saying.

“Let me be clear, we will not permit narco-terrorists to operate with impunity in the Western Hemisphere, nor will we allow their deadly poison to reach American communities. This operation is a powerful demonstration of our lethal precision, overwhelming capability, and absolute resolve to protect the U.S. homeland.”

The US military launched Operation Southern Spear in early September, with President Donald Trump arguing that Washington is effectively at war with Latin American drug cartels.



Since then, more than 200 people have been killed in strikes across the Eastern Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea, according to a tally by the AFP news agency.

However, the Trump administration has not provided definitive evidence that the targeted vessels were involved in drug trafficking.

Legal experts and rights groups warn that the attacks could amount to extrajudicial killings.

The Pentagon’s inspector general said in May that it would review whether the military followed standard targeting procedures, though the evaluation will not examine the legal authority behind the strikes.
