World.title: Kaizer Chiefs must make a difficult decision on fan fave’s future – Report
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs midfielder Nkosingiphile Ngcobo has endured a patchy few years at the club. Is it time to cut ties with him?

Ngcobo’s dismal Kaizer Chiefs stats aren’t improving

His best campaign, in terms of appearances in the league, was 2020-21 when he made 25 outings and scored four goals. Injuries have ravaged subsequent seasons, limiting Ngcobo to 16 appearances in 2021-22, then 13 in 2022-23, 12 in 2023-24 and 11 in 2024-25. Last term, encouragingly, he made 16 league appearances. However, since the aforementioned campaign in 2021, Ngcobo hasn’t managed more than two goals in a single season. He’s only scored two goals in his last three Betway Premiership seasons combined.

When is Kaizer Chiefs’ next match?

The Glamour Boys are next in action on Wednesday, 26 August, with an away clash against Richards Bay at 19:30. Chiefs are two points behind their tally at this equivalent stage last season, when they won their first three league encounters. Nkosingiphile Ngcobo’s future remains unclear after he was an unused substitute in the recent 1-1 draw with Sundowns.

World.title: The next few months could bring more than just a hot summer
World.content:
The WMO now gives a greater than 90% chance El Niño persists until at least November 2026, raising heatwave and veld fire risk: Image ChatGPT

The World Meteorological Organization says there’s now a greater than 90% chance this year’s El Niño will persist until at least November 2026, and with it comes a warning that goes beyond warm days at the beach.

What’s actually at risk this time

The extended forecast raises the risk of extreme heat, drought, and veld fires specifically across the country’s summer rainfall regions.

Above-normal temperatures are already expected from August through December, increasing the likelihood of hot spells and genuine heatwave conditions.



Sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region, the patch of ocean that strongly influences southern Africa’s climate, are already sitting around 1.7°C above average, a level the ENSO Reference Group classifies as a moderate El Niño with real potential to strengthen further.

Why this feels different from past warnings

Unlike earlier updates that focused mostly on rainfall and drought risk, this one names veld fires directly as a likely consequence, a real safety concern for rural communities, farmers, and anyone living near vegetation-heavy areas.

The ENSO Reference Group has continued to stress that South Africa enters this event with healthier dam levels and soil moisture than in past droughts, which should offer some protection, but that buffer does little to reduce fire risk once the land dries out and temperatures climb.



It’s hectic realising this isn’t just a “pack sunscreen” summer anymore, hey.

Are you already taking any precautions where you live, given the veld fire risk?

Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi…

World.title: The best Orlando Pirates XI of their released stars
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have made significant changes to the squad that has enjoyed remarkable success over the past four seasons.

Under Jose Riveiro, the Buccaneers won five trophies in three seasons, while Abdeslam Ouaddou followed that up by guiding the club to a treble in his first campaign in charge.

Ouaddou, however, inherited a strong squad built by Riveiro. He benefited from an established system, quality players and a winning culture, which made his transition into the job considerably easier.



After a difficult start to his tenure, the Moroccan eventually found the right formula. He initially relied heavily on new signings, starting his first two league matches with several of them, before reverting to more experienced players.

Orlando Pirates have been successful over the years

The 2026/27 season has brought another major overhaul, with Pirates bringing in nine new players while releasing several fan favourites.

With the CAF Champions League also on the horizon, some supporters fear that too many changes could disrupt the harmony and winning culture that has been built at the club.

The Buccaneers have made a winning start to the season, but they are yet to produce a truly convincing performance. None of the new signings have consistently stood out either.

Players such as Thabiso Sesane, Thabiso Lebitso and Tshegofatso Mabasa could have provided Ouaddou with valuable options as Pirates chase a second CAF Champions League star.

But what would Orlando Pirates’ best starting XI look like if the recently released players were still available?



Melusi Buthelezi

Buthelezi would take his place between the sticks if Sipho Chaine was injured.

Thabiso Lebitso

Lebitso’s versatility and work rate would make him a useful option at right-back, particularly in a team that needs defensive stability and attacking support from its full-backs. He always delivered when needed.

Olisa Ndah

Ndah’s strength, composure and experience would make him one of the first names in the centre of defence.

Thabiso Sesane

Sesane would partner Ndah at centre-back. His physical presence and ability to defend aggressively would complement Ndah well.In some games where Nkosinathi Sibisi and Lebone Seema needed to be rested, these duo would have taken over.

Bandile Shandu

Shandu’s versatility could have been utilised in defence especially at left-back.

Phillip Ndlondlo

Ndlondlo would add technical quality and composure in midfield, helping Pirates control possession and dictate the tempo. With Thalente Mbatha out, he would have stepped in.

Orlando Pirates have a solid mifield

Miguel Timm

Timm’s experience and work rate would provide balance alongside Ndlondlo, particularly in a midfield expected to compete domestically and in Africa. Orlando Pirates though have the midfield position covered.

Monnapule Saleng

Saleng’s pace, creativity and ability to beat defenders would give Pirates a dangerous attacking outlet. With Relebohile Mofokeng gone, he would added more spark on the attack especially on the right where the Buccaneers struggled.

Vincent Pule

Pule’s experience and technical ability would add another creative dimension to the attack.Just like Timm, he wouldn’t be needed given the quality in the left wing position.

Thembinkosi Lorch

Lorch’s versatility and attacking quality would make him a major threat in the final third.

Tshegofatso Mabasa

Mabasa would lead the line. His physical presence and ability to occupy defenders could give Orlando Pirates a different dimension in attack.

Orlando Pirates Best XI of recently released players

Melusi Buthelezi

Thabiso Lebitso – Olisa Ndah – Thabiso Sesane – Bandile Shandu

Phillip Ndlondlo – Miguel Timm

Monnapule Saleng – Vincent Pule – Thembinkosi Lorch

Tshegofatso Mabasa

What’s your take on this squad?

World.title: Jub Jub court case takes fresh twist after warrant of arrest
World.content:
Media personality Molemo “Jub Jub” Maarohanye faces firearm-related charges stemming from an alleged incident involving an e-hailing driver. Image: Instagram/@official_jubjub

Media personality Molemo “Jub Jub” Maarohanye will return to court next month after his firearm-related case was postponed in the Germiston Magistrates’ Court.

The court postponed the matter to 7 September 2026 after Maarohanye failed to appear due to alleged ill health.

A warrant of arrest was issued following his absence but was subsequently held over until his next court appearance.



What charges does Jub Jub face?

Maarohanye faces charges of discharging a firearm in a public place and pointing an object likely to lead someone to believe it was a firearm.

The charges stem from an incident involving an e-hailing driver in Edenvale on 14 June 2026.

During the investigation, law enforcement officials searched Maarohanye’s residence and seized a pellet gun.

The case had previously been postponed to allow investigators to complete outstanding work.

NPA says State is ready for trial

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) said prosecutors are now ready to proceed with the case.

“The State is ready to proceed with the prosecution and remains committed to ensuring that the matter is dealt with fairly and in accordance with the law,” NPA Gauteng communications officer Magaboke Mohlatlole said.



Maarohanye is expected back in the Germiston Magistrates’ Court on 7 September.

World.title: Latest report: SAFA make decision on Pitso Mosimane
World.content:
Contractual talks between SAFA and Pitso Mosimane were concluded over the weekend. This is according to a report by SABC Sport‘s Velile Mnyandu

The development comes with Bafana Bafana already facing an important September international window. Their AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign begins against Guinea before a trip to Egypt to face Eritrea.

PITSO MOSIMANE FACES IMMEDIATE TEST

The coach will return for his second spell in charge of the national team. He previously coached Bafana Bafana between 2010 and 2012.



His expected appointment comes after Hugo Broos ended a successful five-year tenure. It included consecutive AFCON qualifications and a bronze medal at the 2023 tournament in Ivory Coast.

Broos also guided South Africa to the 2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage. It marked the first time Bafana Bafana reached the knockout phase of the competition.

The timing of Mosimane’s return means he could have little time to settle before facing two demanding AFCON qualifying fixtures.

Bafana are scheduled to host Guinea on Saturday, 26 September, although the venue has not yet been confirmed. Gauteng and North West are reportedly being considered, with proximity to OR Tambo International Airport important because the team is expected to travel to Egypt immediately after the match.

Three days later, on Wednesday, 30 September, Bafana Bafana will face Eritrea in Egypt. Eritrea are taking the fixture outside their country because they do not currently have a stadium that meets the required CAF and FIFA standards.

The Group D campaign also includes Kenya and Guinea, with Kenya already guaranteed a place at the AFCON tournament as one of the co-hosts. Only the group winner will qualify through the qualifying process.



For Mosimane, the trip to Egypt will bring back memories of one of the most successful periods of his coaching career. He spent almost three years with Al Ahly, winning two CAF Champions League titles and establishing himself as one of Africa’s most decorated coaches.

His return now gives the experienced coach an immediate opportunity to begin building his second Bafana Bafana era with qualification for the 2027 AFCON firmly in sight.

World.title: BREAKING: Pollard at 10 for Springboks, Kolbe ruled out
World.content:
For this Saturday’s Test in Cape Town, Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus has named a similar starting XV to the one that lined up against the All Blacks in Johannesburg last week.

The only changes see Siya Kolisi bracketed alongside Paul de Villiers at flanker, while Handre Pollard and Cobus Reinach will start as the halfback pairing, and Ethan Hooker takes over from Cheslin Kolbe on the wing after he picked up a niggle in the first Test.

Should Kolisi make it through training comfortably this week, he will replace Paul de Villiers, joining Du Toit and Jasper Wiese in the loose trio, while Hooker’s inclusion sees Kurt-Lee Arendse switch from the left to right wing in an exciting back three with Damian Willemse. Pieter-Steph du Toit retains the captaincy.



If Kolisi runs out at DHL Stadium, it will be the most experienced Springbok team ever to take the field, with a combined total of 1012 Test caps in the starting XV.

The switches on the bench sees the inclusion of 39-year-old Deon Fourie in a back-up front row with Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit, while Lood de Jager (lock) and Cameron Hanekom (loose forward) will join hybrid Andre Esterhuizen as the replacement forwards.

The two replacement backs, meanwhile, are scrumhalf Morne van den Berg and the versatile Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Saturday’s Test will kick off at 17:10.

Springbok utility forward Pieter-Steph du Toit will become the 11th player in Bok history to earn 100 Test caps, while he has actually been listed as captain in the team sheet due to the uncertainty over Kolisi.



SPRINGBOKS – 15 Damian Willemse, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse, 13 Jesse Kriel, 12 Damian de Allende, 11 Ethan Hooker, 10 Handrè Pollard, 9 Cobus Reinach, 8 Jasper Wiese, 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit (c), 6 Siya Kolisi/Paul de Villiers, 5 Ruan Nortjè, 4 Eben Etzebeth, 3 Wilco Louw, 2 Malcolm Marx, 1 Ox Nchè.

Subs: 16 Deon Fourie, 17 Gerhard Steenekamp, 18 Thomas du Toit, 19 Lood de Jager, 20 Andrè Esterhuizen, 21 Cameron Hanekom, 22 Mornè van den Berg, 23 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

Springbok record against New Zealand:

Played: 111, Won: 43, Lost: 64, Drawn: 4. Points for: 1 866; Points against: 2 302; Tries scored: 182; Tries conceded: 253. Win %: 37,7%.



Aiming to bounce back

All of the players in the matchday squad, with the exception of Fourie – who last wore the green and gold jersey in the 2023 Rugby World Cup Final – featured in the Boks’ last two Test matches, against Argentina and the All Blacks.

“Cheslin and Grant (Williams) suffered niggles last weekend, which ruled them out of contention for selection, while we have bracketed Siya alongside Paul to allow us time to monitor how Siya comes through training this week,” said Erasmus.

“The changes we made are in line with what we want to achieve on the field this week, and it is valuable that almost all of the players have been involved in the last two games, so they will be able to cope with the intensity and physicality of this match.”

World.title: ‘ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken’ - DA
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Democratic Alliance has slammed the ANC’s manifesto as "implausible".

The party says the ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken.

The ANC launched its manifesto at the weekend ahead of the 4 November Local Government Elections, promising to turn around municipalities.

But the DA says the manifesto asks South Africans to believe that the same party that has presided over the collapse of municipalities across the country will suddenly fix them again.

“These promises are implausible and lack all integrity,” DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said in a statement.

“The ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken."

“South Africans deserve a different future with local governments that work, and ultimately a DA-led national government that brings the same culture of accountability, competence and service to the whole country,” Hill-Lewis added.

READ | ANC launches election manifesto in Diepsloot

While admitting his party’s failures over the years, ANC president Cyril Ramaphosa promised South Africans that they will do better.

“There are municipalities, we must admit, that are in financial trouble. There are municipalities that have been weakened by poor leadership, political instability, corruption and the appointment of people who do not have the skills required for the work that they must perform.

“Now, as the ANC, we comrades accept responsibility both for the progress that has been made, but we also accept responsibility for the failures and shortcomings where we govern,” Ramaphosa said.

He added that if citizens vote for the party, work will begin immediately after election day.

But the DA maintains the ANC will not perform miracles in 100 days and fill every critical municipal vacancy within 120 days.

World.title: Shein grapples with EU backlash, but clients keep coming
World.content:
BEIJING - Shein's meteoric growth has made it a lightning rod for critics of ultrafast fashion in Europe, where officials are trying to rein in its operations in the name of social and environmental responsibility.

The probes, financial penalties and fierce debates have dampened but not fully curbed the enthusiasm of millions of clients in a key market for the China-founded online juggernaut.

The company's $1.7 billion stock market listing, announced on Monday, aims in particular to juice its international expansion.

- Short-lived Paris store -

Starting in 2012, Shein began online sales of its continually renewed stock of tops, dresses and other items, drastically undercutting the prices of its rivals -- to say nothing of traditional clothing stores.

Its European customer base rose to 156 million average monthly users by the end of last year, making Shein one of the continent's biggest e-commerce platforms alongside China's AliExpress (193 million users), and Amazon (around 180 million).

In November, the group made waves with its first-ever physical outlet, a dedicated space in the storied BHV department store in Paris.

Hundreds of customers lined up on its opening day, and dozens more people gathered to protest, requiring a heavy police presence to keep the tense situation from getting out of hand.

Demonstrators slammed what they called inhumane working conditions at Shein's suppliers, the environmental costs of selling clothes not made to last, and unfair competition against brick-and-mortar retailers struggling to stay open.

The company says it holds its suppliers to strict compliance standards and does not tolerate forced labour.

- Sex doll scandal -

It did not help that just a few days before the Paris opening, France's consumer protection agency said it had discovered childlike sex dolls for sale on Shein's platform.

Accusing the company of fostering child pornography, French officials asked the European Commission to open an inquiry under the bloc's wide-reaching Digital Services Act.

The EU investigation that opened in February 2026 targeted the sale of illicit goods "including child sexual abuse material" as well as what it alleged was Shein's "addictive design".

In June, French authorities imposed two fines on Shein totalling more than 22 million euros ($25 million), citing problems with product traceability, environmental labelling and delivery times.

The next month it secured an EU-wide halt on the sales of items with crocodile logos -- deemed a counterfeit of France's famed Lacoste brand of polo shirts.

Overall, Shein has paid over 210 million euros in various French fines over the years, and Italy has also imposed fines alleging misleading environmental claims.

In June, the BHV's new owners said they would part ways with Shein, calling the decision to welcome a physical outlet a "strategic error".

- Regulatory pushback -

Shein has called the penalties "disproportionate and discriminatory", while China's commerce ministry says they violate World Trade Organization rules.

That did not stop the European Union from imposing duties on the billions of small, inexpensive retail parcels entering the bloc each year -- most of them from Chinese e-commerce sites.

Since July, a duty of three euros per item applies to packages valued at less than 150 euros, similar to a move last year by US President Donald Trump's administration against products originating in China.

But the EU fee applies to the type of item imported, not the number. So a person buying five T-shirts pays just three euros, but someone buying a T-shirt, jeans and socks would pay nine euros.

Brussels says the duty helps compensate for overwhelmed customs authorities given the popularity of e-commerce, in particular for clothes and other items from China and elsewhere that do not comply with EU standards.

According to the head of the European Parliament's trade committee, Bernd Lange, the number of small parcels from abroad have more than quadrupled to 5.88 billion since 2022.

Starting in November, the EU will impose a still-undetermined handling fee on such parcels.

It is far from clear how effective the duties will be, especially as online giants like Shein could build warehouses in Europe to limit the impact.

After France imposed its own duty of two euros on such parcels this year -- before the EU system kicked in -- the customs office estimated it brought in around 2.3 million euros per month.

That was far below the 33 million euros per month the government had expected in the 2026 budget.

World.title: Cummins eyes ODI return ahead of 'big' SA Test series
World.content:
MACKAY - Skipper Pat Cummins said he "can't wait" to play in Australia's first Test series in South Africa since the infamous "Sandpapergate" affair and he intends to use one-day games beforehand to prepare.

The next assignment for Australia after drawing a two-Test series against Bangladesh are three ODIs in Zimbabwe and another three in South Africa in late September.

They then play Tests in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town in October.

Cummins indicated he could miss the Zimbabwe leg, but would make himself available for some of the South Africa white-ball games.

It is likely to be a similar scenario for fellow quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.

"I'm not sure I should say this, but I think the focus is on the Test series," said Cummins after their innings and 51-run thrashing of Bangladesh in Mackay on Sunday.

"So a lot of the white-ball (series), and how we play that, would be with an eye to the red ball.

"So I'd imagine it'd be one, two, probably a maximum of three games out of those six."

Cummins, who remains Australia's official ODI captain, has played just two from a possible 28 matches in the format since the 2023 World Cup.

Hazlewood told reporters in Mackay he too expected to play some of the 50-over series while Starc said he would "do what he's told".

All three have prioritised Tests over limited-overs cricket in recent years.

The Tests in South Africa will be Australia's first in the country since a 2018 ball-tampering scandal rocked the sport.

Steve Smith was banned for a year and sacked as captain after conspiring to alter the ball using sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town, while David Warner was suspended for 12 months.

Cummins called the series "big" with revenge on his mind after Australia lost the World Test Championship final to the Proteas at Lord's last year.

"We had a big series against them a couple of years ago in Australia (in 2022-23) and we probably exceeded expectations and played really well," said Cummins of their 2-0 series win.

"They got us back at Lord's last year and outplayed us. So it's going to be big in their home conditions and places we haven't played for quite a while.

"Even the difference between Durban to, say, Cape Town can be quite different styles of pitches.

"That's why I love playing Test cricket. It's all different conditions, different opponents, different parts of the world. Can't wait."

Only Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood, Smith, Nathan Lyon, and Matt Renshaw have played Test cricket in South Africa.

Opener Renshaw is likely to hold his place despite a tepid return in Mackay after three years away, with the big question whether Marnus Labuschagne should be on the plane.

The number three made just 36 runs in three knocks against Bangladesh and has not scored a century since 2023.

"I did say a couple of days ago -– and I think it still stands -– that he's been batting fantastically well off the field," said Cummins. "But it doesn't mean much. You've got to convert that into runs out there."

World.title: Tourism boom pushes limits of Athens air traffic control
World.content:
ATHENS - Green arrows representing tourist-laden jets pile up on the screens of the Athens air traffic controllers, a puzzle to solve at the height of tourist season.

"Look at this sky, it's crazy, there's no room for any more planes!" exclaimed Olga Toki, vice-president of the Association of Air Traffic Controllers of Greece.

There is no doubt that this is a busy summer for the overworked air traffic controllers.

In the low season, Greece's airports typically handle between 1,000 and 1,500 flights per day, according to the Greek Civil Aviation Authority. In the first week in July, by contrast, they handled an average of 2,700 flights per day.

Overall traffic in southeast Europe, which includes Greek airspace, has risen about 40 percent from 2019, according to Eurocontrol, the air navigation safety organisation.

That underlined a boom in tourist arrivals in Greece, which last year were 23 percent higher than the 2019 pre-Covid peak, at 38 million, in a country of around 10 million people.

Even before the summer rush, nerves were on edge; a January 4 breakdown in the communication system linking air traffic controllers and aircraft had laid bare a glaring weakness.

Controllers could see the planes on their screens but were unable to hear or talk with the pilots. The authorities had to close Greek airspace for hours, causing chaos, with a chain of cancellations and diversions to neighbouring countries.

- Short-staffed -

The crisis was the catalyst for the announcement of a renovation programme costing around 300 million euros ($350 million), including the installation of new digital communication systems.

The systems began to be installed in mid-August. The entire project -- which includes replacing ageing radar -- is supposed to be completed by 2028.

World.title: In US, rare earths extracted from coal mine wastewater
World.content:
WASHINGTON - In the Appalachian region stretching through the US state of West Virginia, the reddish water flowing out of retired coal mines is acidic, full of heavy metals and toxic for the environment.

But that water is also rich in rare earths, the highly coveted minerals needed for many high-tech products such as smartphones and the clean energy industry that have become a focus of geopolitical competition.

Some believe this acid mine drainage could help the United States improve its position in the increasingly vital rare earths market.

The minerals are used to manufacture powerful magnets used in electric vehicles and wind turbines, but also in drones and fighter jets.

The limited resource is one of the key challenges in the rivalry between the United States and China, which currently dominates the market, both in terms of production and refining.

Washington sees Beijing's near-monopoly as a strategic threat and wants to reduce its dependence on China by finding new producers to develop a domestic supply chain.

So far, the US only has one rare earths mine, in Mountain Pass, California, which primarily yields so-called "light" elements.

"Heavy" rare earths, which are more difficult to mine and more highly desirable, are largely sourced outside the United States.

"The US has started to make inroads on the midstream and downstream portions, but what we haven't had domestically is the front-end feedstock," said Mark Gavin, the vice provost of West Virginia University (WVU).

World.title: AVBOB FCJ Excellence Award winners for 2025 announced
World.content:
[SPONSORED] The AVBOB FCJ Excellence Awards, hosted by the Forum of Community Journalists NPC (FCJ) and sponsored by AVBOB, is a well-known event in the media industry.

The competition received just over 600 entries this year, with participants showcasing exemplary work across 17 categories. Front pages (76 entries), back pages (49), free newspaper of the year (45), hard news/investigative reporting (79) and compelling human-interest reportage (64) dominated the field.

Local government reporting/municipal news was reintroduced after an absence of many years, with Yaseen Gaffar of DistrictMail & Helderberg Gazette taking the honours. A completely new category — story of the year — was also introduced, awarded to Yaseen Bardien and Mahmood Sanglay of Muslim Views.

The dedication and talent displayed by community journalists in various writing and photography categories underscore the vibrancy and diversity of community journalism in South Africa.

The adjudication process was overseen by Dr André Gouws from Akademia. “This year's competition reflects a healthy and evolving community newspaper sector. The judging panel congratulates all entrants and hopes that the feedback they will receive will encourage even greater excellence in the years ahead,” Gouws said.

Through AVBOB's financial investment in the FCJ and the community media industry, along with ongoing support from Caxton, Novus Community Media and the competition's new partner, Stellenbosch University, the FCJ was able to further enrich its offering and support to community journalists.

“Strong communities are built on accountability, trust and access to reliable information. They depend on you to remain informed about issues that affect their daily lives and on having their voices represented in public conversations,” said Eugene Strauss, AVBOB CEO.

“At AVBOB, our covenant with society is rooted in a simple belief: institutions should not only serve society, but they should also help strengthen it. The same principle guides our support for community journalism,” Strauss added.

Winners were announced at a gala prize-giving dinner at The Capital Menlyn Maine in Pretoria on 21 August. Top honours for Journalist of the Year went to Michelle Pienaar of George Herald. Highvelder's Wayne van der Walt took the Photographer of the Year title for an unprecedented fourth consecutive year, and this year's recipient of the Alet Roux Trophy for Most Promising Journalist was Dillon Pillay of Southlands SUN.

The FCJ also hosted its national seminar prior to the gala dinner. The seminar focused on the community journalist's role in the upcoming municipal elections, with industry leaders and experts sharing their knowledge with attendees.

The panel of judges, led by Gouws, comprised seasoned industry professionals and academics. They are Alé Steyn, Chantel Erfort Manuel, Elaine Krige, Elsabé Retief, Fanie Heyns, Heindrich Wyngaard, Jóhann Thormählen, Kyle Cowan, Marenet Jordaan,

Marietjie Gericke, Marlene Malan, Mercy Kannemeyer, Mlungisi Louw, Owen Kock, Pieter Delport, Sibongile Maputi, Simonéh de Bruin, Virginia Keppler-Young, Willem Kempen, Yolanda van der Stoep and Zenande Maqubela.

World.title: 'Cat' Matlala's testimony delayed: Here's why
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged underworld figure Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala’s legal team says difficulties consulting with him at Kgosi Mampuru II Prison have contributed to delays in filing a late affidavit before the Madlanga Commission.

Advocate Fatima Missi, who represents Matlala, told the commission that the legal team has had to navigate a number of challenges to consult with her client and properly prepare his case.

Missi asked the commission to take these circumstances into account and allow Matlala’s legal team an opportunity to file its replying affidavit, heads of argument and an application for condonation for the late filing.

“We beg this Commission humbly to consider all the elements that we consistently have to do to try and ensure that we represent Mr Matlala,” Missi said.

However, commission chairperson Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga was not persuaded that Matlala’s involvement was necessary to deal with the issues causing the delay.

World.title: Infrastructure development takes centre stage at Cape Town symposium
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Infrastructure development in South Africa is a hot topic in Cape Town as the Sustainable Infrastructure Development Symposium gets underway.

Key discussion points will be how to develop economic growth through Ports, Aviation and Logistics Corridors.

The symposium kicked off with a site visit to the Cape Flats Managed Aquifer Recharge project.

Delegates are meeting over the next two days to find ways to eradicate stumbling blocks hampering the maintenance and growth of infrastructure.

Ministers and Mayors from other African countries joined the delegation that visited the Cape Flats Managed Aquifer Recharge project in Cape Town's Pelican Park.

Once completed, the more than R1.3-billion project will play a crucial role in augmenting the Cape Flats Aquifer through the managed injection of treated wastewater.

Infrastructure development at municipal level as well as upgrading the country's roads, railways and ports also takes top priority.

A major focus is on how government manages its infrastructure portfolio. Officials say the state cannot spend billions on private leases while its own buildings stand vacant.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: Gachagua: Opposition does not need Uhuru's money to send Ruto home
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu on August 16, 2026. [Kimaku Chege, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims that former President Uhuru Kenyatta is financing opposition activities against President William Ruto.

Addressing the allegations that Kenyatta was financing opposition campaigns, Gachagua insisted that the movement did not require money from the former President.

Gachagua says the movement seeking political change is driven by Kenyans and does not depend on financial sponsorship.

“Nasikia kwamba Uhuru is sponsoring us to campaign against you. Uhuru is not sponsoring us, we don't need any sponsorship, this is a mass movement for change which does not need funding,” he said.

He was speaking on Sunday, August 16, 2026, during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu County.

Gachagua further said the opposition had sufficient public support to challenge the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election, insisting that Kenyans themselves were the driving force behind calls for a change of government.

He added that the public itself would determine the political fate of the Ruto administration.

“We don't need money but Kenyans will send you home,” Gachagua said.

The comments come against the backdrop of renewed debate over political alliances and the role of former leaders in Kenya's 2027 succession politics. Kenyatta, who served as President from 2013 to 2022, has largely remained outside the day-to-day administration of government since handing over power to Ruto.

Gachagua also defended Kenyatta against what he described as attempts to drag the former President into the current political contest.

“Uhuru Kenyatta asiguzwe na mtu yeyote. Alindwe na atetewe na apatiwe amani. Uhuru alifanya kazi yake na akastaafu,” Gachagua said.

The former Deputy President said Kenyatta should not be treated as a political candidate or blamed for the activities of opposition politicians.

“Nimemwambia Ruto unauliza Uhuru nini na sio candidate in the next election. I am your main opponent,” Gachagua said.

His remarks came amid an increasingly heated political contest over the direction of the country ahead of the 2027 elections.

Ruto and his administration have faced criticism from opposition figures over the economy, cost of living and the government's record since taking office.

Gachagua's comments also followed his broader criticism of the government's economic record.

Earlier in the church address, he challenged Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi's argument that increased consumption of soft drinks could indicate improved household incomes.

Gachagua argued that ordinary Kenyans were experiencing economic difficulties despite government claims of improved economic indicators. He said declining church offerings would provide a more meaningful indication of household financial wellbeing.

“If you want to know if the economy is doing well, ask the pastor about the offering; it will tell you how the economy is moving,” he said.

He further urged Kenyans to prepare for political change in 2027, arguing that the country required new leadership.

“Let us get in line. We look for new leadership that will fix our country and return it to where Uhuru Kenyatta left us,” Gachagua said

World.title: FM, Finance Minister discuss boosting economic diplomacy
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty received Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk on Sunday, August 23, 2026, to discuss ways to enhance coordination and integration with state institutions and support Egypt’s economic and financial efforts through Egyptian diplomatic missions abroad in line with the state’s economic priorities.

Kouchouk also held a meeting with Egyptian ambassadors appointed to head diplomatic missions abroad to review the state’s economic and financial policy priorities, as well as highlight economic reform efforts and opportunities for enhancing cooperation and investment.

The meeting also discussed ways for Egyptian embassies to support efforts to promote the Egyptian economy, highlight investment and trade opportunities, and strengthen engagement with international financial institutions and business communities in host countries.

The efforts are aimed at strengthening the role of economic diplomacy, supporting the state’s efforts to attract investment and increase exports, and opening new markets for Egyptian products.

World.title: FM, Sudanese finance minister discuss reconstruction efforts
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty held talks on Sunday, August 23, 2026, with Sudanese Finance and Economic Planning Minister Gibril Ibrahim to discuss ways aimed at to expanding economic cooperation and supporting reconstruction efforts in Sudan.

The Ministers discussed cooperation between Egyptian and Sudanese institutions on financial policies, as well as measures to increase trade and investment and remove obstacles affecting bilateral commerce.

Talks also addressed cooperation on rehabilitating Sudan’s infrastructure, particularly roads and transport, as well as the medical and pharmaceutical sectors.

Abdelatty said that Egypt’s experience and capabilities in these fields could contribute to Sudan’s early recovery and reconstruction.

The Egyptian Foreign Minister also briefed Ibrahim on preparations for the first Africa Business Summit, to be held as part of the Alamein Forum for Business in Africa.

He encouraged Sudanese participation, saying the event could provide opportunities for greater economic and investment cooperation between the two countries.

The meeting also addressed developments in Sudan. Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s support for Sudan’s unity, sovereignty, territorial integrity and national institutions, while rejecting attempts to divide the country or establish parallel entities.

He called for a Sudanese-led political settlement that preserves the country’s resources and meets the Sudanese people’s aspirations for security and stability.

World.title: Egypt Finance Minister: Global investors regain confidence in economy
World.content:
Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk on Sunday, August 23, 2026, said global investors have renewed their confidence in Egypt’s economic trajectory, with investment risk assessments falling to their lowest level since 2014.

“Our economy has started to improve, while the private sector is growing and accounts for 60% of investments,” Kouchouk said at a meeting with Egyptian diplomats abroad.

He said strong activity in industry, telecommunications, information technology and tourism was supporting economic growth, while the government was working to stimulate investment, reduce debt and expand tax and customs incentives.

Kouchouk said Egypt was seeking to expand its productive, industrial and export base to improve the economy’s competitiveness and attract more investment.

“Global investors have renewed their confidence in Egypt’s economic trajectory, and we look to your efforts to drive investment inflows,” he said.

He added that Egypt has significant potential to increase services exports, while its young workforce is capable of competing in global markets.

World.title: US, Egypt discuss port infrastructure, maritime innovation
World.content:
US and Egyptian officials opened the US-Egypt Ports Infrastructure and Maritime Innovation Forum in New Cairo on Sunday, August 23, 2026, to discuss port development, maritime technology, artificial intelligence and investment opportunities.

US Embassy Chargé d’Affaires Robert Silverman and US Deputy Secretary of Commerce Mark Mitchell opened the forum, while Egypt’s Transport Minister Kamel el Wazir addressed the event.

The US Embassy said that American companies presented advanced technologies that could support Egypt’s port infrastructure and artificial intelligence sectors while creating new opportunities for trade and investment between the two countries.

Silverman said the United States supports Egypt’s efforts to build world-class maritime infrastructure and that American companies are well positioned to compete for new projects and expand bilateral commercial ties.

Mitchell said Egypt occupies an important position in global trade and technology. He said US-Egypt cooperation could support the modernization of maritime transport, the development of the Suez Canal corridor, and the deployment of advanced US artificial intelligence and data infrastructure technologies.

The forum also connected American companies with opportunities in Egypt’s maritime, logistics, data and cloud computing sectors.

Egyptian participants included Suez Canal Economic Zone Chairman Mostafa Sheikhon, North Sinai Governor Khaled Megawer and Deputy Transport Minister for Maritime Transport Nihad Shahin.

The US is seeking to expand bilateral trade and private-sector investment through cooperation with Egypt on maritime infrastructure and technology.

World.title: US Army attack helicopters crashing at historically high rate amid mechanical issues
World.content:
The US Army’s Apache helicopters are crashing at a historically high rate amid a widespread problem with the model’s transmission, according to a CNN analysis of military accident data.

The helicopter type has experienced five major crashes since October, and a deadly mishap earlier this month in Texas killed two soldiers, sparked a wildfire and led the Army to temporarily bar Apache pilots from conducting routine training flights. With that crash, fiscal year 2026 is on pace to be the second worst for Apache flight accidents since a new model of the AH-64 was rolled out in 2011.

The Army announced that the pause in training flights, which exempted units deployed to the Middle East, ended Wednesday.

This year’s rate of major Apache crashes — known as Class A mishaps in Army parlance, meant to represent any accident that kills or permanently disables a person or results in the loss of an aircraft or $2.5 million in damage — surpasses typical years and rivals that of the service’s most severe rate in the 2024 fiscal year, according to CNN’s review of data. The accident rate is based on the number of incidents compared to the total hours the aircraft spent flying, calculated using data that has been publicly released and flight hour estimates for the current year provided to CNN by the Army.

In Fiscal year 2024 there were nine major Apache crashes amid a spike in accidents across all Army helicopter models. Army leaders ordered a special safety training initiative that year and attributed the accidents to human errors stemming from decreased experience among its pilots and an increase in training intensity and complexity after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine inspired a new focus on preparing for major conflicts.

But the causes of this year’s spike are murkier. The July issue of an official Army flight safety newsletter said that just over half of this year’s Apache accidents, including more minor incidents, are primarily attributable to human error. It’s unclear how many of the most-severe crashes are due to equipment failures, but the magazine said that “a catastrophic transmission failure was noted in one Class A mishap.”

Smoke can be seein rising from debris at the scene of a military helicopter crash near Salado, Texas, on Wednesday, August 12. Cliff Coleman/Bell County Sheriff’s Office

CNN estimated this year’s major Apache crash rate to be approximately 6.24 per every 100,000 flying hours. Thus far in fiscal year 2026, five Class A flight mishaps involving the attack helicopter have occurred. The Apache, through August 15, had flown approximately 80,171 hours. That number combines 42,971 hours through March 31 that were listed in the internal Army safety newsletter and an estimate provided to CNN by an Army safety spokesperson that pilots had logged approximately 37,200 additional flight hours through August 15.

Fiscal year 2024, by comparison, had a rate of 7.02 major crashes per 100,000 hours for the aircraft.

The E-model Apache, introduced in 2011, has faced significant problems this year with its transmission that could knock out the aircraft’s tail rotor, electrical power and hydraulics, according to a pair of internal safety messages obtained by CNN. The loss of those systems can put a helicopter into a sudden spin and potentially knock out its flight controls. As of mid-July, the cause of the problems remained “under investigation,” according to a safety message released at the time.

Army spokesperson Maj. Montrell Russell declined to answer questions regarding the transmission investigation or disclose any “preliminary findings” regarding the causes of this month’s deadly Texas crash at Fort Hood.

“We express our deep sadness over the loss of the two Soldiers near Fort Hood,” Russell said in a statement to CNN.

He said that “special controls and release protections” prevent the service from providing detailed “technical aviation information,” to include how many of this year’s crashes are related to the helicopters’ transmission.

The initial April safety message, first reported by trade publication Defense One, identified 70 potentially faulty transmissions and ordered all units to stop flying affected Apaches pending repair. A follow-up message sent in mid-July said the root cause remains “under investigation” and added 10 more suspect transmissions to the no-fly list.

The two safety messages combined to impact roughly a tenth of the Army’s attack helicopter fleet. In early June, an Army official told CNN that all affected Apaches remained grounded, and the Army did not answer CNN’s questions about how many, if any, have returned to flight since then.

Meanwhile, the Apache’s transmission issues continue to be mentioned in Army flight documents. CNN obtained an August 14 internal Army order that formally cited the two transmission safety messages in its references for the service’s training flight pause after the Texas crash. Russell cautioned that “including these messages in safety reviews does not imply causation for any individual mishap.”

The Apache’s manufacturer, Boeing, has deployed teams to Army maintenance depots to assist with inspecting and fixing the transmissions, according to the Army order.

The Army and Boeing did not answer questions on how they identified the potentially faulty parts.

A Boeing spokesperson confirmed to CNN that the company is “supporting the U.S. Army’s investigation to ensure the operational readiness and safety of any affected aircraft,” but referred additional questions to the Army.

Davis Winkie’s work at CNN is supported by a partnership between Outrider Foundation and Journalism Funding Partners (JFP). CNN retains full editorial control of the reporting.

World.title: Trump is trying to tighten the screws on an Iran numb to economic pain
World.content:
Iran, already drained by years of sanctions and a brutal military onslaught from the United States and Israel, now faces another test as President Donald Trump moves to further tighten the economic screws on the Islamic Republic.

The US is preparing measures, to be revealed at a news conference later on Monday, of what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promises to be “the toughest sanctions in history” amid deadlock on talks to end the six-month war and as Iran continues inflicting global economic pain by disrupting shipping through the crucial Strait of Hormuz.

By the admission of its own top officials, Iranians are suffering.

“We are apologetic that these problems exist, as we find ourselves in a full-scale economic, military, and security war,” Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said, according to state media.

“As the government, we are seeking with all our being to steer inflation, public problems, people’s livelihoods, people’s jobs, people’s future, and people’s lives towards dignity and pride,” he added.

Videos on social media published last week showed empty markets in Tehran and Karaj, with sellers complaining that their fresh produce is not being bought. One resident of Tehran and another business owner told CNN that economic pressures have become “untenable.”

Not only is everything expensive, Nima, a 36-year-old resident of Tehran, told CNN, but some of the “important things needed we can’t even get, like certain medications.”

An owner of a small shop who chose to remain anonymous to speak freely about the economic conditions said he is barely making ends meet.

“We are running out of some of the foreign products like foreign shampoo and conditioner, toothpaste. We have limited stock and it’s now too expensive for most people, but even the Iranian-made products I’ve had to raise prices on,” he said.

‘Immediate Pain’

But even with fresh economic pressure, experts say that unless the Trump administration uncovers fresh methods to choke off Tehran’s revenue streams, Washington will once again face a regime long practiced in sanction evasion, resourceful at finding new ways to generate income, and betting on its ability to survive the US’ economic pressure.

Over decades of international pariahdom, the Islamic Republic was forced to develop sophisticated methods to mitigate the impact of Western sanctions, creating a decentralized network of front companies, brokers, exchange houses, and a shadow tanker fleet that uses ship-to-ship transfers, altered tracking data, and false documentation to move oil.

In 2024, $9 billion of Iranian shadow banking activity occurred through US correspondent accounts, the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network said, based on reporting from American financial institutions. Shell companies, including those in oil, shipping, and investment, facilitate billions of dollars in transactions through networks spanning the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, and Singapore, according to the Treasury Department.

Payments are often made in the Chinese yuan, through barter arrangements, or outside the dollar-based banking system, Umud Shokri, an energy strategist and senior visiting fellow at George Mason University told CNN.

The latest measures will “squash” the economy of “this murderous regime” and curtail Iran’s ability to “project power through their proxies” and its ability to pay the Iranian military, Bessent told CNBC in a recent interview.

But experts said that ordinary Iranians will most likely bear the brunt of the new sanctions.

The US is preparing to place the “toughest sanctions in history” on Iran. Majid Asgaripour/WANA News Agency/Reuters

“Ordinary Iranians will experience the most immediate pain, and further sanctions would weaken the rial, increase inflation, raise the cost of imported goods and industrial inputs, and reduce household purchasing power,” Shokri said.

Even if public and military spending, as well as regional allies, suffer under the new strict economic sanctions, it will be the wage earners, pensioners, small businesses, and lower-income families that would be particularly vulnerable, he added.

The “politically connected” institutions and intermediaries would be partially “insulated” as they continue profiting from smuggling, currency manipulation, and control over scarce imports, Shokri said.

Experts say that for the US to effectively target Iran’s economy, it will need to target major Chinese buyers of Iranian oil, independent refineries, and banks processing Iranian revenue, but that could also risk retaliation from Beijing against Washington.

In a Truth Social post Trump threatened other countries with “tremendous economic consequences” if they provide any type of “lifeline” to Iran, without naming specific nations.

Washington would have to target the central nodes of Iran’s trade rather than continue sanctioning replaceable vessels and shell companies,” Shokri said, adding that the US could aim to sanction tanker managers, insurers, ports, ship-to-ship transfer providers while adding more restrictions on technology that could end up with dual-use military functions.

‘Weather The Storm’

Even though the Iranian government has expanded domestic production while operating its sophisticated network of front companies to procure essential goods, largely from China, the Islamic Republic has demonstrated that it can transfer the sanctions burden onto an already struggling population while protecting the institutions essential for the regime’s survival.

Weeks before the war, Iranians took to the streets to protest rising costs and inflation.

Back in January, civilians flooded the streets in Tehran, and other Iranian cities, to protest soaring inflation and the collapse of the Iranian currency, while expanding into demands for political change. Stringer/Getty Images

Yet after initially acknowledging the economic struggle, the government once again accused the protesters of being foreign agents before unleashing one of the worst crackdowns in the Islamic Republic’s history.

For now, the Iranian regime is using the war to justify poor economic conditions and a once struggling government has been given an excuse to its exhausted population, while it is arguably Trump who faces greater political pressure from US consumers angry at gas prices ahead of midterms.

“They are willing to weather the storm, and they are willing to go through the pain,” Dina Esfandiary, Middle East geoeconomics lead at Bloomberg Economics told CNN. “None of the measures that President Trump is contemplating are going to make Iran capitulate.”

What is required, Esfandiary says, is “diplomacy and carrots” with Iran, which “of course is not at all being contemplated.”

For now, Neda, a 34-year-old Tehran resident struggling with kidney disease and needing medication, is holding her breath as she is once again forced to buy only half of her monthly dose.

“I have so much anxiety all the time because without the medication I won’t really survive,” she said. “You know, I went to the doctor the other day and the nurse said people weren’t even able to show up to their appointments for dialysis.”

“The people receiving chemotherapy stopped going because they just cannot afford it anymore.”

World.title: Britain’s giving Ukraine access to secret missile technology. Will it make a difference?
World.content:
Britain will allow the release of classified technology so that a British/French-designed cruise missile can be manufactured in Ukraine, a boost for Kyiv in its efforts to bring more firepower to bear hundreds of kilometers into Russia.

Paris and Kyiv want to set up a Ukrainian production line for the SCALP air-launched cruise missile, known as the Storm Shadow in the United Kingdom, by the end of the year. The declassification of information on British-made components of the missiles, announced Monday, is a key step towards that goal.

Made by European arms manufacturer MBDA, SCALP is a conventionally armed, long-range, deep-strike weapon, of which Ukraine has used imported versions with success against hardened targets, including in November 2024, when they were fired at targets inside Russia for the first time.

Powered by a turbojet engine, it has a maximum range of 550 kilometers (342 miles) and can carry a 400-kilogram (880 pounds) high-explosive penetrating warhead, according to the Missile Threat project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)

Once launched, the missile uses a combination of internal, global positioning and terrain reference navigation coupled with “infrared seeker and automatic target recognition algorithms” to achieve a high degree of accuracy in all weather conditions, according to the CSIS.

A Storm Shadow low-observable, long-range air-launched cruise missile is displayed at the MBDA chalet at Farnborough International Exhibition Centre on July 22, 2026, in Farnborough, England. Carl Court/Getty Images

The SCALP is fired from Ukraine’s Su-24 or Mirage 2000 fighter jets and attempts to avoid air defenses by hugging the terrain during flight.

Its use for Ukraine will be in striking buried military targets, like command bunkers, something more challenging for the lighter weight drones Kyiv has been using to hit more exposed targets like oil refineries or warehouses.

Britain and France have not announced how many SCALP/Storm Shadow missiles have been supplied to Ukraine to date, but in 2025 manufacturer MBDA reactivated production lines that had been shuttered for 15 years.

“Supplied to Ukraine, the Franco-British SCALP/Storm Shadow missile has demonstrated its effectiveness in modern high-intensity combat, in decisive situations,” French Defense Minister Sébastien Lecornu said at the time.

Even with the UK announcement, it could take several years for production to scale up, but British Prime Minister Andy Burnham says London is backing Kyiv for the long haul.

“The Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes,” Burnham said in a press release Monday announcing that the UK would release its missile technology.

“Ukraine’s security is our security,” said the prime minister, who arrived in Kyiv on Monday for Ukraine’s independence day, in his first overseas trip since taking office on July 20.

While there, Burnham will co-chair a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, a 34-nation international alliance formed last year by Britain and France to support Ukraine in the war as US aid waned under the Trump administration.

Interceptor struggle

What the SCALP can’t address is Ukraine’s shortage of defensive missiles, like the US-designed Patriot system, a vulnerability exposed with devastating consequences in recent weeks as Russia has launched large waves of its own missiles and drones in attacks that have killed dozens of Ukrainians.

CNN visited a Patriot battery in Ukraine earlier this month and was told that it had not been fired in weeks because no interceptors were available.

Ukraine has asked for permission to manufacture the Patriot interceptors in the country, an idea US President Donald Trump initially supported in early July but later backtracked on.

The Trump administration has also rebuffed Ukrainian attempts to acquire long-range US Tomahawk cruise missiles, stocks of which have been taxed by the war in Iran.

Ukraine’s domestic missile production has not stood still, however.

FP-5 Flamingo, Ukrainian ground-launched cruise missile developed by defence firm Fire Point in Kyiv, on August 22, 2026. Thomas Trutschel/dpa/AP

Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point has developed the FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile.

With a range of 3,000 kilometers, it can strike deep inside Russia, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said earlier this month it was used to hit a key Russian rocket electronics facility some 900 kilometers from Ukraine’s border.

The Ukrainian leader said the Flamingo made its combat debut in 2025, and open-source intelligence reports indicate its use has been on the increase this year.

Fire Point has also developed long-range drones to go along with shorter range ballistic missiles.

Kyiv’s use of longer-range weapons has turned Russia’s sprawling land mass, once considered a military advantage, into a problem for Moscow as it struggles to allocate limited defensive weaponry to the increasing number of targets within Ukraine’s range, Peter Dickinson, editor of the Atlantic Council’s Ukraine Alert blog, wrote earlier this month.

“A long line of would-be conquerors have invaded Russia only for their armies to swallowed up by the vastness of the country. Ukraine is now attempting to turn this military logic on its head with a strategic bombing campaign that aims to exploit Russia’s immensity and transform it from a key strength into a fatal weakness,” Dickinson wrote.

World.title: Ships violating Hormuz transit rules could be seized, Iran warns
World.content:
Iran warned on Sunday that vessels accused of violating its transit rules in the Strait of Hormuz could face penalties including detention or confiscation, signaling potential risks for shipping through one of the world’s most strategically important waterways.

In a series of posts on X, Iran’s state-controlled Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) said vessels that violate what it described as Iranian arrangements governing transit through the Strait of Hormuz could face “fines, seizure, or confiscation” during future passages.

The authority urged cargo owners shipping to or from the Persian Gulf to review what it called a “Non-Compliant Vessels” list before chartering ships in order to avoid potential issues.
