A group of Polish civil society organisations has urged a former government minister to withdraw his candidacy to become a Constitutional Tribunal (TK) judge, saying his close ties to the prime minister could undermine confidence in the court’s independence. In a joint statement, the nine organisations say that restoring the legitimacy of the court, which has been in crisis since 2015 following illegitimate judicial appointments made by the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, requires not only addressing legal irregularities but also rebuilding public trust. “The existence of the Constitutional Tribunal as an organ of judicial power only makes sense if it is an independent arbiter,” they say. 🔴Wspólnie z innymi organizacjami apelujemy do dr. M. Berka o rezygnację z kandydowania do TK, a do Sejmu o wybór osoby niezależnej politycznie. Droga do praworządności to nie „odbijanie” Trybunału, ale odbudowa jego autorytetu. Przeczytajcie nasz apel, link w komentarzu ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/LPlbk39lNr — Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka (@hfhrpl) August 20, 2026 The appeal follows Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s announcement that Maciej Berek, who until recently served as a government minister and whom Tusk has described as his “right-hand man”, would be put forward as a candidate for the Constitutional Tribunal. The choice has drawn particular attention because Tusk came to power promising to “depoliticise” the court after the previous PiS government appointed former politicians as judges. “Regardless of the extent to which the tribunal has become politicised, the way to reform this institution cannot be for it to be ‘recaptured’ or ‘taken over’ by another ruling majority,” the NGOs write in the statement. The organisations, including the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights, the Institute of Public Affairs and the Stefan Batory Foundation, say Berek’s close ties to the current political leadership could cause his appointment to be perceived as political, regardless of his legal qualifications or personal integrity. “Not only must courts and tribunals operate independently and impartially, but citizens must also recognise and have confidence in that independence and impartiality. This is not possible when judges are appointed whose links to the government are immediately apparent,” the organisations add. “We therefore call on Dr Maciej Berek to withdraw his candidacy in the interests of the independence of the constitutional judiciary.” The proportion of Poles who negatively assess the justice system has increased under the current government, despite its promises to restore the rule of law. State pollster @CBOS_Info found 61% now hold a negative view, up from 55% in 2022 and 51% in 2017 https://t.co/P3fbTTbS5C — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 12, 2026 The organisations also argue that Berek’s nomination goes against a principle that the current ruling coalition sought to introduce: that anyone who has held political office within the previous four years should be barred from appointment to the tribunal. Berek was a government minister until last week. The coalition’s proposal was included in a bill approved by parliament in 2024. However, the Constitutional Tribunal itself later ruled the provision unconstitutional after former President Andrzej Duda, an ally of PiS, referred the legislation for review. “Although this law has not come into force, it would be reasonable for the Sejm to adhere to the standard it has adopted,” they said, referring to the lower chamber of the parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 However, the selection of Berek, whose candidacy was put forward by MPs from Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO), has exposed divisions within the ruling coalition, which ranges from centre-right to left. “We were supposed to be different from PiS; we were supposed to do things differently, not exactly the same way,” Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, told Polsat News. Paweł Śliz, leader of the centre-right Poland 2050’s (Polska 2050) caucus, said Berek would make an excellent Constitutional Tribunal judge were it not for his recent role as a government minister. “I consider him an excellent, outstanding professional; I value his experience and expertise. However, my position on this matter is unequivocal. I will not compromise my principles,” he told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The chief justice of the constitutional court has refused to accept four new judges appointed by parliament but whom the opposition-aligned president has refused to swear in. The decision deepens an unprecedented standoff over Poland's top court https://t.co/B02DKA3uBL — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 9, 2026 Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition opposing Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. Last week, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Presidential spokesman Rafał Leśkiewicz told PAP on Thursday that “there are serious doubts” about Berek’s formal qualifications to become a Constitutional Tribunal judge. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland summons Israeli ambassador over discontinued investigation into killing of Gaza aid workers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has summoned Israel’s ambassador to express its “great disappointment” that the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) have discontinued an investigation into the strikes on an aid convoy in Gaza in 2024 that killed seven humanitarian workers, including a Pole, Damian Soból. “Partnership requires mutual respect,” declared foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, as well as the failure of accountability for [the] IDF’s excessive use of force[,] are undermining public support in even pro-Israel nations.” Partnership requires mutual respect. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, as well as the failure of accountability for IDF’s excessive use of force are undermining public support in even pro-Israel nations. https://t.co/9H0nhiDE4H — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) August 20, 2026 The incident in question took place in April 2024, when Israeli drones struck a convoy delivering humanitarian aid from World Central Kitchen (WCK), a major international food relief NGO. The attack killed seven aid workers, including Soból. The incident caused outrage in Poland, whose government demanded that Israel fully explain the circumstances. The IDF expressed “sincere sorrow” over the deaths and pledged to carry out a “thorough and transparent” investigation. On Wednesday this week, the IDF announced that it had closed the case after determining “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct that would justify the opening of a criminal investigation or the taking of additional measures against any of those involved in the incident”. The IDF said that its troops had identified a gunman on one of the trucks in the convoy. It also claimed that WCK had hired an armed security force to protect the convoy without coordinating that with IDF authorities and that the convoy deviated from the route previously agreed with the IDF. However, the IDF also acknowledged that it had mistakenly identified several individuals as being armed. It added that attempts to contact WCK representatives over a half-hour period while the convoy was on the move were unsuccessful. The IDF noted that, after the incident, two military officers were removed from their positions while three others were reprimanded. But it found that there was no basis for any further action. ⚖️ IDF prosecution rules on five FFAM cases: The IDF says its General Staff Fact-Finding and Assessment Mechanism has completed reviews of approximately 150 exceptional wartime incidents since the beginning of the war and transferred them to the Military Prosecution. Decisions… pic.twitter.com/H5g4qOu5e2 — Israel Realtime (@IsraelRealtime) August 19, 2026 On Thursday, Poland’s foreign ministry issued a statement saying that it was “greatly disappointed to receive the information provided about the discontinuation of the proceedings by the Israeli military authorities”. It announced that it had summoned the Israeli ambassador in order to “communicate a critical assessment of the actions taken to date to clarify the causes and course of the tragedy”. It also noted that Polish prosecutors are still conducting their own investigation and that the foreign ministry had informed the Israeli ambassador that they “expect the Israeli side will provide the relevant Polish authorities with all necessary explanations and materials requested”. “The circumstances of the tragedy should be fully investigated and [we] do not accept that the perpetrators are avoiding legal and moral responsibility,” concluded the ministry, adding that “the families deserve adequate compensation”. We strongly condemn the Israeli military prosecutor’s account of the deaths of our seven colleagues on April 1, 2024. And we fundamentally disagree with their decision about criminal investigations into the IDF airstrikes that killed our team. Read our full statement here:… — World Central Kitchen (@WCKitchen) August 19, 2026 The IDF’s findings were also condemned by WCK itself, which called them “inconsistent with the full truth and deeply offensive”. It added that, “at the time of the lethal attacks, the IDF knew that our team in Gaza was unarmed and posing a threat to nobody”. The NGO repeated its demand for an independent investigation into the incident, “because the IDF cannot credibly investigate its own conduct”. On Friday, the UK, Canada and Australia, whose citizens were also killed in the strike, issued a joint statement calling the IDF’s decision to drop the investigation “shameful” and another example of the lack of accountability for incidents in Gaza. Joint statement from the foreign ministries of Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom on Israel closing the investigation into strikes on the World Central Kitchen convoy in Gaza on 1 April 2024 ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/V3CZe286tN — Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (@FCDOGovUK) August 21, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: New official tasked with promoting Poland criticised over error-strewn, potentially AI-generated report
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A government official appointed last month to promote Poland abroad has been hit by a wave of criticism after it emerged that she authored a report containing errors and which shows signs of being generated by artificial intelligence. The document mislocated major Polish cities and included bizarre language mixing Polish and English. It was marked as being part of a project financed by the sport and tourism ministry, though the ministry itself has denied that claim. The opposition has called on prosecutors to investigate potential misuse of public funds. ⁉️ Czy “Markę Polska” ma nam wygenerować sztuczna inteligencja? ⁉️ Czy Ministerstwo Sportu i Turystyki zapłaciło 200 000 złotych w ramach zadania publicznego za raport wygenerowany przez AI? ⁉️ Czy mogę prosić Panią Minister prof. @b_mroz_gorgon o odniesienie się do tych pytań… pic.twitter.com/lM2AY88oAh — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 The official in question, Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, is a professor at Wrocław University of Economics who was appointed three weeks ago as the government’s plenipotentiary for the promotion of Poland’s brand, a newly created position. She was presented at a press conference by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. However, this week, journalists and commentators began highlighting cases of bizarre errors from a report, titled A Self-Portrait of the Poles (Polaków Portret Własny), published last year with Mróz-Gorgoń named as the author, in her position as president of a think tank called Marka Polska (Brand Poland). The report contained some glaring errors, such as describing the city of Katowice as being in “north central” Poland (whereas in fact it is in the south) and Wrocław as being in the “northwest” (when it is actually in the southwest). Geografia – czyli gdzie leżą Katowice A propos miast jest też ciekawy chochlik lub też, jakby to powiedział ktoś złośliwy, klasyczna halucynacja AI. Przy opisie badań FGI miasta opisane są w następujący sposób (zdjęcie poniżej): 👉 Olsztyn – północny wschód 👉 Szczecin -… pic.twitter.com/SF6XBRfhWS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 Other parts contain strange analysis, such as noting that “after World War Two, Germany did not build its brand on the Holocaust”. The text also features unusual language, including random use of words in English, some of which have been turned into Polish ones. It is also regularly features words written in capital letters. One sentence, for example, refers to “INSTABILNOŚĆ” and “REZILIENCE”, presumably meaning “instability” and “resilience”, but neither of which is a Polish word. Another section claims that 95% of Poles born after 1990 are “polilingwalni” (an invented Polonised version of “polylingual”) who speak “angielski fluent”, a strange linguistic mix that means they speak English fluently. As well as the unusual language, the very claim that 95% of young Poles speak fluent English, as well as that many additionally speak Mandarin, has been questioned by many commentators. The report also contains bizarre errors in footnotes, which are numbered randomly (on one page, three consecutive footnotes are numbered “41, 517, 6”) and some of which are completely empty. A number of expert commentators have suggested that the text contains clear indications that it was generated by AI, a claim supported by evidence from programmes that check texts for AI-generated content. AI czy nie AI, oto jest pytanie Czytając ten raport kilkukrotnie, trudno mi było pozbyć się wrażenia, że nikt poważny, a szczególnie naukowiec z tytułem doktora habilitowanego, nie wygenerowałby dużych części raportu, za który zapłacili podatnicy, w jakimś LLM. No bo przecież… pic.twitter.com/jyTexgmeXS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 As well as bearing Mróz-Gorgoń’s name as author, the report also features on its front cover the logo of the sport and tourism ministry. The first page then includes a note saying that the project was carried out under an initiative co-financed by the ministry. After the issue began to draw attention and criticism on Thursday, the ministry issued a statement saying that the report was not ordered by them, was not part of any agreement to which the ministry was a party, and that no request to use the ministry’s logo was submitted. However, a social media post last November by deputy sport and tourism minister Piotr Borys shows him attending an event to present the report. He thanked Mróz-Gorgoń for coordinating the project and inviting him to the presentation. 📚W Akademii Leona Koźmińskiego odbyła się prezentacja raportu „Polaków Portret Własny”, przygotowanego Think Tank Marka Polska. To wyjątkowe wydarzenie poświęcone premierze badań dotyczących DNA Marki Polska. 🧬To pierwsze tak kompleksowe badanie, które pokazuje, kim jesteśmy… pic.twitter.com/jb7KdCJTPM — Piotr Borys (@piotr_borys) November 26, 2025 On Thursday evening, Mróz-Gorgoń herself addressed the controversy in an interview with Polsat News. She said that the report was actually a “work in progress” that “should never have appeared in the public space”. However, she still defended the work, saying that “the research was conducted reliably” and “the conclusions stand up to scrutiny”. But she also admitted that the writing of the report had been “aided by artificial intelligence”. In separate remarks to the Polish Press Agency (PAP), she said that “we used AI tools solely for transcription, summarising and text editing; they did not design research content or draw conclusions…We worked according to social science methodology, diligently and without cutting corners”. Meanwhile, on the Marka Polska think tank’s website, where the report had been published, it was initially changed on Thursday to being marked as a “draft version” before later being deleted entirely. Od raportu i deklaracji, że “praca badawcza [została] przeprowadzona zgodnie z zasadami nauk społecznych, rzetelnie i merytorycznie, w oparciu o opisaną metodologię”, przez “work in progress”, aż do “Oops! That page can’t be found”. Myślę, że to słowo “Oops!” jest najlepszym… pic.twitter.com/OaSTxkwKwa — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 On Thursday evening, the main opposition party, Law and Justice (PiS), announced that it was submitting requests to both prosecutors and the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (ABW) to investigate the use of around 200,000 zloty (€46,380) in state funds for the project that the report was allegedly part of. PiS has also called on Mróz-Gorgoń to resign or to be fired. On Friday, a deputy digital affairs minister, Dariusz Standerski, told the Wirtualna Polska news website that “all the circumstances surrounding the creation of this report will be clarified”. The controversy around Mróz-Gorgoń comes just days after the sport and tourism ministry was involved in the launch of a new advertising campaign designed to encourage tourism to Poland, but which many commentators have argued was poorly conceived and executed. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to attract tourists from Europe and the US. The first video, under the slogan "Poland. More than you expected", features footballer Robert Lewandowski, Hollywood star Jesse Eisenberg and supermodel Anja Rubik https://t.co/3jtqyUWQyy — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A speed of 253 km/h (157 mph) has been reached by a Pendolino train during tests carried out as part of preparations to speed up rail connections between Poland’s major cities from next year. The plans will see the journey time between Warsaw and Kraków cut to well under two hours. “Polish rail is accelerating – and 250 km/h is just the beginning,” declared the infrastructure minister Dariusz Klimczak, alluding to plans for Poland to later begin running trains at speeds of up to 320 km/h. Osiągnęliśmy 250 km/h na Centralnej Magistrali Kolejowej❗🚅 Dzisiejsze nocne testy systemu GSM-R na linii nr 4 zakończyły się pełnym sukcesem. Oznacza to, że pociągi pojadą tą trasą z rozkładową prędkością 250 km/h już w przyszłym roku❗ Pozwoli to znacznie skrócić czas… pic.twitter.com/ndXvePZP4t — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) August 18, 2026 The tests on the GSM-R data transmission system, a communication standard designed to be used at very high speeds, were carried out on Monday night. Trains will be able to run on Poland’s Central Main Line (CMK), which connects Warsaw with Kraków and Katowice, at a scheduled speed of 250 km/h from December 2027. That will cut the expected journey time between Warsaw and Kraków, the country’s two largest cities, by around half an hour to 1 hour and 52 minutes, reports rail news service Portal Kolejowy. It will also be possible to travel from the capital to Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, in around three hours. The fastest current connection is 3 hours and 30 minutes. Reaching the target speed of 250 km/h was a “very important moment for Polish rail”, said Maciej Kaczorek, a board member of PKP Polskie Linie Kolejowe, the state railway infrastructure manager, quoted by news website Money.pl. Poland has been operating Pendolinos, built by France’s Alstom, since 2014. The trains are designed to run at speeds of up to 250 km/h, but currently operate at a maximum of 200 km/h in Poland and run on routes connecting Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław and the Tricity area. However, this week’s tests are not a record rail speed in Poland. In 2013, a Pendolino reached 293 km/h during a test on the CMK a year before the high-speed trains commenced passenger services in the country. A Polish Pendolino high-speed train has begun running in the Czech Republic for the first time. The Prague-Bohumín service will run until June as part of a certification process that Polish operator PKP Intercity hopes will lead to a Warsaw-Prague route https://t.co/hmUNd7ft0E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 10, 2026 Speaking to Rynek Kolejowy, deputy infrastructure minister Piotr Malepszak said that it had “taken too long” for the network to be adapted to allow regular speeds of 250 km/h. The current government, which took power in December 2023, has much broader plans for expanding high-speed rail travel in Poland, including building 2,700 km of tracks capable of carrying trains at 320 km/h. In December 2025, state rail operator PKP Intercity launched a tender for 20 such trains. They would cut the journey time between Warsaw and Gdańsk, on Poland’s Baltic coast, to around 100 minutes – from 2 hours 25 minutes currently – by 2040, Malepszak told the Polish Press Agency in June. Passenger numbers on Poland’s rail network have been booming in recent years. In the first half of 2026, a record 44.7 million passengers travelled with PKP Intercity, more than 10% up on the previous year’s record and some 45% higher than three years earlier. Poland has launched a tender to buy 20 trains that can reach speeds of 320 km/h (199 mph), making them the fastest ever to travel on Polish tracks. World.title: Polish government proposes middle-class tax cuts funded by increased rates for wealthiest
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. The country is already under the EU's excessive deficit procedure, requiring it to take steps to bring public finances under greater control https://t.co/LNJ0YrP2Ge — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland launches tourism campaign featuring Lewandowski, Eisenberg and Rubik
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 The city of Lublin in eastern Poland, which will be a European City of Culture in 2029, last year welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors, including over half a million from abroad. The city is known for its rich Jewish history, and featured prominently in the 2024 Oscar-nominated film A Real Pain, directed by and starring Eisenberg, whose ancestors were Jews from Lublin and the nearby town of Krasnystaw. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP within a decade, from about 5% now. The strategy includes creating a “Polish brand” through which internationally recognised athletes, artists, historical figures and products are showcased more prominently. Last month, the government appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. The city of Lublin in eastern Poland welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors in 2025. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: A Multi-Brand K-Beauty Pop-Up Is Coming to Prague This September
World.content:
A Korean beauty pop-up will bring eight K-beauty brands and K-pop entertainment to Prague’s Vltava River this September.

The HARUNARU K-Beauty Pop-up will take place aboard KVASOUL, a self-brewing boat restaurant, from September 4 to 8.



An industry preview for beauty professionals and influencers will be held on September 3.

Visitors will be able to discover, test and buy products from eight Korean brands, including GASH, ranked No. 1 at Olive Young, South Korea’s leading beauty retailer, and ilso, known for its pore-care products.

The event will also feature K-pop performances, a Random Dance Challenge, an idol-style makeup show and a dedicated selection of K-pop albums and merchandise.

The pop-up is aimed at introducing emerging Korean beauty brands to consumers and industry professionals in the Czech Republic and across Central and Eastern Europe.

Entry is free, although visitors are encouraged to register online in advance.

The event is organized by Bramasole Prague s.r.o., which operates several Korean restaurant brands in Prague.

📍 KVASOUL, Vltava River, Prague

World.title: Dancing House Marks 30 Years With a Free Weekend of Dance in Prague
World.content:
Prague’s Dancing House will celebrate its 30th anniversary with a free two-day program of dance classes, performances and workshops on August 29 and 30.

Jiráskovo náměstí, next to the landmark on the Vltava embankment, will host a temporary stage and dance floor throughout the weekend.



The program will run from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. on both Saturday and Sunday.

Visitors can join professional instructors for classes in bachata, street dance and Latin American dance. There will also be sessions for children, dance demonstrations and opportunities to meet and talk with instructors.

The event is open to all levels, with participants able to watch performances or take part in the classes.

Weekend program

The schedule is the same on both days until the evening finale.

11:00 a.m. – Opening

11:05 a.m. – Children’s dance class

11:50 a.m. – Talk with the instructor

12:00 p.m. – Bachata demonstration

12:05 p.m. – Bachata class

12:50 p.m. – Talk with bachata instructors

1:00 p.m. – Street dance demonstration

1:05 p.m. – Street dance class

1:50 p.m. – Talk with the street dance instructor

2:00 p.m. – Latin American dance demonstration

2:05 p.m. – Latin American dance class

2:50 p.m. – Talk with instructors

3:00 p.m. – Hat Jazz performance

3:05 p.m. – Children’s dance class

3:50 p.m. – Talk with the instructor

4:00 p.m. – Bachata demonstration

4:05 p.m. – Bachata class

4:50 p.m. – Talk with bachata instructors

5:00 p.m. – Street dance demonstration

5:05 p.m. – Street dance class

5:50 p.m. – Talk with the street dance instructor

6:00 p.m. – Latin American dance demonstration

6:05 p.m. – Latin American dance class

6:50 p.m. – Talk with instructors

7:00 p.m. – Acrobatic performance

7:05 p.m. – Hula Hoops performance

The closing acrobatic performance will differ each day. Saturday will feature a handstand performance, while Sunday will bring Duo ReAct.

Admission is free. Organizers will also provide light refreshments.

Completed in 1996, the Dancing House is one of Prague’s best-known examples of modern architecture. It stands at the corner of Rašínovo nábřeží and Jiráskovo náměstí, overlooking the Vltava.

The building was designed by Croatian-Czech architect Vlado Milunić in collaboration with Canadian-American architect Frank Gehry. Its curved forms and leaning towers give the impression of a dancing couple, which inspired its Czech name, Tančící dům.

The building is also known by the nickname “Ginger and Fred,” referring to American dancers Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire.

World.title: Bolt Launches App-Free Ride Kiosks in the Czech Republic
World.content:
Bolt has introduced self-service kiosks in the Czech Republic that allow customers to order a ride without a smartphone, mobile data or the Bolt app.

The first kiosk is now operating at Westfield Chodov in Prague. A second will open at Westfield Černý Most on September 1. The company says it plans to consider other high-traffic locations in the future.



The kiosks use TapBox technology and provide access to the same Bolt driver network, pricing and safety standards available through the app.

Customers can place an order directly at the screen, making the service available to people who do not use smartphones or cannot access their phones at the time.

Both shopping centres have also introduced dedicated parking spaces for Bolt drivers collecting passengers. Customers are directed to these designated areas rather than having to meet drivers at potentially unsafe stopping points such as bus stops.

How Bolt kiosks work

Ordering a ride takes several steps. Customers enter their destination, select a ride category and provide their phone number. The available categories are Standard, Comfort, Premium and XL.

Payment is made by card. Once the booking is completed, the kiosk prints a confirmation and sends an SMS containing the vehicle details, estimated arrival time and instructions for finding the driver.

The kiosks operate around the clock and support Czech, English, German, French and Ukrainian.

Each ride booked through a kiosk carries an additional CZK 25 fee.

Bolt says the system could also benefit drivers by connecting them with customers who might otherwise be unable to use the app. The company expects the kiosks to reduce waiting times between rides at busy shopping centres and create additional opportunities for drivers.

The Czech launch follows the introduction of similar kiosks in Slovakia earlier this summer, including at airports.

World.title: Prague Adds 18 Kilometers of Cycle Routes but Cycling Numbers Barely Rise
World.content:
Prague is continuing to expand its cycling infrastructure, but the number of recorded bicycle journeys across the city has remained largely unchanged.

Automatic counters installed on major cycling routes recorded about 5.6 million passages in 2025, roughly 1 percent fewer than the previous year.

After adjusting for counter failures and temporary route closures, however, the Technical Road Administration (TSK) calculated a 0.4 percent increase in cycling traffic.



Prague Adds 18 Kilometers of Routes Away From Traffic

The city added 18 kilometers of two-way cycle paths and other cycling routes separated from motor traffic during the year. The total length of marked cycling routes increased by one kilometer to approximately 550 kilometers.

Routes separated from car traffic now account for 263 kilometers of the network, an increase of seven kilometers compared with the previous year.

TSK operates automatic counters at 31 locations on Prague’s main cycling routes. The devices use induction loops or radar to record cyclists and can determine their direction of travel.

The largest increase in two-way cycling routes came over the past year. Their combined length grew from 63 to 81 kilometers. These routes allow cyclists to travel in both directions on streets that are otherwise one-way for motor vehicles.

New two-way routes were added mainly in Prague 7 around Letná, in Prague 5 in Barrandov, and in Prague 6 around Na Petynce, Rozdělovská and Podbaba.

Modřany Remains Prague’s Busiest Cycling Route

The highest number of cyclists was recorded in Modřany, at the intersection of Vltavanů and U Kino streets. The counter registered 578,016 passages during the year.

Another 540,656 cycling journeys were recorded on Povltavská Street south of Troja Castle.

The largest year-on-year increase was recorded on the Barrandov Bridge, where cycling traffic rose following the completion of its more than two-year reconstruction.

World.title: “Upcycling” Prague: Old Offices and Industrial Sites Find New Life as Apartments
World.content:
Former offices, commercial properties and industrial sites in Prague are being converted into apartments rather than demolished, giving developers another option in a city struggling to build enough new homes.

The approach is sometimes described as “upcycling” — adapting ageing buildings for a new purpose while making use of structures and land that are already developed.

One recent example is in Pankrác, near Vyšehrad, where an office building has been converted into the Mo-cha HOME residential complex.



Developed by Cimex, the project opened this spring with 91 fully equipped apartments, most of them in the Czech 2+kk layout, consisting of a living room with a kitchenette and one separate bedroom.

Existing buildings offer valuable locations

Owners of older properties increasingly have to decide whether to renovate them, change their use or demolish them. Many were built for different needs and standards than those expected from buildings today.

Their locations, however, can be a major advantage. Older properties are often close to public transport, shops and other services, making them attractive for residential conversion.

Transforming an existing building can also be faster to prepare than developing a completely new project on a brownfield, although each property must be assessed individually.

The approach can preserve existing structures, reduce demolition and make better use of land that is already developed.

More former offices are becoming homes

Pankrác is not the only part of Prague where old buildings are being converted into housing.

In Holešovice, the former Tesla complex, once used for light-bulb production, has been transformed into a residential project with 149 apartments. The building had stood unused for years, but its main structure remained in relatively good condition.

In Prague 7, another former administrative building near Urania has also been adapted for residential use.

In Prague 3, PSN is preparing the reconstruction of a former telecommunications exchange on Fibichova Street. Built in 1926 and designed by architect Bohumír Kozák, the building is expected to become a rental housing project with 116 units.

One of the largest transformations is planned in Žižkov, where the functionalist former General Pension Institute will be converted into an apartment building with smaller units. The project received a building permit last year.

Not every older building is suitable for conversion. Technical condition, layout, location, project costs and future use all determine whether redevelopment makes economic and practical sense.

World.title: More Czech Companies Test Four-Day Work Weeks Despite Political Resistance
World.content:
A growing number of companies in the Czech Republic are experimenting with a four-day working week, with some reporting higher productivity and greater employee satisfaction.

But politicians remain reluctant to make the arrangement a standard option across the country.

Under the model, employees work four days instead of five while keeping their full salaries. Companies that have introduced the system say workers can maintain their output while having more time to rest.



At Trinity Group, the arrangement has been in place for five years. Jan Hanulík, the company’s product and marketing director, said productivity had risen despite employees working one day less each week.

“Although we have one working day less, productivity has increased,” Hanulík said, adding that the company’s results have roughly doubled since the system was introduced.

A survey cited in the report found that around 70 percent of employees in the Czech Republic would welcome a four-day working week.

Politicians remain cautious

The idea has already been adopted in different forms elsewhere in Europe. In Belgium, for example, employees can request to work their weekly hours over four days rather than five. The system therefore does not necessarily mean fewer working hours.

Czech politicians, however, argue that a single system would not work across all sectors.

Labor and Social Affairs Minister Aleš Juchelka of ANO said a legally mandated four-day week could create problems in areas already facing staff shortages, including social services and health care.

SPD lawmaker Lucie Šafránková also said the working week should reflect the conditions of individual professions and employers rather than follow one nationwide rule.

Czech companies are already experimenting

Several companies have introduced or tested four-day schedules, including SAB Finance, Phonexia, Sherpas, Digiskills and Café Eternity.

Not every experiment has lasted. The Cognito agency eventually returned to a traditional five-day working week after testing the shorter schedule.

World.title: Foreign Workers Now Make Up 22% of Czech Employees
World.content:
Foreign workers accounted for around 22% of all employees in the Czech Republic at the end of 2025, according to data from the Czech National Bank (ČNB).

Their number has nearly tripled over the past decade, rising from about 323,000 in 2015 to 935,000 last year.

The increase has significantly changed the makeup of the Czech labor market. Foreign workers represented roughly 8% of all employees in 2015. By the end of 2025, their share had reached 22%.

Ukrainians made up the largest group of foreign employees, with approximately 358,000 working in Czechia at the end of last year. Slovaks were the second-largest group, numbering almost 230,000.



The Czech labor market has also seen increasing numbers of workers from other countries outside the European Union, including the Philippines and India.

Foreign workers are particularly important in several sectors, including manufacturing, construction, retail, transport and hospitality.

Their presence is most pronounced in accommodation, food services and hospitality. Foreign nationals accounted for more than half of all employees in the sector at the end of 2025.

The figures should, however, be interpreted with some caution when comparing individual industries. The CNB notes that employment agencies can distort the sectoral breakdown.

Workers employed through agencies are recorded in official statistics under administrative and support services, even when their actual jobs are in manufacturing, construction, logistics or other industries.

World.title: Tesco Teams Up With Wolt. Can Express Delivery Save Its Czech Business?
World.content:
Tesco will launch a new express delivery service in Prague in September, working with Wolt to deliver orders within 40 minutes.

The service, called Tesco Hned, will initially be available from selected Tesco stores in the Czech capital.

The launch comes as speculation continues over a possible sale of Tesco’s Central European operations and the British retailer’s future in the Czech Republic.



Tesco Hned is designed for customers who need groceries and other everyday products quickly rather than as part of a larger planned shop. Orders will include food, drinks, cosmetics, household products, pet supplies and other goods.

The company says its standard online shopping service will continue to focus on larger orders, while the new option is aimed at customers who need a few items immediately.

Tesco has already tested the service at six Prague stores. It plans to extend Tesco Hned to another 22 locations in the coming weeks.

Delivery will be provided through Wolt, giving customers access to Tesco products through the courier company’s platform.

Tesco faces questions over its future

The new service comes at a difficult time for Tesco in Central Europe.

According to the Financial Times, Tesco’s British owners are considering selling their operations in the region, including the Czech Republic. The Schwarz Group, which owns Lidl and Kaufland, and Polish retailer Biedronka have reportedly been mentioned among potential buyers.

Tesco has not announced plans to leave the Czech market, and the launch of Tesco Hned suggests the company continues to invest in its services.

World.title: Orbán’s secret EU campaign revealed: How Hungary took its message to Europe – and how much we paid for it
World.content:
A newly obtained media plan reveals that Viktor Orbán’s government paid more than HUF 313 million for a campaign placing the Hungarian prime minister’s seven-point criticism of the European Union in newspapers across Europe in 2021.

Hungarian taxpayers paid more than HUF 313 million for a government advertising campaign that promoted then-Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s criticism of the European Union in foreign newspapers, newly obtained documents reveal.

The campaign, launched in the summer of 2021, was considerably broader than previously known. While two full-page s – one in a Danish newspaper and another in Spain – attracted attention at the time, documents obtained by investigative outlet Átlátszó show that Orbán’s message was ultimately published in 18 foreign newspapers.

The campaign came at a particularly tense moment in Hungary’s relationship with the EU, following a series of disputes over the Hungarian government’s policies and its increasingly confrontational stance towards Brussels.

A HUF 313 million campaign against the “European empire”

The , titled On the Future of the European Union – Hungary’s Proposals, presented seven points under Orbán’s signature. Its opening message declared: “We say no to a European empire!”

According to the media plans obtained from the Prime Minister’s Cabinet Office, the government paid a total of HUF 313 million gross for the campaign. The net advertising cost was HUF 213.4 million. On top of this came a 15 per cent agency fee of HUF 32 million paid to New Land Media, the company responsible for organising the campaign, followed by VAT.

The documents indicate that the government initially targeted even more publications. In total, 25 newspapers appear to have been approached, although seven ultimately did not publish the . One of them, Bulgaria’s 24 Chasa, reportedly could not run it because of technical reasons. The campaign therefore went far beyond the two s that became publicly known at the time.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Why was Orbán’s message published in 2021?

The timing was important. In March 2021, Fidesz left the European People’s Party group in the European Parliament after changes to the group’s rules opened the way for an entire delegation to be expelled.

Three months later, Hungary’s parliament adopted the government’s so-called child protection law, which drew widespread criticism over its restrictions concerning LGBTQ-related content. The legislation was promulgated on 23 June.

Just days later, EU leaders gathered for a summit in Brussels, where the Hungarian government faced strong criticism over the law. Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte had already taken an exceptionally hard line before the summit, saying that, in his view, Hungary had no place in the EU.

At the summit itself, leaders from 17 member states signed a declaration condemning the Hungarian legislation as a “blatant form of discrimination”.

The first s featuring Orbán’s response appeared in foreign newspapers the following day, on 26 June. Over the next two weeks, readers of a further 16 publications encountered the Hungarian prime minister’s seven-point message.

What did Orbán’s seven points say?

The  presented a very Eurosceptic vision of the European Union. Orbán argued that Brussels was building a “superstate” without democratic authorisation and called for rejecting what he described as a European empire.

He also said European integration should be regarded as a means rather than an end in itself, arguing against the principle of an “ever closer union” being included in the EU treaties.

Another point called for decisions to be made by elected leaders rather than international NGOs, while accusing the EU of outsourcing the rule of law. The Hungarian prime minister also linked the future of European integration to economic success, arguing that the EU would have no future if member states could not become more successful together than separately.

Other points focused on migration and pandemics, strengthening national parliaments and restoring public confidence in European democracy. The final proposal was particularly notable: Serbia should be admitted to the European Union.

Several major European newspapers refused the 

Not every newspaper approached by the Hungarian government agreed to publish the campaign. The editor-in-chief of The Times of Malta said the newspaper did not want to accept money from a government that restricted press freedom, human rights and the rule of law. Publishing the , he argued, could have turned the newspaper into a tool of a policy running counter to press freedom.

Belgium’s De Standaard similarly rejected the  and instead published a full-page rainbow-coloured response. La Libre Belgique reportedly argued that Orbán’s  did not reflect the truth, while De Morgen rejected it because the message was incompatible with the values represented by the newspaper.

Sweden’s Dagens Nyheter offered Orbán an interview instead, but received no response. Meanwhile, The Irish Times argued that the Hungarian government was attempting to use money to bypass the editorial process and place its own message directly before readers.

A campaign designed to reach beyond Orbán’s allies

The newspapers that did publish the s were not exclusively sympathetic to the Hungarian government. According to the documents, roughly half of the publications that carried the campaign were critical of Orbán’s government to some degree, while the other half were more favourable towards it.

The selection also suggests that the government was seeking a broad international audience rather than simply targeting publications in countries considered political allies. The campaign included conservative and right-wing newspapers, but also mainstream titles such as France’s Le Figaro and Sweden’s Dagens Industri.

World.title: Breaking: Hungarian Air Force Gripen fighter jet crashes near Szolnok – UPDATE: Video
World.content:
A Hungarian Air Force Gripen fighter jet has crashed near Szolnok for reasons that are currently unknown, Prime Minister Péter Magyar said on Monday. The pilot successfully ejected from the aircraft.

Pilot successfully ejects

“For reasons that are currently unknown, one of the Hungarian Defence Forces’ Gripen fighter jets crashed near Szolnok a few minutes ago,” Magyar said in a statement on Facebook.

He added that the pilot had successfully ejected and that an investigation into the incident was already under way. The Defence Minister was travelling to the scene, while further information was expected to be provided shortly.

Pilot in ambulance

Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi stated in a Facebook video that the pilot is in an ambulance but was not injured, because the pilot did everything possible to land the aircraft on military property.

According to the minister, an investigation into the incident is already underway, and he and the Chief of the General Staff are heading to the scene, from where they will provide updates on the situation.

No reported injuries or damage to civilian infrastructure

According to the preliminary report, there were no personal injuries and no damage to civilian infrastructure in the crash. The exact circumstances of the accident, including what caused the fighter jet to go down, remain unclear.

We will update this article with any updates.
