World.title: Cash Cow: China’s Most Mocked Cartoon Is Suddenly a Viral Hit
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018905/Cash Cow: China’s Most Mocked Cartoon Is Suddenly a Viral Hit
World.content:
Poorly animated yellow cows walking on two legs, raw voice acting, and extremely slow pace — these are characteristics of China’s most recent box office hit and viral phenomenon.

Released Aug. 5 after virtually no promotion, the movie, “Niu Lai,” or “Cow Comes,” is named for its titular character: a calf who struggles to stand. The film follows Niu Lai and his herd as they overcome a number of difficulties while migrating, eventually growing up into an able-bodied adult cow unfazed in the face of danger. Except, Niu Lai awakens, realizing that he is still a calf — but he is finally able to support his own weight.

The movie, reported to have no financial backing, earned just 5,500 yuan ($815) at the box office in its first week. But after multiple viewers posted images of the film on social media criticizing it, that number suddenly surged to over 710,000 yuan on Aug. 15, according to ticketing platform Maoyan. As of Tuesday afternoon, it has taken in 20 million yuan, a figure projected to grow to 135 million yuan by the time it leaves screens.

The reason for its explosive popularity? Its absurdist visuals and overall crude production design have turned it into a word-of-mouth viral phenomenon. The characters’ legs rarely move in sync, making them appear like they’re sliding. Close-ups of their heads are overblown and blurry. Transitions between scenes are jarring and illogical, and the characters’ voices are poorly recorded and overly stilted.

The effect has led to highly polarized ratings on domestic review platform Douban, with many giving it either one or five stars. As one highly upvoted comment on Maoyan reads, “You don’t have to watch bad movies, but when a movie is bad enough, you have to.”

Wang Yunfei, the founder of a cartoon studio and an acting animated film judge at various film festivals, told Shanghai-based media outlet The Paper, “Professional animators couldn’t produce something this poorly even if they made mistakes. So from a professional standpoint, there’s really nothing to critique. It’s just spectacle-watching.”

The movie’s unexpectedly raw, homemade production has also been regarded by critics and viewers alike as a rebuke to high-investment but poorly reviewed films.

“Niu Lai” was produced by Jingyuan Culture Film and Television Media, based in the northeastern city of Dalian, which was converted from a one-person renovation company, according to corporate data platform Qichacha.

The renovator in question is the film’s creator, 34-year-old Xin Yumeng, who made it alongside his mother, Sun Lifang. The pair reportedly had no background in animation and made the film over five years, without the help of AI. They also provided the voices for the characters, while Sun composed and sang the film’s theme song.

On a domestic radio show, Xin said that he made the film out of a love for animated films, and chose a cow as the protagonist because his father was born in the Year of the Ox.

As for the quality of the film, Xin added that much of the equipment he bought secondhand for the film’s production eventually broke down. “Even the computer motherboards burned out ... The final result has a lot to do with the equipment used.”

Le Fumin, a 35-year-old security worker from Shanghai, told domestic media that he liked that “Niu Lai” was made by two ordinary people, rather than having large film-industry backing. “It shows a bit of rebellion against the assembly-line formula of mainstream filmmaking,” he said. “Why should I only be allowed to watch what the industry feeds me? The kind of happiness I choose for myself is worth the ticket price, too.”

Le said the atmosphere in the theater was particularly relaxed. “Over the course of two hours, the pressure of meeting KPIs at work, the exhaustion of commuting, and all the troubles of everyday life just melted away with the laughter of the whole theater,” he said. “It felt like returning to something simple and genuine — like the carefree feeling of watching random films in a video rental shop as a kid.”

As “Niu Lai” has risen in popularity, fan-made tributes to it have spread online and offline, with some placing Niu Lai into posters for recent international box office hits such as “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey.” Cinema staff have also put up rudimentary, hand-drawn posters advertising the film — and paying homage to its crude animation — outside theaters.

Even stocks of three companies with “niu” in their names — Jinniu Chemical Industry, Goneo Group, and Tongniu Information — shot into the top five trending list on domestic finance data platform Tonghuashun over the weekend, as the film’s title can be interpreted as “the bull market is coming,” domestic media reported.

Other entities are also capitalizing on the film’s virality, creating their own animal-based animated shorts to promote products. On Monday, local authorities for Dongguan City in the southern Guangdong province produced a video titled “E Lai,” or “Goose Comes,” to promote the city’s local specialty — roast goose — garnering more than 26,000 likes on Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok.

For most, however, the movie is simply about having fun. Mak SzeNing, a 27-year-old pet care worker from Hong Kong, watched the film in the eastern city of Hangzhou at a nearly sold-out screening. “I don’t think the movie’s value lies in its production quality,” she told Sixth Tone. “Its value is that it brings a group of strangers into the same theater, and suddenly everyone feels like they’ve found their kindred spirits and laughs together.”

“If a movie can make people laugh, then I think it’s a good movie,” she said.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: A still from “Niu Lai.” From Douban)

World.title: Pagcor imposes P1-M fine on gambling firm linked to Ivana Alawi iPhone giveaway
World.content:
GAMING. Pagcor chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco speaks during the agency's budget hearing in the House of Representatives on August 24, 2026.

Pagcor chairman Alejandro Tengco says, 'We fined the online gaming company P1 million and, together with that, gave them a stern warning na hindi na dapat maulit ito'

MANILA, Philippines –The Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (Pagcor) imposed a P1 million fine against a gambling firm for sponsoring influencer Ivana Alawi’s giveaway of 100 iPhones back In July without seeking permission to undertake the promotion.

During the House of Representatives’ committee on appropriations budget hearing for 2027, Kamanggagawa party-list Representative Elijah Fernando showed surprise and alarm at influencers and gambling firms linking up to promote each other. Fernando also called out Alawi without naming the specific gambling firm she was linked to.

In Alawi’s case, she has a brand ambassadorship with Casino Plus as previously disclosed by the online gaming platform.

Alawi bought some P4.28 million in iPhone 17 Pro Max units — 100 in all — and the promotion to give them away tasked prospective winners with following her “CP Fam” and commenting on a given post to be considered for the giveaway.

Pagcor chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco said, “We fined the online gaming company P1 million and, together with that, gave them a stern warning na hindi na dapat maulit ito (that it shouldn’t happen again).”

He added, “Kung maulit ito (If it occurs again), a heavier fine and the possibility that another violation can lead to the suspension and ultimately, the cancellation of their license,” a warning that those endorsements should have the blessing of the Ad Standards Council and Pagcor.

Tengco also noted that about “50% of the current operators of online gaming are illegal, meaning that we do not have any jurisdiction over them.”

When asked about enforcement against illegal gambling operators, Tengco said Pagcor coordinates with the Department of Information and Communications Technology, the National Telecommunications Commission, and the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center in filing cases against the endorsers of illegal gambling sites in a bid to take down the sites themselves.

Further, Tengco also said a number of influencers and content creators withdrew their sponsorships and endorsements when this was made known, finding legal operators to tie up with instead.

– Rappler.com

World.title: Typhoon Obet now in PAR, may eventually enhance southwest monsoon
World.content:
PAGASA says Typhoon Obet (Saudel) may already exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility just hours after its entry, but it is still seen to enhance the southwest monsoon during the week

MANILA, Philippines – Typhoon Saudel entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) at 1:20 pm on Monday, August 24, and was given the local name Obet.

Obet is the country’s 15th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the fourth for August, after Tropical Depression Luis, Tropical Storm Maymay (Kujira), and Tropical Depression Neneng (Gaenari).

As of 4 pm on Monday, Obet was located 1,350 kilometers east northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, moving west northwest at 30 kilometers per hour (km/h).

The typhoon has maximum sustained winds of 165 km/h and gustiness of up to 205 km/h.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said in its 5 pm bulletin that Obet will stay far from Philippine landmass, and may already exit PAR within 12 hours. There are no rainfall or wind warnings due to the typhoon.

However, even after Obet leaves PAR, it is still seen to enhance the southwest monsoon or habagat later in the week.

The southwest monsoon is currently affecting Luzon and portions of the Visayas.

On Monday evening, the southwest monsoon is causing scattered rain and thunderstorms in Metro Manila, the Ilocos Region, the Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Cavite, Batangas, and Rizal, as well as isolated rain showers or thunderstorms in the rest of Luzon, Western Visayas, and the Negros Island Region.

Flash floods and landslides are possible during periods of moderate to heavy rain or severe thunderstorms.

Starting midweek, the enhanced southwest monsoon could trigger significant rain in at least three provinces, particularly the following:

Tuesday afternoon, August 25, to Wednesday afternoon, August 26

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 millimeters): Zambales

Wednesday afternoon, August 26, to Thursday afternoon, August 27

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Zambales, Bataan, Occidental Mindoro

More provinces and regions are likely to be covered by rainfall warnings in the last days of August.

The southwest monsoon is also bringing strong to gale-force gusts to these areas:

Monday, August 24

most of Luzon, most of Visayas, Northern Mindanao, Dinagat Islands, Agusan del Norte, Surigao del Norte, Davao Occidental, Davao Oriental

Tuesday, August 25

most of Luzon, most of Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Misamis Oriental, Agusan del Norte, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Basilan, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Lanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Sultan Kudarat, Davao Occidental, Davao Oriental

Wednesday, August 26

most of Luzon, most of Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Misamis Oriental, Agusan del Norte, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Basilan, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Lanao del Norte, Davao Occidental, Davao Oriental

For coastal waters, moderate to rough conditions are expected in the next 24 hours.

Up to rough seas (small vessels should not venture out to sea)

Seaboard of Batanes; northern seaboard of Babuyan Islands – waves up to 3.5 meters high

Western seaboard of Babuyan Islands; northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte; western seaboard of Kalayaan Islands – waves up to 3 meters high

Up to moderate seas (small vessels should take precautionary measures or avoid sailing, if possible)

Seaboards of Ilocos Sur, mainland Cagayan, Isabela, and Zambales; western seaboards of Pangasinan, Bataan, and Lubang Islands; eastern seaboard of Davao Oriental; remaining seaboards of Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, and Kalayaan Islands – waves up to 2.5 meters high

Seaboards of La Union, Aurora, Surigao del Norte, Davao del Sur, and Davao Occidental; western seaboards of Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and mainland Palawan including Calamian Islands; northern and eastern seaboards of Polillo Islands, Catanduanes, and Northern Samar; northern seaboards of Camarines Norte and Camarines Sur; eastern seaboards of Albay, Sorsogon, and Eastern Samar; remaining seaboards of Pangasinan and Lubang Islands – waves up to 2 meters high

Meanwhile, PAGASA is still monitoring two other tropical cyclones outside PAR.

The tropical depression near the PAR eastern boundary intensified into a tropical storm on Monday morning, and was given the international name Atsani.

Atsani was located 1,765 kilometers east of Central Luzon as of 3 pm on Monday, moving east northeast or away from PAR at 35 km/h. It has maximum sustained winds of 65 km/h and gustiness of up to 80 km/h.

PAGASA Weather Specialist Grace Castañeda-Carpio said Atsani may either weaken into a low pressure area (LPA) outside PAR or possibly follow Obet’s track and enter PAR. But even if the latter happens, it would not have a direct impact on the country, added Carpio.

The other tropical cyclone outside PAR, Neneng, remains a tropical depression. At 3 pm, Neneng was last spotted 505 kilometers north northwest of Itbayat, Batanes, moving northwest at only 10 km/h. It has maximum sustained winds of 45 km/h and gustiness of up to 55 km/h.

Neneng had weakened into an LPA and exited PAR last Thursday, August 20, then redeveloped into a tropical depression on Saturday, August 22. It is not expected to reenter PAR.

PAGASA previously estimated that up to four tropical cyclones may develop within or enter PAR in August. – Rappler.com

World.title: [Rappler’s Best] The ‘maleta’ boys’ travelogue
World.content:
Does the complaint against Martin Romualdez stand on a house of cards?

What a weekend for the trading world following Canada’s suspension of its negotiations with the US, an “uncharted territory” for the two neighbors, as the BBC put it.

Canadian negotiators walked away from the trade talks over what Prime Minister Mark Carney described as America’s “new terms that were uneconomic, unfair, and undermined the net benefits” for their country. (Read and watch Carney’s full speech here.)

The Trump administration’s response was swift, imposing 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods — though they represent just a thin slice of exports to the US.

Canada retaliated by announcing the “dollar for dollar” tariffs on steel, electronics, and other products from the US effective September 8.

“We take this step reluctantly,” Carney said, but stressed that suspending the negotiations was to Canada’s best interests. “We set our own course. We make our own weather. In Canada, we are masters in our own house,” said Carney, who faces a major political test for this move.

Was Canada engaged in a trade war? “You’re at war when you get attacked,” Carney told a press conference. “We got attacked.”

Carney was elected only last year — at the height of Trump’s attacks against Canada — and promised to play tough with US President Donald Trump. At the World Economic Forum in Davos early this year, he urged “middle powers” to come together to counter American hegemony. Trump reacted in his own Davos speech, claiming that Canada “lives because of the United States,” and later threatened it with a 100% tariff.

Trump’s tariff regime has sent shockwaves globally. Just last month, his government imposed new tariffs of 10% and 12.5% on goods from at least 60 trading partners, including the Philippines (which was the only one slapped with 12.5%), over their alleged poor enforcement of existing bans on forced labor. Philippine officials have given assurances, however, that they will be negotiating with the US for some consideration.

Back home, another tit-for-tat persisted, this time between the Ombudsman and former House speaker and presidential cousin Martin Romualdez, who is the subject of an investigation for possible plunder, bribery, graft, and money laundering.

Romualdez wants the probe to end, and reiterated this last week, following the recantation of some of the so-called maleta (luggage) boys of their allegations against him.

Former Marine Orly Guteza, who had accused Romualdez of receiving kickbacks for budget allocations to corrupt infrastructure projects, made an about-turn and said he made those claims at the behest of politicians belonging to the rival Duterte bloc.

Guteza is an ex-security aide of Romualdez’s former sparring partner in the House, the now fugitive and resigned congressman Zaldy Co. He testified at the Senate in 2025, where he disclosed that he regularly delivered luggages packed with cash to Romualdez’s residences. Read more here.

Guteza, along with seven of the more than a dozen “maleta boys,” later signed affidavits that the Ombudsman’s panel of investigators used to build its complaint against Romualdez and Co.

But Guteza recanted last week, along with three others — Benny Bulontate, Bernard Tube, and Rosebert Waupan, whose affidavits were part of the Ombudsman’s supplemental complaint against Romualdez, Co, and others last July. What’s the impact of these recantations on the complaint, which has yet to reach the court? Dwight de Leon explains here.

Five other ex-security aides, whose testimonies were secured by the Ombudsman, have not withdrawn them. At least not yet, anyway. Without them, it’s tough to connect the properties allegedly bought by Romualdez through dummies to the corruption of the public works budget. The Ombudsman has said, however, that 28 more witnesses are lined up against the former speaker.

Last month, the Ombudsman announced it was close to filing plunder complaints against Romualdez, since the investigation pointed to him as the “central figure” in the flood control corruption scheme. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. himself said in his State of the Nation Address in July that his cousin will soon be charged in court.

What’s delaying it then? Does the complaint against Romualdez stand on a house of cards?

Here are some of Rappler’s bests that you shouldn’t miss:

Fred Lubang recommends concrete measures — “trace every gun, close every leak” — to address school violence in the wake of the shooting at the Ateneo de Zamboanga Junior High School in Zamboanga City. Kevin Hapal weighs in on the debate about video games and school violence, arguing that the problem is the “monetized, unguarded social environment” around these games.

Lala Rimando spells out the trade-off embedded in ABS-CBN’s P6-billion rescue. Lala also breaks down where the P6 billion will go — to the banks and retirees, among others.

John Nery chimes in on the debate over the call made by Filipino journalists and media workers to travel to Israel on the invitation of Israel. They were “dead wrong” to go there, he said.

Marites Vitug sits down with UP assistant professor Enrico Gloria about China’s sophisticated use of its toolkit of coercive measures — and whether Manila and Beijing can meet halfway over both its hardline stance on the West Philippine Sea. Bea Cupin tells us what we know so far about the controversial provisional agreement between both sides on Ayungin.

– Rappler.com

World.title: This maritime leader is the first woman to receive the RVR Nation Building award
World.content:
Doris Magsaysay Ho, the CEO and president of the Magsaysay Group of Companies, receives the award for her 'people first' style of leadership

MANILA, Philippines – The maritime industry is one of the biggest in Philippine overseas employment — with Filipinos accounting for over 25% of the entire world’s demographic of seafaring professionals.

This industry, however, has long been male-dominated. A report by UP-CIFAL Philippines even found that Filipino women only make up over 6% of the maritime workforce, and often take on jobs in hospitality, catering and passenger services. As if these numbers aren’t already glaring enough, the same report also found that very few Filipino women actually go on to occupy technical and senior leadership positions.

Doris Magsaysay Ho, however, breaks that chain as the current CEO and president of the shipping, human resources, and logistics firm Magsaysay Group of Companies. Throughout her time as its head, the Magsaysay Group became the first local maritime company to be awarded the EDGE Assess certification for workplace gender equity, as it is women that have filled up 45% of junior management roles.

Now, Ho is being honored with a Ramon V. del Rosario (RVR) Nation Building award — and has just become the first woman to receive the distinction.

The CEO and president’s leadership style is simple: she shifts the focus from ships to people, and recognizes that the holistic wellbeing of seafarers is just as important as the economic support they are able to provide their families through their jobs. Testament to this is the MOL Magsaysay Maritime Academy, an institution founded by the Magsaysay Group and Mitsui O.S.K Lines in 2018 to train up to 1,000 maritime students.

“Dr. Doris Magsaysay Ho pioneered the Philippine maritime industry’s transformation into a globally respected sector while, in equal measure, expanding opportunities for Filipino seafarers and contributing to national progress. Her leadership has shown that shipping is not merely about connecting ports and markets, but also about advancing the welfare of the people who keep the industry moving,” said retired Chief Justice Artemio Panganiban, who serves as the award’s board of judges chair.

The Magsaysay Group has also placed a bigger emphasis on progressive welfare initiatives with Ho’s help.

There’s Fundamayan, which provides financial assistance to employees and their families when they need it most. Most interestingly, though, there’s also MATTERS, a crew welfare system dedicated to Filipino seafarers’ health, mental wellness, financial literacy, and career advancement.

But this is not the first time Ho has achieved a historic first. In 2023, she also became the first woman to occupy the chair of the Steamship Mutual Underwriting Association (Bermuda), which addresses insurance issues for ship owners across the globe.

Ho pursued a degree in industrial design at the Pratt Institute in New York before coming home to work for the Magsaysay Group of Companies — her family’s business. She eventually also received an honorary Doctor of Humane Arts degree from the same university.

The president and CEO received the RVR Nation Building award after the late Howard Dee, the former Philippine ambassador to the Holy See.

Other notable names who have earned the same distinction since 2010 include Jollibee founder Tony Tan-Caktiong, SM Group founder Henry Sy Sr., businessman Manuel V. Pangilinan, and Ayala Corp. chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala, among many others.

The Ramon V. del Rosario Nation Building award is organized by the PHINMA Group, the Junior Chamber International Manila, De La Salle University, and the Asian Institute of Management. It awards notable Filipino business leaders who make a social impact through their work. – Rappler.com

World.title: Alex Eala earns new career-high ranking going into US Open
World.content:
Alex Eala eclipses her previous career-high ranking of No. 20 following strong runs in the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open

MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala returns to the US Open with a new career-high ranking.

The Filipina tennis star rose to No. 18 in the latest WTA rankings released on Monday, August 24, days before she begins her campaign in the last Grand Slam of the year.

Eala eclipsed her previous career high of No. 20, which she achieved on August 3 after winning her breakthrough WTA Tour crown in the Washington Open following strong runs in the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open.

She reached the round of 16 in the Canadian Open, where she fell to Swiss world No. 12 Belinda Bencic, then made the round of 32 in the Cincinnati Open, where her winning streak against top-10 players got snapped at the hands of American world No. 10 Amanda Anisimova.

It will be a busy US Open schedule for the 21-year-old as she first takes part in mixed doubles play, teaming up with Canadian star and ATP No. 4 Felix Auger-Aliassime.

Eala and Auger-Aliassime will take on husband and wife Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina in the round of 16.

The Filipina will also see action in the Stars of the Open exhibition event, which features other top male and female players in Anisimova, Ukraine’s Marta Kostyuk, USA’s Iva Jovic, Alex Michelsen, and Learner Tien, Brazil’s Joao Fonseca, and France’s Arthur Fils.

After that, Eala will open her campaign in the women’s singles tournament, where she is expected to be seeded 17th, her highest in a major.

She seeks to surpass her second-round appearance in the 2025 edition, where she beat Denmark’s Clara Tauson in the opening round to become the first Filipino to win a Grand Slam main draw match in the Open era. – Rappler.com

World.content:
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

World.title: No Justin Brownlee in Gilas Pilipinas’ homestand vs Jordan, Iran
World.content:
Head coach Tim Cone says Gilas Pilipinas will go 'all-Filipino' against Iran and Jordan in the fourth window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers as Justin Brownlee has yet to return to the pink of health

MANILA, Philippines – Gilas Pilipinas continues to miss the services of Justin Brownlee as it plays without the naturalized star in two crucial home games in the fourth window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers.

Head coach Tim Cone made the announcement on Monday, August 24, saying Brownlee has yet to return to the pink of health.

“At this point, he doesn’t feel he’s really healthy enough to contribute. Whether that’s really injury or health, he was having some issues, obviously,” Cone said in a press conference at the Mall of Asia Arena, where the Philippines will host Jordan and Iran on August 28 and 30, respectively.

Brownlee last donned the national colors in a 106-102 double overtime loss to New Zealand in the third window in July, putting up 5 points, 8 rebounds, 4 assists, 3 steals, and 1 block.

Leg and knee injuries, however, kept Brownlee sidelined during the next game against Australia, with the Philippines absorbing a 92-49 beating.

“As we know from the last window, he wasn’t able to play against Australia. We’re hoping that those issues would be resolved by the time we play here, but as it turned out, he’s telling us that he’s just not healthy enough,” said Cone.

Without Brownlee, the Nationals are forced to parade an “all-Filipino” lineup as no other naturalized player is available to suit up in the upcoming window.

Bennie Boatwright still needs President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to sign the bill granting him Filipino citizenship, while Ange Kouame is currently under contract with a team in France.

Losing Brownlee is a major blow, considering that Gilas Pilipinas seeks to sweep Jordan and Iran to boost its prospects of qualifying for the World Cup for the fourth straight edition.

With a 2-4 record, the Philippines sits at joint fifth with Syria in Group E behind Australia (6-0), Iran (5-1), Jordan (4-1), and New Zealand (4-2). Only the top three teams and the best fourth-placed squad between groups E and F will advance.

But optimism is still high for Gilas Pilipinas as it welcomes back Kai Sotto to the fold. – Rappler.com

World.title: Kazakhstan Judo Team Wins Historic Mixed Team Gold at World Championships
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s national judo team secured its first-ever gold medal in the mixed team event at the World Judo Championships among cadets in Guayaquil, Ecuador, marking a historic achievement for the country’s judo programme.

The team title capped a record-breaking individual campaign, with Kazakh judokas winning 11 medals – four gold, three silver and four bronze – at the championships. The result was described as the best in the history of Kazakhstan’s judo at the youth world level, reported the Ministry of Tourism and Sports’ press service on Aug. 24.

Kazakhstan’s boys finished first in the team standings, while the girls placed second. Fatima Supygalieva also made history as the first Kazakh female cadet to win a world championship title.

The results come as part of broader changes to Kazakhstan’s national sports training system led by the Ministry of Tourism and Sports in cooperation with the Judo Federation of Kazakhstan and Zhenis (Victory) club.

Following the Paris Olympics, the federation began updating its approach to the preparation of national teams, with Kazakh coaches working closely with leading international specialists, including Ezio Gamba’s team. Cadet, junior and senior national teams are being integrated into a unified training system.

“We are building a single pathway: cadets – juniors – national team – Olympic Games. When an athlete moves from one age category to another, they should not have to start their preparation from scratch. They continue working within a unified model, with common requirements, scientific support and a clear development trajectory,” Minister of Tourism and Sports Yerbol Myrzabosynov said.

He described the team gold and record medal haul as concrete evidence that the new system is producing results.

“The team gold and record ten medals in the individual competitions are concrete confirmation that the new system works. Our task now is to consistently scale this experience to other sports,” he said.

The unified training model includes scientific analysis of the training process, functional diagnostics, individualized workloads, sports medicine, recovery programmes and continuous monitoring of each athlete’s progress. The National Sports University is expected to play an important role by providing national teams with scientific and analytical support.

Similar approaches are being introduced in fencing, boxing, wrestling and other sports, with the involvement of leading Kazakh and international specialists.

President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated the Kazakh judo team on its performance in Guayaquil, praising its victory in the mixed team competition and congratulating Gabit Rasulhan, Supygalieva and Adilzhan Zhaudinov on their individual gold medals.

Tokayev also held a conversation with International Judo Federation President Marius Vizer, who congratulated the Kazakh leader on the team’s unprecedented success at the world youth championships.

Tokayev expressed appreciation to Vizer for constructive cooperation with Kazakhstan’s national federation and the Ministry of Tourism and Sports, which contributes to the promotion and development of judo in the country.

World.title: Adilet Party Leads Preliminary Results in Kazakhstan’s First Kurultai Election With 71.17%
World.content:
ASTANA – The Adilet party secured 71.17% of the vote in Kazakhstan’s first elections to the Kurultai, according to preliminary results announced by the Central Election Commission (CEC) on Aug. 24.

A total of 9,351,539 citizens participated in the election out of 12,623,289 registered voters, bringing preliminary voter turnout to 74.08%. The Adilet party received 6,528,948 votes, or 71.17%, according to the preliminary results. The Auyl People’s Democratic Patriotic Party received 574,621 votes, or 6.26%, followed by Respublica with 509,631 votes, or 5.56%, the Aq Zhol Democratic Party with 478,083 votes, or 5.21%, and the Nationwide Social Democratic Party with 469,058 votes, or 5.11%.

The People’s Party of Kazakhstan received 285,395 votes, or 3.11%, while the Baytaq Green Party received 97,751 votes, or 1.07%. The Against All option received 2.51% of the vote.

Under Kazakhstan’s election legislation, political parties must secure at least 5% of the vote to qualify for seats in the Kurultai. Based on the preliminary figures, five parties crossed the threshold.

Voting concludes abroad

According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, all 79 overseas polling stations established at Kazakhstan’s diplomatic missions and consular offices in 61 countries have completed their work as of 8 a.m. Astana time.

A total of 9,623 Kazakh citizens cast their ballots abroad, representing a voter turnout of 84.4% among registered overseas voters. The protocols of overseas precinct election commissions will be transmitted to the CEC for inclusion in the overall election results.

What comes next

The figures announced by the CEC are preliminary. The commission is expected to establish the official election results by Aug. 30. The formation of the new Kurultai will trigger a series of political and institutional changes under Kazakhstan’s new constitutional framework.

Following the formation of the Kurultai, the government is expected to resign. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said on election day that changes would be made to the composition of the cabinet, while stressing that personnel changes should be aimed at giving the Government new momentum rather than being made for the sake of dismissals.

Another expected institutional change is the appointment of a Vice President. Tokayev said the name of the person who will take the newly established position is expected to become known within a week or 10 days.

First election under new constitutional system

The Aug. 23 election was the first parliamentary election held under Kazakhstan’s new constitutional system. The 145-member Kurultai replaced the country’s former bicameral Parliament under the Constitution that took effect July 1.

All seats are allocated proportionally through party lists in a single nationwide constituency. Seven political parties fielded a total of 545 candidates. A total of 10,423 polling stations were established in Kazakhstan and abroad, with more than 12.6 million citizens registered to vote.

Overall, 777 foreign observers from 42 countries and 13 international organizations were accredited to monitor the election.

World.title: Experts Say Tokayev’s G20 Invitation Will Test Kazakhstan’s Balancing Act
World.content:
ASTANA — President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s participation in the G20 summit in Miami this December is set to put Kazakhstan’s carefully balanced foreign policy to a new test, as growing United States (US) interest in the country creates opportunities for deeper economic and strategic cooperation while intensifying competition among the major powers with which Astana has sought to maintain close ties.

Kazakhstan is not a G20 member and has participated in the summit only twice before, in St. Petersburg in 2013 and Hangzhou in 2016, each time at the invitation of the host country. This time, however, the invitation comes from the US, amid a rapidly expanding Kazakhstan-U.S. relationship and a sharp rise in Washington’s interest in the wider Trans-Caspian region.

The invitation can therefore be read in two ways. It may signal that Kazakhstan has become a more important strategic and economic partner for Washington. But it may also reflect the Trump administration’s broader effort to strengthen ties across a region increasingly important for energy, critical minerals, trade routes and technology. The difference matters because Kazakhstan’s traditional strength — its ability to work with competing powers without aligning exclusively with any of them — may also become harder to sustain as geopolitical competition deepens.

Iskander Akylbayev, CEO of Xander Group and chairman of CFive, sees the summit as a practical opportunity for Kazakhstan.

“My expectation is that the Miami G20 will be highly pragmatic and transaction-driven,” he said, pointing to economic growth, secure energy supply chains and technological innovation as central priorities of the U.S. G20 presidency.

He added that Tokayev’s participation “should therefore be seen as more than a diplomatic gesture,” noting that the invitation reflects a wider change in Washington’s view of Central Asia, which he believes is moving “from the geopolitical periphery to the global economic agenda.”

For Akylbayev, Kazakhstan’s economic weight helps explain the shift. He noted that Kazakhstan generates more than 60% of Central Asia’s GDP and accounts for approximately 75% of the region’s trade with the US, while bilateral goods trade reached $5 billion in 2025.

The broader relationship has indeed acquired a markedly commercial dimension over the past year. During President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s November 2025 visit to Washington, Kazakhstan and the United States signed 29 agreements worth $17 billion across industry, digitalization, education, healthcare, transport and other sectors. The Astana Times reported at the time that the visit represented a new phase in the strategic partnership, with experts describing a shift from symbolic diplomacy toward a more results-oriented model of cooperation.

Akylbayev said Miami should therefore be seen not as the culmination of this process but as an opportunity to move it into a more advanced stage.

“For Kazakhstan, however, the invitation itself is not the result. The real task is to convert political access into investment, technology and market access,” he said.

He pointed to critical minerals, AI, advanced manufacturing and the Middle Corridor, as well as Kazakhstan’s accession in June to the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative, which focuses on trusted supply chains linking semiconductors, critical minerals, data centers, energy infrastructure and high-tech manufacturing. Akylbayev’s broader argument is that Kazakhstan should move beyond its traditional role as a resource supplier.

“Our ambition should not be to export minerals and later import the technologies made from them,” he said, highlighting that Kazakhstan should process more resources domestically, expand computing infrastructure, develop engineering talent and produce higher-value components.

The logic is attractive, particularly as the US seeks to diversify strategic supply chains. Kazakhstan has become an important supplier of uranium and has substantial deposits of tungsten, copper, lithium and other critical minerals, while its geographic position gives it a central role in the Trans-Caspian transport route linking China and Europe.

Akylbayev believes this lets Kazakhstan present itself in Miami as a “connector state”—linking East and West, natural resources and technology, and major powers without becoming dependent on any one of them.

But that proposition rests on an important assumption: that the same balanced foreign policy that makes Kazakhstan attractive to multiple powers will continue to be accepted as competition among those powers intensifies. Darren Spink, managing director of Janus Forum and a non-resident fellow with the Danube Institute, believes that assumption may face its greatest test in technology.

“Kazakhstan has built its foreign and commercial policy around a balanced approach, but artificial intelligence (AI) may be emerging as the sector where Washington is least willing to accept that balance,” Spink said.

He pointed to the Middle Corridor as an example of an area where competing powers can still pursue overlapping interests. AI, however, is different, he said, because Washington increasingly sees technology, data infrastructure, semiconductors and supply chains through a strategic rather than purely commercial lens.

Kazakhstan joined the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative in June, while also deepening its participation in Chinese-led technology and governance structures. Spink cited Kazakhstan’s role in the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO), its participation in the Friends of Global Governance, and major technology agreements announced with China. For Washington, he noted, this could eventually create a problem. The concern is not necessarily that Kazakhstan is cooperating with China, but that some areas of cooperation may move from economic diversification into competing technological ecosystems, particularly if Beijing seeks to influence AI standards, governance and infrastructure in ways that conflict with U.S. strategic interests.

This brings the discussion back to Tokayev’s G20 invitation. Spink agrees that the invitation reflects Kazakhstan’s growing importance to Washington, but he sees another layer behind it.

“President Tokayev’s invitation to the G20 later this year should be viewed as recognition of both Kazakhstan’s growing importance to the US and of the Trump Administration’s broader geopolitical priorities,” he said.

Spink pointed to the nearly $17 billion in commercial agreements announced during Tokayev’s 2025 Washington visit and Kazakhstan’s participation in several U.S.-backed initiatives as evidence that Washington increasingly values the bilateral relationship.

“Perhaps the clearest demonstration of the value Washington now places on the relationship came when Vice President JD Vance personally urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to halt attacks affecting the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, protecting both Kazakhstan’s principal oil-export route and significant U.S. commercial interests,” Spink said.

But Spink says that Washington is also looking beyond the bilateral relationship toward the wider Trans-Caspian region.

“Just as Kazakhstan has pursued a balanced foreign policy among competing great powers, Washington is increasingly strengthening relationships across the Trans-Caspian rather than relying on any single regional partner. Reports that the leaders of Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan have also been invited to the G20 demonstrate this,” he said, pointing to the region’s growing importance to U.S. economic and strategic planning.

That distinction is important. If the invitation is read exclusively as recognition of Kazakhstan’s growing individual importance, its significance lies primarily in the bilateral relationship. If it is instead understood as part of a broader U.S. strategy toward the Trans-Caspian, Kazakhstan is one particularly important piece of a larger regional puzzle.

That broader regional interpretation does not undermine the case for Kazakhstan’s growing importance. Rather, it puts it in context. Washington has clear reasons to deepen ties with Kazakhstan, but also increasingly sees the Trans-Caspian as a strategic space for alternative trade routes, energy supplies, critical minerals and technology partnerships.

Kazakhstan’s growing importance to Washington is real, and the scale of the agreements signed in 2025 shows the relationship has moved beyond diplomatic symbolism. At the same time, the very factors that make Kazakhstan attractive to Washington – its location, resources and ability to maintain relations with multiple powers are also what may eventually put its balancing strategy under greater pressure.

This may be the central question Tokayev will carry to Miami. Kazakhstan has spent decades turning its position between major powers into an advantage. Its first two G20 appearances came at the invitation of Russia and China, while its third will come at the invitation of the United States. The sequence is almost a snapshot of Kazakhstan’s broader foreign policy: engage with competing centers of power without becoming dependent on any one.

But the international environment is changing. Trade can remain multipolar. Transport corridors can serve multiple markets. Investment can come from several directions. Technology is less forgiving. That is where Akylbayev’s optimism about Kazakhstan’s economic opportunity meets Spink’s warning about strategic limits.

Therefore, Miami should not be judged simply by whether Tokayev receives attention from world leaders or whether another package of commercial agreements is announced. The more consequential test will be whether Kazakhstan can convert its growing relevance into long-term industrial and technological capacity while retaining enough flexibility to work with competing powers.

For now, the answer is still open. Kazakhstan has something that major powers increasingly value: geography, resources, connectivity and political predictability. The challenge is to turn those advantages into bargaining power without letting them become the very reasons others ask Kazakhstan to choose.

World.title: IFC and Bank CenterCredit Partner to Boost Trade Finance in Kazakhstan
World.content:
IFC, a member of the World Bank Group, and Bank CenterCredit today announced a partnership to help Kazakh importers and exporters, particularly small and medium enterprises (SMEs), gain greater access to the cross-border financing they need to trade internationally.

Under the agreement, Bank CenterCredit joins IFC’s Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP) as both an issuing and confirming bank, becoming IFC’s only current partner bank in Kazakhstan under the program. The partnership also marks IFC’s re-engagement with BCC, a long-standing client. Backed by IFC’s guarantees, Bank CenterCredit will be able to issue and confirm trade finance instruments, such as letters of credit, giving companies from Kazakhstan more reliable access to the financing that underpins international trade.

The partnership is expected to be particularly impactful for SMEs, which often face the greatest barriers to securing trade finance. Smaller firms are frequently turned away because banks lack the risk capacity or correspondent relationships to support their cross-border transactions. By leveraging IFC’s global network and risk mitigation tools, Bank CenterCredit will be better positioned to support companies from Kazakhstan seeking to grow their international trade activities.

“Joining IFC’s Global Trade Finance Program is an important milestone for us,” said Ruslan Vladimirov, President of Bank CenterCredit. “This facility will allow us to expand our trade finance offering, better serve our corporate and SME clients, and support Kazakhstan’s growing role in regional and global trade.”

“We are pleased to welcome Bank CenterCredit as IFC’s sole active GTFP partner bank in Kazakhstan,” said Zafar Khashimov, IFC Country Manager for Kazakhstan. “By expanding access to internationally backed trade finance instruments, this partnership will help businesses from Kazakhstan, especially SMEs, pursue new markets, strengthen supply chains, and participate more actively in regional and global trade. In doing so, it will support business growth, job creation, and greater economic resilience in Kazakhstan.”

The GTFP is IFC’s flagship trade finance program, providing confirming banks with risk coverage on trade transactions across emerging markets. Since its launch in 2005, it has supported over $141 billion in trade through more than 100,000 transactions. The program supports key strategic priorities, including job creation and food security, with many of the beneficiary firms operating in IDA (International Development Association) countries.

About IFC

IFC — a member of the World Bank Group — is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. IFC works in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org.

World.title: Exit Polls Put Adilet Party Near 72% in Kazakhstan’s First Kurultai Election
World.content:
ASTANA – The Adilet party was projected to receive around 72% of the vote in Kazakhstan’s inaugural election to the Kurultai on Aug. 23, according to three exit polls released at midnight on Aug. 24. Exit polls, which were announced during a live election night broadcast, also showed four other parties narrowly clearing the threshold for representation in the country’s new unicameral Parliament.

The seven parties contesting the election were Adilet, Respublica, the Auyl People’s Democratic Patriotic Party, the People’s Party of Kazakhstan, the Aq Jol Democratic Party, the Baytaq Green Party and the Nationwide Social Democratic Party.

The three surveys put Adilet’s support between 70.7% and 72.3%, positioning the party for a commanding majority in the new 145-member unicameral Parliament. The figures are preliminary and do not constitute official election results.

According to the Institute of Public Policy, Adilet is expected to get 72.3% of the vote, followed by the Auyl party with 6.2%, Respublica with 5.2%, the Aq Jol Democratic Party with 5.1% and the Nationwide Social Democratic Party (NSDP) with 5%.

The People’s Party of Kazakhstan received 2.8%, while the Baytaq Green Party received 0.9%. Another 2.5% of respondents selected the “against all” option.

A separate exit poll by the Institute of Eurasian Integration put Adilet at 71.8%, Auyl at 6.4%, Respublica at 5.4%, NSDP at 5.2% and Aq Jol at 5.1%. The People’s Party received 3%, Baytaq 1% and “against all” 2.1%.

The Institute for Comprehensive Social Research-Astana, known as SOCIS-A, projected 70.7% for Adilet, 6.4% for Auyl, 5.5% for Respublica, 5.4% for Aq Jol and 5% for NSDP. It put the People’s Party at 3.2%, Baytaq at 1.2% and “against all” at 2.6%.

All three exit polls suggested that five of the seven competing parties had reached the 5% electoral threshold. The People’s Party and Baytaq remained below the threshold in all three polls.

The Central Election Commission (CEC) is expected to announce preliminary results after ballots have been counted. Exit polls survey voters after they leave polling stations and serve only as an early indication of the outcome.

Preliminary CEC figures showed voter turnout at 74.19% when polling stations across Kazakhstan closed at 8 p.m. Sunday. More than 12.6 million citizens were registered to vote at more than 10,000 polling stations nationwide and abroad. The final overseas voting process will conclude at the polling station at Kazakhstan’s Consulate General in San Francisco at 8 a.m. Astana time on Aug. 24.

Sunday’s vote was the first parliamentary election held under the new constitutional system. The election determines the composition of the 145-member Kurultai, which replaced Kazakhstan’s former bicameral Parliament under the new Constitution that took effect July 1. All seats are allocated proportionally through party lists in a single nationwide constituency. Parties must receive at least 5% of the vote to qualify for seats. A total of 545 candidates representing seven political parties contested the election.

Overall, 777 foreign observers from 42 countries and 13 international organizations have been accredited to monitor Kazakhstan’s election.

World.title: Kazakhstan’s First Kurultai Election Concludes With Preliminary Voter Turnout at 74.19%
World.content:
ASTANA – Voting in Kazakhstan’s first elections to the Kurultai concluded at all polling stations across the country at 8 p.m. on Aug. 23, with 9,352,151 voters, or 74.19% of those registered, having received ballots, according to preliminary voter turnout data from the Central Election Commission (CEC).

Polling stations have now closed nationwide, and precinct election commissions have begun counting the ballots. Under Kazakhstan’s election legislation, the vote-counting process may not exceed 12 hours from the start of counting. Territorial election commissions will transmit preliminary voting and counting results to the CEC through electronic channels.

The highest turnout was recorded in the Turkistan Region at 92.16%, followed by the Zhetisu Region at 91.19% and the Kyzylorda Region at 90.75%. Turnout in the Aktobe Region reached 88.30%, while the East Kazakhstan Region recorded 87.50% and the Zhambyl Region 85.18%.

Turnout stood at 82.69% in the Akmola Region, 81.41% in the Abai Region, 77.31% in the North Kazakhstan Region, 76.47% in the Kostanai Region and 76.28% in the Karagandy Region.

Among the cities of national significance, Shymkent recorded 75.42% turnout, Astana 51.67% and Almaty 43.23%.

Other regional figures included 73.38% in West Kazakhstan, 71.38% in the Mangystau Region, 71.20% in the Pavlodar Region, 71.17% in the Almaty Region, 70.74% in the Atyrau Region and 70.72% in the Ulytau Region.

Voting continues at overseas polling stations

Voting abroad is continuing in accordance with local time zones. As of 7 p.m. Astana time, all 79 polling stations established at Kazakhstan’s diplomatic missions and consular offices in 61 countries had opened. Voting had concluded in 11 countries, with 6,007 of the 11,402 registered voters abroad having cast their ballots.

Polling stations in Washington, New York, San Francisco, Ottawa and Brasilia continued operating as of the latest update. Seventy-four overseas polling stations were expected to complete voting by midnight Astana time.

The final overseas voting process will conclude at the polling station at Kazakhstan’s Consulate General in San Francisco at 8 a.m. Astana time on Aug. 24.

Protocols from overseas precinct election commissions will be transmitted to the CEC for inclusion in the overall election results.

Observers assess new parliamentary system

International observers said the election represents more than a change in the structure of Kazakhstan’s legislature. They noted that the new political system, established under the Constitution adopted in 2026, will ultimately be assessed by its ability to strengthen accountability, ensure institutional stability and create a predictable environment for citizens and investors.

The election marks the first vote for Kazakhstan’s new unicameral Kurultai, which will comprise 145 deputies elected through proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency.

The CEC will announce preliminary election results at a dedicated briefing, with the time to be communicated separately.

World.title: Observers See Unicameral Parliament as Boost for Stability and Investment
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s transition to a unicameral parliament and the implementation of its new constitutional framework were among the key issues raised by foreign observers during the parliamentary vote taking place on Aug. 23. The country’s prospects for attracting international investment were also a major focus of their discussions.

For international observers, the election to Kurultai, a new unicameral parliament, established under the Constitution adopted in 2026, represents more than a change in the structure of Kazakhstan’s legislature. They said the new political system will ultimately be judged by its ability to strengthen accountability, ensure institutional stability and create a predictable environment for citizens and investors.

Indonesian Ambassador to Kazakhstan Rachman Mohamad Fadjroel said the country’s Constitution provides the foundation for its ongoing political reforms.

“I believe the most important point in Kazakhstan is its Constitution, because this is the vision for the future of the country. Article 1 defines Kazakhstan as a democratic, secular, social and law-based state,” Fadjroel told The Astana Times.

He said the reforms underway are guided by these constitutional principles and demonstrate Kazakhstan’s commitment to democratic development.

“Today’s Kurultai election is an opportunity to demonstrate how democracy works in Kazakhstan in practice,” he said, adding that the country’s election has sent a positive message to the international community.

Unicameral parliament as a new political chapter

Domenico Palmieri, secretary general of the Italian Institute of Asia, described the election as a milestone for Kazakhstan, calling it the first major step in implementing the country’s new constitutional framework.

In an interview with The Astana Times, he said the transition to a unicameral parliament could streamline the legislative process and facilitate political reforms.

“From my point of view, a unicameral system is better. It is easier to work smartly and efficiently,” Palmieri said, adding that its effectiveness will ultimately depend on the performance of the new parliament and government.

“Only the future, starting from today, with the new parliament and government, can show whether this was the right decision taken by the Kazakh people,” he said.

He also noted that five Italian parliamentarians were observing the election in the Almaty Region.

“This shows the interest and attention of Italy toward the Kazakh nation,” Palmieri said.

He added that the new constitutional arrangements should now be translated into practical policies that contribute to social stability and economic development.

Clearer institutions could support investment

Nicolas Butylin, head of geopolitics at Berliner Zeitung, Germany’s daily newspaper, spoke about the implications of the new political system for foreign investors. He said a streamlined institutional structure could make it easier to understand where decisions are made and how checks and balances operate.

He described the Kurultai as another step in the country’s institutional development, stressing that the country should be assessed against its own progress rather than measured solely against Western democracies.

“I would not compare Kazakhstan to Western European democracies. I don’t think this is the benchmark. The more useful question, from my perspective, is to compare Kazakhstan with the state of Kazakhstan 10 years ago. To see if, with the new Kurultai, the system is more open, more accountable and more competitive,” Butylin said.

He noted that for Western businesses considering investment in Kazakhstan, institutional evolution and predictability would remain key factors.

Butylin also emphasized Kazakhstan’s growing importance to Germany and Europe through the Middle Corridor, particularly amid disruptions to established trade routes.

“From this perspective, especially in the economic part with natural resources, Kazakhstan will play a crucial role for the future of Germany as well,” he said.

Glenn Agung Hole, professor at the University of Southeast Norway and an expert in economics and international relations, noted that the parliament’s ability to provide legislative stability would be critical for business.

“From an economic perspective, the new Kurultai is important because they need to make stable laws. And business, finance and the stock exchange need to see that taxes and laws are followed through,” Hole said.

He emphasized that international investors need confidence that the rules governing their investments will remain predictable over time.

“We have to see stability over time. At least three to five years, international investors need to see that they can put their investment here and that it will be safe for the next three to five years and longer,” he said.

Kazakhstan’s strategic role in China-West trade

Ken Moriyasu, a senior researcher at the Washington D.C.-based Hudson Institute, placed Kazakhstan’s political reforms within a broader geopolitical and investment context.

“When it comes to investment, it’s important to understand the players involved here. China clearly is the biggest investor,” Moriyasu said.

He described Kazakhstan as a key partner for China as Beijing is seeking to reduce its reliance on maritime routes and expand overland connections.

“Political stability is very important,” he said, noting that Kazakhstan’s vast territory and strategic location make it an important component of these routes.

Moriyasu also emphasized that the development of overland corridors through Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Türkiye does not necessarily conflict with U.S. interests.

“It is very beneficial for the United States that China creates these land transport corridors, but the countries that these corridors pass through remain friends with America,” he said.

The Kurultai vote continues in Kazakhstan with 10,423 polling stations operating across the country. The Kurultai will have 145 seats elected for five-year term. A total of 777 foreign observers from 42 countries and 13 international organizations have been accredited to monitor Kazakhstan’s election.

World.title: Tokayev Says Vice President Appointment Expected Within 10 Days
World.content:
ASTANA – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said the new Vice President is expected to be appointed within the next week or 10 days, speaking to media representatives after casting his ballot in the country’s first elections to the Kurultai on Aug. 23.

Responding to questions about the reforms and the changes expected after the Kurultai and the Kazakhstan Khalyk Kenesi (People’s Council) begin their work, Tokayev described the newly established Vice President position as a significant and necessary institutional change.

“We deliberately established this new position in the Constitution. I would not be mistaken in saying that it is extremely necessary. In the current difficult times, such a position is particularly needed by our country,” Tokayev said.

He said the name of the person who will take the position is expected to become known within the next seven to 10 days, adding that it would be premature to disclose the candidate’s name during the voting process.

“I think this will be a well-known person whom you all know very well,” he said.

Tokayev also highlighted the planned launch of the Kazakhstan Khalyk Kenesi, a new state body that he said would build on the work previously carried out by the Assembly of the People of Kazakhstan. According to him, the new institution will serve as a multifunctional political mechanism as part of the country’s broader reforms.

Tokayev on 2029 presidential election

Asked whether he intends to use his constitutional right to seek another presidential term in 2029, Tokayev said the Constitutional Court’s recent decision confirming his eligibility is lawful, but that discussing his future candidacy would be premature.

“The Constitutional Court made this decision. It is lawful, and I have the legal right to be re-elected. But as for the upcoming elections or, as you put it, whether I will run or not, and in which year, it is premature to speculate on this,” he said.

Tokayev said the government has many tasks to complete before it can address such questions. He also said the government’s composition would change, while stressing that there are currently no grounds for concern about its work.

“Personnel changes are always inevitable because they give the government new strength,” Tokayev said, adding that such changes should be aimed at providing a serious impetus to the government’s work rather than dismissals for their own sake.

Voter turnout exceeds 65.37%

Meanwhile, voter turnout in Kazakhstan’s first elections to the Kurultai reached 65.37% by 4 p.m. on Aug. 23, with 8,240,336 voters having received ballots, according to the Central Election Commission (CEC).

The Kyzylorda Region recorded the highest turnout at 81.38%, followed by East Kazakhstan at 79.33%, Zhetisu Region at 77.03%, and Turkistan Region at 76.73%.

Turnout in the Aktobe Region stood at 75.63%, Akmola Region at 73.69%, Abai Region at 71.18%, Karagandy Region at 70.91% and Kostanai Region at 70.09%.

Among the cities of national significance, turnout reached 67.92% in Shymkent, 46.38% in Astana and 36.65% in Almaty.

Other regional figures were 67.23% in the Almaty Region, 67.06% in Pavlodar Region, 65.86% in Mangystau Region, 64.29% in Ulytau Region, 63.94% in North Kazakhstan, 63.37% in Atyrau Region, 61.81% in West Kazakhstan and 69.11% in the Zhambyl Region.

The CEC will provide the next update on voter turnout at 6 p.m.

World.title: $12m dispute and house sold at auction: where has former Georgian PM Nika Gilauri gone? – RFE/RL
World.content:
Nika Gilauri case

At the end of 2024, former prime minister Nika Gilauri became one of the most vocal critics of the ruling Georgian Dream party. Over the following months, he faced serious problems: authorities seized his foundation, while a court ordered him and his companies to pay $12 million in compensation to former business partners. Gilauri himself stopped appearing in public.

Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty published an investigation into the case. The circumstances described in the report raise suspicions that the legal proceedings against Gilauri may amount to political persecution. Georgian and German lawyers have called the court ruling unfounded.

The material draws on a Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty investigation.

Gilauri’s house put up for forced auction

On 16 July 2026, the National Bureau of Enforcement put Nika Gilauri’s house in Tsavkisi up for auction. A 3,368-square-metre plot of land and a 1,157-square-metre villa sold for almost four million lari (about $1.54 million).

The property had an estimated value of 4.876 million lari (about $1.87 million), but bidding started at 10% of that amount. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, businessman Vano Sturua bought the house. He is a former business partner of Nika Gilauri’s brother, Irakli.

Since 2018, this house has remained the only property in Georgia registered in Gilauri’s name. However, court rulings have also ordered the seizure of other assets and his shares in companies.

Gilauri himself has not commented on the situation. He only responded to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty in writing:

“The legal proceedings are still ongoing, and on my lawyers’ advice, I will not make any comments or give interviews at this stage.”

Gilauri’s return to politics

Nika Gilauri served as energy minister and finance minister under Mikheil Saakashvili. He then headed the government from 2009 to 2012. After leaving public service, he founded the consulting company Reformatics and stayed out of Georgia’s public political life for about 12 years.

The situation changed ahead of the 2024 parliamentary election. A few days before the vote, Gilauri and the Reformatics team presented a 100-page document outlining their vision for a “Third Republic of Georgia”. It addressed Georgia’s exit from Russia’s sphere of influence, judicial independence and European integration.

Media reports said Gilauri was financing the opposition Coalition for Change. Several coalition leaders later confirmed that they had worked with him and received campaign donations.

After security forces violently dispersed protests in November and December 2024, Gilauri called the Georgian Dream government illegitimate. He demanded new elections and the release of detained protesters.

Gilauri also called on business representatives to create a fund to support protesters. His Prosperity foundation raised 246,000 lari (about $94,450) in three months. The money was intended to support protesters and people who had lost their jobs because of their political views.

In March 2025, the prosecutor’s office froze the assets of the Prosperity foundation and four other foundations. Authorities opened an investigation into allegations of sabotage, assisting the activities of a hostile foreign organisation and actions against the constitutional order. The investigation remains ongoing, and the foundations remain suspended.

Gilauri has not appeared in public since then.

Dispute over the construction of three hydropower plants

The multimillion-lari legal dispute involving Gilauri began several years before he returned to politics.

In 2015, Aquahydro signed memorandums with the Georgian government and state-owned companies to build three small hydropower plants in the Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti region: Ipari, Khelra and Nakra.

Black Sea Group took responsibility for the construction work. Under the agreement, the contractor would receive payment for the completed work as well as a 20% stake in the company operating the hydropower plants.

Ipari and Khelra were completed and brought into operation. However, Black Sea Group halted construction of Nakra in 2020. A few months later, Aquahydro terminated its contract with the company and hired another contractor to complete the project.

In 2021, Black Sea Group went to court. The company said it had not received full payment for the work it had completed. It sought several million lari in compensation, as well as damages for lost profits.

Gilauri’s side filed a counterclaim seeking 14.5 million lari (about $5.57 million) from Black Sea Group. They argued that the suspension of construction at Nakra deprived the company of expected revenue for 2020-2022. Their expert assessment found that the contractor had received $600,000 more than the actual cost of the work, according to official documentation.

Black Sea Group rejected the assessment, arguing that it had not received full payment for the work it had completed.

Why was Gilauri held personally liable?

On 12 February 2025, Tbilisi City Court judge Liana Kajashvili ruled in favour of Black Sea Group. The court ordered the former prime minister and companies under his control to pay Black Sea Group more than $12 million in damages.

The Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court upheld the ruling. It became final in November 2025. The amount owed continues to increase each day until the court order is enforced.

The direct parties to the dispute were Aquahydro and Black Sea Group. Nika Gilauri had no direct contractual relationship with either company. He owned a stake in a firm whose subsidiary acted as the project’s direct client.

Despite this corporate structure, the court held Gilauri personally liable. It also imposed liability on Reformatics, even though the company had no involvement in the hydropower project.

The court concluded that Gilauri and companies linked to him had acted together against Black Sea Group under what it described as a “joint agreement”.

What do the lawyers say?

German and Georgian lawyers Heinz Böling and Giorgi Jughéli analysed the ruling. Their analysis appeared in a German legal journal in June 2026.

The authors argue that the court conflated the common goal of the economic project with the legal liability of the individual companies involved. They believe the ruling effectively erases the distinction between a company and its partners.

“Neither German nor Georgian law provides for such legal consequences. This is incorrect and, moreover, as already stated, simply fabricated,” the lawyers write.

In their assessment, the court imposed personal liability “through three corporate veils” on a person who was not a party to the disputed contract.

“As far as we know, there is no other court ruling allowing such liability — not only in Georgia, but anywhere in the world,” the authors note.

Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty also asked two other Georgian lawyers to independently review the ruling. Both said there were insufficient legal grounds for holding Gilauri and Reformatics liable.

One of the lawyers said that common ownership does not automatically make companies liable for each other’s obligations. To impose personal liability, the court would have had to prove that Gilauri used the corporate structure to defraud a creditor or pursue other unlawful purposes. The ruling contains no such evidence or reasoning.

There is no documented evidence of a political link between Gilauri’s public criticism, the acceleration of the court proceedings and the final ruling. However, the chronology raises questions. The trial court concluded a four-year dispute about two months after Gilauri made a series of high-profile political statements. The higher courts then reviewed the extensive case file within eight months.

The state has now sold Gilauri’s house at auction. The former prime minister remains silent, while authorities continue to pursue his assets and business interests to recover the money.

Nika Gilauri case

World.title: Aliyev’s Uzbekistan visit: ‘Eternal friendship’ and family business expansion
World.content:
Ilham Aliyev’s visit to Uzbekistan

The state visit to Tashkent was presented by official media as a “new, symbolic and practical stage” in relations between Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

Presidents Ilham Aliyev and Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a one-on-one meeting, chaired the third meeting of the Supreme Interstate Council, signed a “Treaty on Eternal Friendship”, awarded each other their countries’ highest state honours, and took part in ceremonies marking the opening and laying of foundations for Azerbaijani investment projects in Uzbekistan.

However, behind the official statements and rhetoric about “brotherhood” lie specific financial and business interests. Against the backdrop of the visit, attention has also focused on the parallel expansion of private companies directly or indirectly linked to Ilham Aliyev’s family, including PASHA Holding and Emin Agalarov’s Sea Breeze project.

What happened?

The main document signed during the visit was the “Treaty on Eternal Friendship”. Under the treaty, the two sides intend to build relations based on the principles of eternal friendship, mutual trust, strategic partnership and alliance, as well as support each other’s national development models. They undertake not to join blocs or alliances that could harm the other side’s sovereignty, security or territorial integrity, and not to allow their territory to be used by third parties for such purposes or for the activities of such groups.

Areas of cooperation outlined in the treaty include strengthening the UN’s central role, developing interparliamentary ties, trade and investment, including in energy, transport and logistics, digital development, agriculture, the green and digital economies, e-commerce, ICT and space technologies. The treaty also provides for the development of interconnected transport systems, the preservation of cultural and humanitarian ties, language learning, scientific and educational exchanges, interregional cooperation and tourism.

The heads of state exchanged their countries’ highest state honours, with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev receiving the Heydar Aliyev Order. Ceremonies were also held to open and lay the foundations for specific Azerbaijani projects in Uzbekistan, including hotel and residential complexes, tourism facilities, a building for the Nizami Ganjavi University, an “Azerbaijan” park and other facilities.

Joint projects have been launched in banking and finance, construction materials production, education, the oil and gas sector, tourism, housing construction, mining and agriculture. A corresponding “road map” was also adopted.

Azerbaijan’s state-owned bank enters Uzbek market

President Ilham Aliyev cited several specific examples of cooperation, including the entry of a leading Azerbaijani bank into the Uzbek market, the expansion of SOCAR’s retail network, oil and gas exploration nearing its final stage, and the prospect of drilling production wells next year.

The bank in question is the International Bank of Azerbaijan (ABB), the country’s largest state-owned bank, with around 88–92% of its shares held by the Finance Ministry and other state bodies. ABB is acquiring a 51% controlling stake in the privately owned Uzbek bank Davr Bank, investing more than $100m in the deal.

Despite its state-owned status, ABB was previously implicated in the Azerbaijani Laundromat scandal, involving a $2.9bn money-laundering scheme. The bank is now entering the Uzbek market with the backing of state resources and political will. The deal is being presented as a purely commercial decision, but comes against the backdrop of a strengthening political alliance between the two countries.

Economy Minister Mikayil Jabbarov announced the deal at an interregional forum a day before the visit, and it was formally concluded on the day of the visit. ABB will operate in Uzbekistan under the Davr Bank brand. The bank has assets of around $1bn, a customer base of 1.4 million and a network of 43 branches. Fitch Ratings expects the deal to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026.

Expansion of businesses linked to Aliyev family

Alongside the official banking deal, several private projects have also attracted attention during the visit and in the preceding period. Some are linked to companies and structures directly or indirectly associated with the president’s family.

Sea Breeze Uzbekistan: A $5bn resort project being developed by Agalarov Development, owned by Emin Agalarov, the former husband of President Aliyev’s daughter Leyla Aliyeva. The complex is planned for a 577-hectare site on the shores of the Charvak Reservoir. In 2025, the project was presented directly to Mirziyoyev and fast-tracked without a tender, while the environmental assessment had not yet been fully completed. A foundation-laying ceremony took place on the day of the visit. Although Agalarov is no longer related to the presidential family by marriage, he continues to enjoy high-level political support.

The complex is planned for a 577-hectare site on the shores of the Charvak Reservoir. In 2025, the project was presented directly to Mirziyoyev and fast-tracked without a tender, while the environmental assessment had not yet been fully completed. A foundation-laying ceremony took place on the day of the visit. Although Agalarov is no longer related to the presidential family by marriage, he continues to enjoy high-level political support. PASHA Holding projects: The holding company, which has been linked to the president’s daughters Leyla and Arzu Aliyeva, as well as to Mehriban Aliyeva’s father Arif Pashayev, is building a Ritz-Carlton-branded hotel and residential complex in Tashkent. The group includes private lenders Kapital Bank and PASHA Bank. Banks linked to the family control a significant share of Azerbaijan’s banking-sector assets — more than 40%, according to some estimates.

The group includes private lenders Kapital Bank and PASHA Bank. Banks linked to the family control a significant share of Azerbaijan’s banking-sector assets — more than 40%, according to some estimates. SOCAR: Azerbaijan’s state oil company is also entering Uzbekistan’s retail fuel market and plans to establish a network of filling stations there. At the same time, the company plans to cooperate with BP and Uzbekneftegaz on the Ustyurt field.
